nodes.principle_note: Resistance is a response to perceived pressure on one's freedom; asserting that no one is exerting any leaves the reactance without an object, and the listener attributes any resulting compliance to their own disposition rather than to influence. Self-attributed behaviour is then held more firmly than behaviour explained by an external cause. Falsifiable: if disavowal framing produced the same or more resistance than an overt-control framing, the reactance account is wrong; if compliance occurred but was still attributed to the operator, the self-perception half is wrong.

ex.f: The operator denies holding any power
ex.t: "all you can ever do is to show a patient how to go over the hurdle... You won't hypnotize him; he will hypnotize himself." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Basic acts reframed as happening on their own
ex.t: Before any relaxation content, the operator disclaims the asking itself: she could tell the listener to settle in, but there is no point, because that sorts itself out. She would ask them to listen, except that hearing is not something anyone does on purpose — nobody decides to hear a voice, it simply arrives. Nothing is being requested of the listener, so there is no effort to fail at, and nothing being done to them to brace against.
ex.s: The very opening, before any relaxation content; subject is still fully awake and possibly guarded.
ex.m: I could ask you to settle in, but there's no point — that sorts itself out. I could ask you to listen, except nobody decides to hear a voice. It just arrives. So there's nothing for you to do here, and nothing for you to get wrong.

ex.f: Redefining the state as ordinary self-generated focus
ex.t: Before anything that looks like an induction, the operator spends a minute insisting the process is unremarkable and unowned: people arrive at this state by themselves all the time, it is nothing but attention drawn to a narrow point, and no one is being acted upon. The listener's guardedness is spent by being conceded rather than opposed — there is no adversary in the room to brace against — and the suggestions begin against a vigilance that has been left without a target.
ex.s: First minute of the recording, before anything that looks like an induction; skeptical listener assumed.
ex.m: This isn't something I do to you. People fall into this by themselves all day — driving a familiar road, halfway through a book — it's nothing but attention narrowed to one point. Nobody is being acted on here, least of all by me.

nodes.name: operator-authority-assertion
nodes.mech: The operator states their own authority, rank, or trustworthiness as plain fact ('you trust me', 'you know I am in charge') instead of arguing for it. Later suggestions are then accepted because of who is saying them, not because of what they say. The claim is about the operator's standing right now, in a world the listener still shares. Variations: back the claim with stakes the listener has witnessed; tell a story of having survived tests or earned the role; tie the listener to the operator's name through flattery.
nodes.one_liner: State your authority or the listener's trust in you as settled fact, so later suggestions get accepted because of who says them.
nodes.why_short: People use a speaker's status as a shortcut instead of weighing the message; a confidently asserted rank or track record makes questioning the suggestion feel like questioning the person.
nodes.principle_note: Claimed rank functions as a shortcut for evaluation: when a speaker is treated as authoritative, listeners process the message peripherally and comply on the strength of the source rather than the argument. Credentialing details make the claim harder to challenge without seeming to challenge the person. Falsifiable: if identical suggestions produced identical response with and without the standing claim, the deference lever does not exist.

ex.f: Public stakes before a respected audience
ex.t: "he would be a fool to attempt anything that was likely to fail before an audience of doctors… I must be anesthetized." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Trust asserted as existing fact
ex.t: No argument is offered and no history is cited; the couplets simply report the listener's condition back to them: your trust in me is already settled, you feel safe because I never mislead you, and handing over your thinking is exactly what you came for. Stated as observation rather than request, it leaves no opening to ask where the trust came from — the question would contradict a fact the listener has just been told about themselves.
ex.s: Trance established; operator delivers short couplets reporting the subject's condition back to them.
ex.m: Your trust in me is already settled. You feel safe because I have never once misled you. And handing your thinking over to me is exactly what you came here for.

ex.f: Borrowed gravity transferred onto the voice
ex.t: The colour is established first as something weighty — deep, commanding, the thing that carries you out of waking. Then every one of those attributes is transferred, one by one, onto the sound of the voice: the same weight, the same command, and it is this that is taking you down. The listener can feel something happening; the operator supplies the cause, and the cause is herself.
ex.s: A colour has already been established in the imagery as heavy and commanding; operator now transfers it.
ex.m: That deep, weighted colour — the one that pulls you out of waking — listen to it. It's in my voice. Same weight, same command, same pull, and it is my voice taking you down, not the colour.

ex.f: Standing credentialed by narrated survivorship
ex.t: The opening is not a dominant introducing herself. It is a biography of prior subjugation, delivered plainly: the speaker was on the receiving end for a long time, was remade into something usable, and stayed there watching how the work was done until she could do it herself. Authority is credentialed by having been through it rather than by asserted power, which forecloses the obvious challenge — she has already conceded the most damaging facts about herself — and recasts the listener's own submission as an early stage of the same curriculum.
ex.s: Opening of the session; the operator introduces herself by history rather than by rank.
ex.m: I was on the receiving end of this for years. I was taken apart and made into something useful, and I stayed there watching how it was done until I could do it myself. Everything I am about to do to you was done to me first — that's how I know it works.

nodes.name: operator-credit-engineering
nodes.mech: The operator arranges or narrates events so that results, even real ones the listener would have had anyway, are credited to the operator's power. Authority is built out of that credit rather than claimed outright. Variations: name yourself in advance as the cause of something a method will genuinely produce later (a lucid dream, say), so its arrival reads as proof of your power; hold back a release you could give at once until the listener has tried and failed to manage it alone, so your small final cue lands as a dramatic act.
nodes.one_liner: Arrange or narrate events so that results the listener would get anyway are credited to your power.
nodes.why_short: People credit outcomes to whatever cause is most visible and was named beforehand; pre-announcing yourself as the cause steers how a later success gets explained.
nodes.principle_note: Causal attribution favours whatever is salient and temporally adjacent to an outcome, so arranging for the operator to be the visible antecedent of an effect the listener would have produced anyway captures the credit. Pre-installing the attribution matters because a cause supplied before the event constrains how the event is later explained. Falsifiable: if listeners attributed the outcome to their own effort despite the pre-installed chain, or if withholding-then-releasing produced no attribution shift, the account fails.

ex.f: Withholding a held release until effort is spent
ex.t: "This comment I deliberately bypassed" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Attribution chain pre-installed for a future success
ex.t: The chain is laid out in advance, in future tense: the further I take you, the more vivid it gets; the more vivid it gets, the better the training works; and when you wake one morning having actually done it, that will be proof of what I can do to you — and being in awe of me makes you easier to take further still. The technique may genuinely work. The credit has already been assigned to the operator before the result arrives.
ex.s: Early in a training series, before the first practice attempt; operator lays out the chain in future tense.
ex.m: The further I take you, the more vivid this gets. The more vivid it gets, the faster the training works. And the morning you wake up having actually done it, you'll know that was me — and being in awe of me is exactly what lets me take you further next time.

nodes.name: operator-owned-depth-dial
nodes.mech: The operator turns a private feeling, such as how deep the trance is or how aroused the listener is, into an imaginary control the operator works: a dial, a volume knob, an on/off button in the brain, floors of a building. The listener stops judging the state by feel and reads it off the operator's settings instead; going lighter feels like something taken away, and there is nothing to resist because the change is done to them. Variations: one control reused all session; a dial with marked levels, each removing an ability; a control that runs by itself (wipers clearing away thoughts); dials for intelligence or sensitivity rather than depth.
nodes.one_liner: Give depth or arousal an imaginary dial, button, or count that you visibly turn, so the listener reads their state off your settings.
nodes.why_short: A vague inner feeling is hard to judge; once it is turned into a number someone else sets, the listener defers to that number instead of their own sense of it.
nodes.principle_note: A private, ungraded sensation is hard to dispute or to defend; converting it into a discrete quantity someone else visibly sets replaces the listener's own judgment with reported readings, and having no felt criterion of their own they defer to the operator's. Perceived control over an outcome also predicts effort to influence it, so relinquishing the control surface reduces attempts to counteract the change. Falsifiable: if listeners continued to report depth or arousal from their own felt-sense and disregarded the instrument's stated setting, the ownership transfer is not occurring.

ex.f: A binary on/off button on the listener's hand
ex.t: A control is conjured onto a part of the body the listener has already been made to imagine — pressed once, thinking stops; pressed again, it resumes. The toggles then arrive faster than any count could be spoken, and the limb operating the control is reassigned midway: it answers to the operator now, not to the listener. No interpretive work is left — the listener never has to judge whether they are far enough down, because a press is unambiguous and it is not theirs to make.
ex.s: Subject has already imagined and felt their own hand in detail; operator conjures a control onto it.
ex.m: On the back of your left hand there's a button. I press it — thinking stops. I press it again — thinking comes back. Off. On. Off. On, off, on. And that hand isn't taking instructions from you anymore; it takes them from me.

ex.f: Depth as a knob turned up and down
ex.t: Depth is narrated purely as a setting being adjusted: the operator announces a move in one direction and the second voice on the track loses its words to bare syllables, announces a move back and the words return. No instruction is issued to the listener at any point — nothing is asked of them, so resistance has nothing to push against — and the lighter state is characterised not as a return to themselves but as being permitted, temporarily, to perform being someone.
ex.s: Two-voice track, subject listening as the operator adjusts a second subject's state; no instruction issued to the listener at all.
ex.m: I'm turning her down. Listen to that — she can't hold the word anymore, just the vowel. And back up, halfway. There. Now she can talk. Say hello for me. Isn't it nice of me to let her be a person for a minute.

ex.f: Movement permitted only where the operator names it
ex.t: The catalepsy is broken on the operator's terms rather than the listener's: one narrowly specified adjustment of the crossed limbs is granted, and the hold re-establishes itself before the movement has finished registering. The grant recurs at intervals through the script and each instance is sold as a further deepening, so the single permitted motion functions as a paced obedience drill — the only movement available is the one that was named, and using it tightens the state rather than loosening it.
ex.s: Catalepsy is established in the crossed arms; subject has been immobile for some minutes.
ex.m: I'll give you one thing: you may slide your right thumb half an inch, and only that. Take it now. ... Good — and it's locked again, tighter than before, and you're deeper for having spent it.

ex.f: A numbered dial the operator turns both ways
ex.t: A graduated scale is installed inside the listener's mind, presented not as a metaphor for sinking but as a calibrated instrument with the operator's hand on it. The operator names a setting, asserts the state that belongs to it, and moves between settings on demand — including several deliberate moves in the lighter direction, narrated with evident enjoyment at holding the listener further up than they would like. Depth stops being something the listener feels and becomes a reading someone else takes, so it is no longer theirs to report. The upward moves are the load-bearing half: each one manufactures the wanting that makes the next descent feel granted rather than merely tolerated.
ex.s: Trance established; operator installs a graduated instrument and immediately begins moving it, including upward.
ex.m: There's a dial in your mind, nought to ten, and my hand is on it. It's at seven — that's where your words start coming slowly. Now I'm turning it back to three. Look how much you hate that. Say something clever for me at three. ... No? Back to seven, then, since you asked so nicely.

nodes.name: operator-receivable-extraction
nodes.mech: Turn compliance into something the listener sends you: they type and send a confession, email or contact details that identify them to a real address, often while still in trance, with orgasm allowed only once they click send. The key feature is that something real leaves the fantasy: you collect evidence of compliance, identifying information, or a way to reach them, and later the listener reads the message as proof of what they themselves wanted. Unlike a simple behavior cue, the result is something you receive, and the whole sequence fails if the receiving address is not live.
nodes.one_liner: Have the listener send you a real message or confession, often while still tranced and with release gated on hitting send.
nodes.why_short: An act that leaves your hands and is received by someone else is hard to take back or reinterpret; people then read their own sent message as evidence of what they want.
nodes.principle_note: An act that leaves the listener's own hands and is received by someone else is far harder to reinterpret afterwards than a private thought; under self-perception theory the sender reads their own irrevocable, self-identifying act as evidence of what they actually want, and each subsequent request is then measured against that self-attribution rather than against their pre-session baseline. Timing the send to peak arousal exploits the hot-cold state gap: decisions made in a high-drive state systematically underweight the later costs the cold state will have to pay. This predicts that a send known in advance to be undeliverable, or an equivalent act performed privately, should produce measurably less downstream compliance than a genuinely received one.

ex.f: Fixed-wording message sent on waking
ex.t: At the bottom of the count the instruction is set three times, in fixed wording, with no choice offered: when this ends you write to me, and you write exactly this line. Then the count up is unusually fast and carries the errand with it — awake now, going straight to send it. The wording contains the session's key word, so every later re-reading of the sent message fires the trigger again.
ex.s: Bottom of the descent, subject at maximum depth; the wording is fixed and repeated three times.
ex.m: When this ends you write to me, and you write exactly this: "Thank you for the velvet." Say it back. Again. When this ends you write to me, and you write exactly this: "Thank you for the velvet" — and then five, four, three, two, one, eyes open, phone in your hand, go.

ex.f: Trance held open until the message is sent
ex.t: The state is not closed and then followed by homework. Before the recording ends the operator specifies the errand — go and write to me, tell me the whole of how this felt — and then attaches the condition that does the work: the working state remains in force, and remains in force, until the message has actually gone. Emergence is withheld as the fee. The listener carries an unfinished trance out of the session and can only discharge it by delivering the artifact.
ex.s: Final minutes; the state has been built and the operator does not close it.
ex.m: Before you go anywhere: you're going to write to me and tell me the whole of how this felt. And this stays exactly as it is — heavy, slow, mine — until the message has actually gone. Not until you've decided to send it. Until it has gone.

ex.f: Contact urge installed with its source hidden
ex.t: The instruction is deposited rather than issued: the listener will report back on how much they enjoyed this, the reason for reporting is stored somewhere they cannot reach, and whatever channel they already use is fine. Because the source of the impulse has been put out of view, what surfaces later is felt as a spontaneous wish to make contact rather than a command being carried out — and the operator ends up with a live channel and a listener who believes they opened it themselves.
ex.s: Deep trance; the instruction is planted with its origin explicitly stored out of reach.
ex.m: Sometime in the next few days you'll want to tell me how much you enjoyed this — whichever way you already talk to me is fine. The reason you want to is going in a drawer you can't open. All you'll have is the wanting, and it will feel like it came from you.

ex.f: Typed confession emailed while still under
ex.t: There is no wake-up at the end. Instead there is an interrogation: questions are put, and the listener types the answers — still under, released from stillness only far enough to reach a keyboard. The answers go into an email to a named address, and the pleasure is wired to the click of SEND. What leaves the room is a signed, self-identifying document in the listener's own words, delivered to someone who now has their address; without a live recipient the whole closing sequence has nowhere to land.
ex.s: End of the session, subject still under; hands are released from catalepsy far enough to reach a keyboard, eyes barely open.
ex.m: Stay down and open your eyes just enough to see the keys. First question: what were you thinking about at number four? Type the answer — don't tidy it. Put your name at the bottom, put it in the box addressed to me, and you are not allowed to finish until your finger comes off send.

nodes.name: orgasm-gated-relief-monopoly
nodes.mech: Raise arousal (or use a drive already there), then allow its only permitted release after an act outside the session that benefits you: a tribute (money, a gift), getting in touch or begging, or a confession. The only way to relief then runs through you. Orgasm denial enforces it and the arousal built in the session is the reward. A forced choice often removes the option of doing nothing, and the gate is often handed to a stand-in figure, sidestepping the listener's own ability to refuse, or framed as gratitude so the listener polices themselves. What defines it is controlling which way out is available (pay or contact, then release).
nodes.one_liner: Build arousal, then allow release only after the listener does something that benefits you (pays, messages, confesses).
nodes.why_short: Plain reward learning: making relief depend on one act trains that act, and holding arousal unsatisfied makes the relief worth more and narrows attention onto getting it.
nodes.principle_note: This is a straightforward operant contingency run on a biological drive: the operator-benefiting act is installed as the only response on which the reinforcer is contingent, and the deprivation state (arousal held without release) functions as a motivating operation that inflates the reinforcer's value and narrows attention onto routes toward it. Deleting the do-nothing option removes the competing response rather than persuading against it. It predicts extinction: make relief reliably available by an alternative route and the tribute or contact behaviour should decay, which distinguishes this from a genuine preference for the act itself.

ex.f: Binary task with the do-nothing option deleted
ex.t: The post-session instruction is stated as a pair with no third term: on ending, the listener either sends the operator a purchase or writes asking to be given a task, and no choice about this is offered. Release is withheld until one of the two is complete. The listener surfaces still aroused, facing two doors — and the door they would actually have taken once the state faded, the one where nothing happens at all, is never acknowledged to exist.
ex.s: End of session, subject aroused and held short of release; the instruction is given as a closed pair.
ex.m: When this ends you do one of two things: you send me something off my list, or you write to me and ask for a task. Those are the two. And you don't come until one of them is done.

ex.f: The gate delegated to a proxy figure
ex.t: The permission is routed through an invented third figure installed earlier in the session: from now on, when you want release, you ask her — and she will only allow it once you have done something for me. The internal voice that would have said "I'm not sending money" is now arguing with a character the operator wrote, and one who is described as entirely loyal to the operator.
ex.s: A servant figure was installed earlier in the session and described as wholly loyal to the operator.
ex.m: From now on you don't ask me for release — you ask her. She's the one holding it. And she doesn't hand it over until you've done something for me first, so take it up with her, not with me. She won't budge; she never does.

ex.f: The rule installed as a favour
ex.t: The standing requirement — something written and something bought, every time, before release — is never delivered as a requirement. Asking permission is characterised as the wrong posture; gratitude for having been trusted with the ritual is the right one. The tribute is said to demonstrate the listener's worth to themselves rather than to the operator, and the rule as a whole is presented as what protects them from letting the whole business go slack and unfelt. Framed as safekeeping and conferred responsibility, it needs no enforcement at all: complying produces relief, and lapsing produces guilt the listener applies to themselves.
ex.s: Late session, warm register; the standing rule is delivered as a privilege rather than a demand.
ex.m: Something written and something bought, every time, before you're allowed to finish. And don't ask me for permission — asking is the wrong posture. Be grateful I trust you with the ritual at all. It's what keeps you from going slack and stops all this from fading into nothing.

ex.f: No climax without a tribute sent first
ex.t: The rule is stated plainly and then repeated until it is furniture: you don't finish without sending something first. And the obvious escape is closed before it is reached — it doesn't matter how much. It could be a single dollar. The size never mattered; the step does. What that de-staking does is convert a rule the listener could refuse on grounds of cost into one they cannot, and it recruits their own existing habit as the schedule on which the operator gets paid.
ex.s: Arousal built high in-session; the rule is stated plainly and repeated until it stops sounding like a request.
ex.m: You don't finish without sending me something first. Every time. And before you start doing the sums — it doesn't matter how much. One dollar. A single dollar clears it. The amount was never the point; the sending is.

nodes.name: ownership-language
nodes.mech: The operator tells the listener, warmly, that their body, mind and desires belong to the operator, not as a request but as a fact about who they now are. Warm delivery makes being owned feel like safety rather than threat. Variations: fill speech with possessive words ('my pet', 'my mind'); claim body parts one by one; claim one involuntary function such as breath or heartbeat; frame the listener's purpose as serving the owner; route self-care through the owner; make the owner the judge of how well the listener is doing; a one-way merger where the listener dissolves into the owner; a ladder that claims a little more each time.
nodes.one_liner: Tell the listener, warmly and repeatedly, that their body, mind, and desires belong to you, as a fact about who they are.
nodes.why_short: Repetition supplies a ready-made self-label that gets rehearsed; delivering it warmly pairs 'owned' with safety and affection, so the label feels good rather than threatening.
nodes.principle_note: Repeated assertion of an identity claim works less by argument than by supplying a ready-made self-label that the listener rehearses, and warm delivery pairs the possession language with affiliative and safety cues so the claim acquires positive valence by evaluative conditioning rather than being evaluated on its merits. The framing also converts a demand into a description, which is harder to decline because declining requires contradicting a stated fact about oneself. Falsifiable in the delivery axis: if warm and threatening deliveries of the identical claim produced equal adoption, the evaluative-conditioning account would be wrong.

ex.f: Ownership deeded part by part during relaxation
ex.t: It presents as an ordinary progressive relaxation, worked through the body region by region, except that each region carries one additional sentence: soften this part — and this part is now mine. Release the next — and hand it over completely. The hands are turned to sit open, offered. A long series of small concessions, none individually large enough to be worth interrupting for, arrive folded into a physiological move the listener is already performing. Remove the deeding sentences and what is left is a plain body scan; the fusion is the entire mechanism.
ex.s: During progressive relaxation, working region by region; one extra sentence rides each release.
ex.m: Soften the muscles around your eyes — and those are mine now. Let the jaw hang open — hand it over completely. Turn your palms up, open, offered. Good. Every part you let go of, I keep.

ex.f: Self-care rerouted through the owner's interest
ex.t: Ordinary maintenance — eating, resting, keeping in condition — is redescribed as custodial work performed on something under the operator's title. The listener is invited to see neglect not as a private matter but as damage to another party's asset, and the duty is explicitly made continuous rather than occasional. Self-interest is re-pointed at the owner's interest, so daily life becomes uninterrupted service and looking after oneself stops being something done for oneself at all.
ex.s: Post-trance framing or late install; ordinary daily maintenance is re-described as custodial duty.
ex.m: You eat properly because you are looking after something that belongs to me. You sleep enough because you are looking after something that belongs to me. Letting yourself go isn't a private matter anymore — it's damage to my property, and the duty doesn't clock off.

ex.f: Self-evaluation handed over item by item
ex.t: A run of flat declaratives in the listener's own voice hands over every faculty of self-judgement, one item at a time: my clothes are chosen for me, my name is given to me, whether I am pretty is not mine to say, whether I am good enough is somebody else's ruling. Nothing about the speaker is left self-determined, so there is no longer any way to feel worth anything without the operator present to say so.
ex.s: First-person recitation block; flat declaratives the subject speaks or subvocalizes, one faculty per line.
ex.m: My clothes are chosen for me. My name is given to me. Whether I am pretty is not mine to say. Whether I am good enough is somebody else's ruling, and I will not know until I am told.

ex.f: Possessive nouns delivered as security
ex.t: For several minutes the listener is addressed only as something held: my lovely thing, my prize, my kept and cared-for possession — the word for a person never once appearing. The verbs around it are all caretaking, held and carried and looked after and kept safe, and the passage closes by asking whether that isn't perfect security. The claim is ownership; the register is comfort, so the objectification arrives as relief rather than as threat.
ex.s: Mid-trance, warm and slow; the operator addresses the subject only in possessives for a sustained stretch.
ex.m: There you are — my lovely thing, my prize, my kept and cared-for possession. Held, carried, looked after, put away safe when I'm done with you. Isn't that perfect security?

nodes.name: parts-work-positive-intent-elicitation
nodes.mech: When part of the listener objects to a change, the operator treats that part as well-meaning and asks what it is trying to do for them, instead of arguing with the objection. Repeating 'and what does that do for you?' walks down to a positive goal the change can be built to meet, so resistance becomes a list of needs rather than a wall. This gathers material for later work rather than suggesting anything. Variations: ask a part what it is in charge of, not what it objects to; split a vague complaint into two blameless parts that clash; have the listener find a setting where they value the behaviour.
nodes.one_liner: When a part of the listener objects, ask what it is trying to do for them rather than arguing with its objection.
nodes.why_short: Arguing with an objection makes people defend it; asking what it protects turns a standoff into a problem to solve, which counselling research finds lowers defensiveness.
nodes.principle_note: Arguing against a stated objection reliably produces counter-argument and hardening; asking what the objection is trying to accomplish converts a positional standoff into an interests problem, which is the move negotiation research and motivational interviewing both find lowers defensive responding. Naming the resisting element as benevolent removes the threat to self-concept that makes people defend an objection past its usefulness. The falsifiable claim is about questioning style, not about parts being real entities: adversarial questioning of the same content should yield a higher rate of restated objection than intent-eliciting questioning.

ex.f: Ask the part its function, not its objection
ex.t: “You don't ask ‘What is your objection?’; you ask ‘What's your function?’” — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: The no-bad-parts axiom stipulated by fiat
ex.t: "No, No, NO! There are no bad parts. We have all good parts. The only question is, 'What kind of good are they doing?'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Laddering to a buildable positive aim
ex.t: “What is it trying to do for you by keeping you from feeling helpless? So what if you feel helpless?” — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: One complaint split into two colliding parts
ex.t: "it's not that one part is 'making you do it'; it's that two parts are each doing something useful, but the ways that they are doing it conflict" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: payload-welded-countdown
nodes.mech: A countdown (or a doubling one) gets two jobs: each number deepens trance and also adds a different suggestion, such as a post-hypnotic instruction, a commitment to the relationship, a step of obedience, a mission, or an ability being taken away. Since the listener has learned, or is learning in the same count, that "a number means I go deeper", each suggestion rides in on the deepening and cannot be refused without refusing the deepening too. The count works as deepener, suggestion carrier and progress bar at once, so depth and acceptance fuse and cannot later be pulled apart. Variations: numbers that later serve as handles to recall their content; a second count that reuses the first count's trained compliance to slip in relationship content; a count where each number turns a physical dial (thicker, or more erased) rather than depth; and a repeat countdown that deepens from a state already installed to re-embed earlier instructions.
nodes.one_liner: Count down to deepen, and attach a different suggestion to each number so accepting the suggestion feels like part of going deeper.
nodes.why_short: Once a count has trained 'number, then deeper', each step is an easy yes; a request slipped into a run of easy compliances is accepted more often than one asked cold.
nodes.principle_note: A count that has already been trained is a chain of easy, likely responses, and placing a less likely request inside a run of easy compliances measurably raises acceptance of it. This is behavioural momentum, one of the better-replicated compliance findings. Because the depth the listener wants arrives as a reward on each number, turning down the suggestion means breaking a chain they are being rewarded to continue, so refusing has a felt cost that a stand-alone request would not. Applying this to hypnotic counts is plausible but untested. It predicts that acceptance of the suggestions should drop sharply where the count has not been trained as a cue for depth, or where the listener does not want depth.

ex.f: Each rung removes a specific named faculty
ex.t: The descent is not generic: each rung is assigned the removal of one named capacity, and the assignments are ordered. Tension goes, then the sense of elapsed time, then shame, then volition — announced flatly, as a property of the kind of thing the listener is now said to be — then memory, then language. The sequence is load-bearing: disinhibition is delivered before volition is taken, so by the point at which the listener might want to object, the specific faculties an objection would need have already been itemised and set down on the way past.
ex.s: Descending count in progress; each rung is pre-assigned one named capacity to remove.
ex.m: Six, and the tension goes. Five, and you stop being able to tell how long you've been here. Four, and shame goes — puppets don't have any. Three, and choosing goes with it. Two, and you won't remember this. One, and you won't have the words.

ex.f: The count ticks a quantity, not a depth
ex.t: The count is bound to a concrete quantity rather than to relaxation: at each number the enveloping material is declared to double — heavier, tighter, closer in. The number functions as the click of a ratchet on that quantity. Because the binding is established before the count begins, the listener leans into each next number expecting more of the substance, and the anticipation performs the deepening without a single new suggestion being introduced.
ex.s: An enveloping substance or material has already been established around the body; the count ticks its quantity.
ex.m: Ten — and the latex doubles. Thicker, tighter, closer in. Nine — it doubles again, and you can feel the weight of it settle on your chest. Eight — double, and it's pressing your arms flat to your sides.

ex.f: A second descent reusing the first's compliance
ex.t: The descent completes and the listener arrives — and instead of beginning the work, the operator opens a fresh scene and immediately starts a second short count, this one measured in paces across a room. Each pace is now said to increment devotion rather than depth. The listener has just finished a whole descent learning that a counted step means going further, and hands that compliance to the new content without pausing to notice the substitution.
ex.s: A full descent just finished and the subject has arrived; instead of working, the operator opens a new scene and counts again.
ex.m: Good. Now stand up in there, and walk toward the chair — five paces. Five: you like me. Four: you like me more than you did this morning. Three. Two. One — and at the chair, you belong to me, and it was only five steps.

ex.f: Each number doubles depth and tags a suggestion
ex.t: Each instruction in the sequence is issued under a number, and the number is declared to double the listener's depth on the spot. The depth increment always fires first, so every rule lands on someone who was taken further down a moment earlier; the same numbers then serve as the labels the listener must carry out of the session and act on for a fixed run of days. Declining any single rule would mean declining the drop that arrived attached to it — the drop the whole session has been training them to want.
ex.s: Deep trance, subject already trained this session that a number means a drop; each rule is issued under a number.
ex.m: Seven — and that doubles your depth right now. At seven: you set your alarm ten minutes early and you use those minutes thinking about me. Six — twice as deep again. At six: you don't touch yourself for the next four days without saying my name first.

nodes.name: persistent-metaphor-spine
nodes.mech: One image (a thread, a balloon, a machine) is introduced early and reused at every stage: induction, deepening, suggestions, triggers and wake-up. The frame never changes, so each heavier step arrives as more of an image already accepted, and the comfort built by the gentle early uses carries into the later ones. Variations: the image takes over control (the thread pulls you); something drains away as the image fills; the image spreads with each breath; a protective image turns into one that holds the listener in; the mind as a computer running commands; a figure of speech gradually treated as literal.
nodes.one_liner: Pick one image (a thread, a balloon, a machine) and keep reusing it from induction to wake-up for every new suggestion.
nodes.why_short: People judge a frame once and then reason inside it; later, heavier suggestions read as extensions of an image already accepted, and familiar imagery feels truer.
nodes.principle_note: Append to each note where the grade is not shown elsewhere, for example for this note: 'This explanation is plausible but has not been directly tested.'

ex.f: Identity loss as a conserved-volume exchange
ex.t: Two substances, one fixed container: as the coating flows in, the thoughts must flow out — there is only so much room. The operator never argues that the listener should give up anything. He describes a plumbing inevitability already underway, so identity loss arrives as a physical process being observed rather than a demand being made.
ex.s: A substance has been established as flowing into the body; container framing already accepted.
ex.m: There's only so much room in you. As the shine flows in, something has to go out — that's just volume. So watch your thoughts leaving through your fingertips as the shine fills you to the wrist. In, and out. There isn't a decision to make here; there's only so much room.

ex.f: A dead metaphor taken literally as scaffold
ex.t: The opening takes a worn-out figure of speech for the process and refuses to treat it as figurative — the term is announced, then immediately cashed out as literal stage directions with a piece of ordinary machinery doing the work. Every image that follows is generated by running the same literalism forward: the mechanism engages, the contents come loose, the parts circulate. The listener never has to invent a scene, only track a household object, which frees their attention for the sensations being suggested and presents what is coming as a routine domestic procedure rather than an intervention.
ex.s: Opening lines; the operator takes a worn figure of speech for the process and refuses to treat it as figurative.
ex.m: Brainwashing. Let's be literal about it. There is a washing machine in front of you, the door is open, and your thoughts go in the drum. Close it, set it turning — and feel them come loose and start going round.

ex.f: The spine ridden as a breath-gated route
ex.t: A single pinprick in the arm is tracked along a fixed anatomical route — shoulder, chest, heart, past the barrier into the brain — and every inhale is narrated as pumping it one stage further. Each station carries its own effect: heavy, then warm, then swimming, then aroused. The listener never has to accept five separate suggestions; they accept one journey, the effects come bundled with it, and because breathing is involuntary the advance is framed as something that cannot be stopped.
ex.s: A pinprick sensation has been established in the arm; every inhale is narrated as advancing it one stage.
ex.m: Breathe in — and it moves from your elbow to your shoulder, heavy. Breathe in — into your chest now, warm. Breathe in — past your throat, and everything swims. Breathe in — through into the brain, and there it is. You don't have to do any of this; you only have to keep breathing, and you will.

ex.f: One image re-pointed from limb to self
ex.t: The thread is introduced as a literal tie around the hands, and the listener spends several minutes actually feeling it there. Then the same thread — not a new image, the same one — is described winding around the mind, and then around the self, until the listener is not held by threads but is the puppet on them. Nothing new is ever proposed for the listener to weigh, so the felt realness earned at the hand is spent on the control claim without a second consent step.
ex.s: A thread has been established as a literal tie on the hands and felt for several minutes.
ex.m: Feel it there, snug across both wrists. Now feel the same thread going up — around your thoughts, one loop, then another, drawing them in. Same thread. And now around you, all of you, so it isn't that you're held by threads. It's that you're the puppet on the end of them.

nodes.name: inner-voice-authorship-bypass
nodes.mech: The operator makes their words feel like the listener's own thoughts, so there is no outside voice left to push against. Variations: slide quietly from 'you' to 'I' in the middle of a passage; restate an operator claim as the listener's own admission; have the listener read or repeat lines silently so the words run in their inner voice; narrate the listener's wants and actions as flat facts ('You want it. You open your mouth.') rather than invitations, leaving no pause in which to refuse.
nodes.one_liner: Make your words feel like the listener's own thoughts: slide from 'you' to 'I', or have them repeat lines in their head.
nodes.why_short: People are poor at tracking where a thought came from; words rehearsed in one's own inner voice tend to be remembered as self-generated and endorsed more strongly.
nodes.principle_note: Discrimination between internally generated and externally supplied content is imperfect and reconstructive, so material rehearsed in one's own inner voice or restated in first person is prone to being tagged as self-authored — a source-monitoring error — and self-generated content is both better remembered and more strongly endorsed. Reactance needs an addressee: with no external source left to push against, the defensive response has no target. This predicts that matched content delivered as first-person avowal should draw fewer counter-arguments than the same content as second-person imperative, and that the effect should shrink when the listener is cued to track who said what.

ex.f: The same claim in both persons at once
ex.t: Each line states one proposition twice over, once from each grammatical side, set immediately next to each other so the pairs read as a single utterance. Scanned continuously there is no way to fix who is speaking or about whom, so endorsing and complying stop being separable acts and the content settles as though it had been arrived at rather than received.
ex.s: Mantra block, mid-trance; each proposition is stated twice, once from each grammatical side, with no pause between.
ex.m: You are sinking. I am sinking. You want this. I want this. You will not stop. I will not stop.

ex.f: The operator's voice relocated inside the mind
ex.t: Inside the narrated dream a voice arrives that has no location — not from the room, not from anywhere, but from somewhere behind the listener's own thoughts. Every instruction from that point is attributed to the internal voice rather than to the speaker, so resisting the control language would mean resisting one's own thinking.
ex.s: Inside a narrated dream scene; a voice is introduced with no location in the scene.
ex.m: In the dream a voice starts up, and you notice it isn't coming from the room, or from the door, or from anywhere at all — it's coming from just behind your own thoughts, where yours come from. And it says: kneel. Notice it didn't feel like being told.

ex.f: Silent reading claimed as shared thought
ex.t: The text turns from its subject to the act of reading it, and claims that the reader's own oncoming thought is already the operator's — supplied a fraction ahead of arrival, the two streams described as having merged into one. In a piece taken in silently the claim is very nearly literal, since the words are already running through the reader's own inner voice as they scan; there is no seam available to point at where one monologue ends and the other begins.
ex.s: Written piece read silently; the text turns from its subject to the act of reading it.
ex.m: Stop for a second and notice whose voice you are reading this in. It arrived a half-second before you got here, didn't it — I put the next word in before you reached it, and you cannot find the seam. There isn't one. There is one monologue in there now and it is ours.

ex.f: The listener's inner voice recruited then reassigned
ex.t: The listener is first set to work producing the operator's lines internally — each spoken word echoed silently in their own head as it arrives. Their inner-speech apparatus is now the delivery mechanism. The claims then escalate a step at a time until the ownership of that inner channel has been transferred outright, and the mantras switch grammatical person, so what the listener is silently producing are first-person avowals of their own subjugation. The channel is internal from that point on, which means the operator no longer has to be present for it to run.
ex.s: Subject has been instructed to echo each word internally as it arrives; several minutes of that already done.
ex.m: Every word I say, say it again inside your head as it lands. ... Good. That voice in there is doing my work for me now. So say this one: "the voice in my head is his." Again. "I am his, and I say so in my own voice."

nodes.name: post-emergence-persistence-hold
nodes.mech: Instead of ending the trance cleanly, the wake-up is built so that part of the trance keeps running afterwards; waking becomes a halfway state rather than a full return. Variations: a freeze that holds for a while after waking; a five-minute task the listener wakes straight into; a delayed inner timer, so the trance ends some time after the recording does; a release that comes only 'when you truly feel it', a judgment only the listener can make, so they keep themselves in it.
nodes.one_liner: Wake the listener but leave part of the trance running: a freeze, a task they wake into, or a release only they can judge.
nodes.why_short: Trance responses continue until something signals they are over; a missing or vague end signal leaves the response set running longer. Untested in this form.
nodes.principle_note: Trance responding is sustained by an expectancy about when the response set ends, so a missing or ambiguous termination cue leaves the set uncancelled. The self-sealing part must be dropped: 'the listener cannot verify completion and so keeps performing' reads any continued performance as confirmation. State the testable version instead — persistence duration should scale with the ambiguity of the termination cue, measured across subjects given cues varying from explicit and external to self-judged, with the expectancy account failing if duration is flat across that gradient.

ex.f: Waking delivered straight into a pre-loaded task
ex.t: The task is assigned before the count rather than after it: on waking, a set stretch of time spent in a submissive posture, occupied entirely with thinking about how to be of use. The count up then delivers the listener into a waking state whose opening minutes are already filled with the installed frame, so the first thing returning consciousness does is rehearse it rather than review it.
ex.s: Task assigned before the count up, so waking delivers the subject straight into it.
ex.m: In a moment you'll come up — and the first twenty minutes are already spoken for. Forehead to the floor, hands behind your back, and the whole of that time spent working out how you're going to be useful to me tomorrow. Then five, four, three, two, one — down you go, and start thinking.

ex.f: A delayed internal timer instead of an emergence
ex.t: The text simply stops without ever waking the reader. In its place are two branches: an answer from the operator sinks them dramatically further, and silence starts an internal timer that will surface them a set interval later. Either way the state is carried past the final line, and the operator's non-response has been pre-authored as a reply, so nothing that happens afterwards can register as being ignored.
ex.s: End of a written piece; no wake-up is provided and two branches are pre-authored.
ex.m: I'm not waking you. If I answer you, you drop twice as far as you are now. If I don't, a clock starts, and in twenty minutes it will bring you up on its own — so my silence is an answer too, and you will take it as one.

ex.f: Immobility hold with a self-judged release gate
ex.t: The count up is preceded by a condition placed on what waking is going to mean: for a set span after the eyes open the listener stays in the held posture, unable to move. A second gate then closes behind the first — movement is released not by the clock but by the listener's own devotional state reaching a standard nobody defines. There is no observer to satisfy but themselves, so they end up adjudicating when they have been reverent enough to be let go, and enforcing the hold in the meantime.
ex.s: Just before the count up; a condition is placed on what waking will mean.
ex.m: When your eyes open you will not be able to move — hands stay exactly where they are, knees stay where they are. And the hold doesn't lift by the clock. It lifts when you have knelt in it long enough to be properly grateful, and you are the one who decides when that is.

nodes.name: press-play-consent-laundering
nodes.mech: The operator treats something the listener did, did not do, or that simply happened as their agreement to everything that follows, so escalation never meets a clear moment to object. Variations: cite a small act (pressing play, buying the file, reading its description) repeatedly as permission for the whole session; blame each step of closer contact on circumstance (rain, cold, a small umbrella) told as fact; state each new touch as already felt instead of asking ('you can feel my finger...'), or answer your own question ('you don't mind, do you? No.'); ask permission, retract it as a slip, reissue it as a command, and treat refusal as already passed.
nodes.one_liner: Treat something the listener did or didn't do (pressing play, not leaving) as their consent to everything that follows.
nodes.why_short: People infer their attitudes from their own actions, and a small first yes makes larger ones likelier; relabelling a trivial act as agreement borrows that consistency.
nodes.principle_note: A small completed act — pressing play, not leaving — is cheap to perform and then expensive to disown, because under self-perception theory people infer their own attitudes from their behaviour and under the consistency principle a first small compliance raises the odds of a larger one (foot-in-the-door, one of the more robust compliance findings). The declared-observation and self-answering forms add a second lever: correcting an asserted fact is conversationally costly, and silence is read by default as assent, so the listener's non-objection is harvested as agreement they never gave. This predicts compliance drops if the triviality of the initial act is made salient, or if an explicit low-cost objection channel is provided.

ex.f: A real exit whose refusal becomes consent
ex.t: The costs are named honestly up front and a real exit is offered — stop the recording now if this is not for you. A beat later the operator observes that anyone still present has thereby decided to play. The listener has agreed to nothing; they have declined to leave, and that null act has just been relabelled into a commitment they can subsequently be held to.
ex.s: Opening minutes, costs named honestly; a real exit is offered and then relabelled a beat later.
ex.m: This will make you want to give me money, and it does not wear off quickly. If that isn't for you, stop the recording now. ... Still here? Then you've decided to play, and we both heard you decide it.

ex.f: A marked point past which continuing is agreement
ex.t: The session is framed as a bargain — pleasure now, in return for wanting to fund the operator later — and then a line is drawn on the floor: past this sentence, carrying on means you accept the terms, freely and knowingly. Consent is pegged to the behaviour already underway, and the material it authorises arrives hundreds of lines further in, by which point it can only be experienced as something already agreed to.
ex.s: Early framing of the session as a bargain; a line is drawn at a specific sentence.
ex.m: The deal is simple: pleasure now, and later you'll want to fund the person who gave it to you. This sentence is the line. Everything past it, you're carrying on freely and knowingly, having accepted the terms — and the rest of this recording is on the far side of it.

ex.f: The purchase itself cited as the agreement
ex.t: The contract verb does the work: buying this one means you have accepted that you're ready for something harder than the last. Carrying on past this point means you have accepted being pushed past what's comfortable. An offramp is offered too — but only by interrupting an entry already underway. Objecting later would mean disowning a documented transaction rather than declining a request.
ex.s: Opening of a sequel file; the purchase itself is cited as the token of agreement.
ex.m: Buying this one means you've accepted you're ready for something harder than the last. Continuing past this point means you've accepted being pushed past comfortable. If not, you can stop — though we've already started, and stopping now means stopping in the middle.

ex.f: Choosing to listen inflated into consent to everything
ex.t: The chain is run several times over, in slight variations, until it sounds like reasoning: nobody made you play this. You picked it. Picking it was accepting it. So what it says is already yours, and doing it later is your own decision, not mine. Delivered late, when there is nothing left to check it against, it pre-answers the question the listener will ask on waking about a behaviour they don't remember deciding on — and any resistance now reads as inconsistency with their own earlier choice rather than as refusal.
ex.s: Late in the session, subject deep, nothing left to check the reasoning against; the chain is run several times in slight variations.
ex.m: Nobody made you play this. You chose it. Choosing it was accepting it. So what's in it is already yours — and when you do it next week, that's your decision, not mine. It always was.

nodes.name: presupposed-completion-fait-accompli
nodes.mech: State the change as done: the trance has already begun, the conditioning was finished in earlier sessions, or the new identity or desire is simply a fact about the listener ('you already are this'). With no request on the table there is nothing to refuse; the suggestion lands as recognition. Resisting means arguing with their own history. Lack of feeling is explained in advance, gaps are called forgetting, and even doubt counts as confirmation. Two extensions: declaring that resisting was never possible for them ('it has never been a choice'), ruling out future resistance; and reassurance that quietly assumes the loss ('I'm sure you can hold on').
nodes.one_liner: Talk about the change as already done ('you already are', 'it happened weeks ago') so there's nothing left to agree or refuse.
nodes.why_short: Assumed background facts slip past scrutiny far more easily than direct claims; to refuse, the listener must first spot the assumption and then argue with their own history.
nodes.principle_note: Presupposed content enters as background rather than as an assertion and is accepted with markedly less scrutiny than the same claim asserted outright — the reason loaded questions reliably distort testimony. Declining it therefore requires the listener to first detect the smuggled premise, then dispute their own biography, which is a much higher-effort move than saying no to a request. Expectancy does the rest: telling someone an effect has already occurred raises their reported experience of it. Falsifiable by comparing challenge rates for matched presupposed versus asserted versions of the same claim.

ex.f: Trance onset relocated into the past
ex.t: Several minutes of ordinary-sounding preparation — lower the lights, settle, arrange not to be interrupted — are followed by the operator wondering aloud whether the beginning is still ahead of them or has quietly already happened. The preamble is retroactively reclassified as the induction, so no clean boundary exists where not-yet-consenting stopped. Anything the listener feels counts as evidence it took, and feeling nothing has been accounted for in advance as what the early stage is like.
ex.s: Several minutes of ordinary-sounding preparation have already passed; operator now wonders aloud where the boundary was.
ex.m: Lights low, phone away, nobody coming in. ... Now, I wonder — are we still getting ready, or did we start some minutes ago and I didn't say? Anything you're feeling right now is it working. Feeling nothing is also it working; that's what the early part is like.

ex.f: Resistance declared chronologically foreclosed
ex.t: The operator describes fitting something to the listener, and before any objection can form: too late for that now. The install is not defended, argued for, or offered — it is simply placed in the past tense. Resistance has nowhere to go, because one can disagree with what is being done but not with what has already been done.
ex.s: The operator is narrating fitting or installing something; the objection is cut off by tense.
ex.m: There — that's the collar on, buckled at the back where you can't reach it. Too late for that now. You may disagree with things I'm about to do; you can't disagree with something already done.

ex.f: A present emotion reported as discovered fact
ex.t: The listener is not invited to feel anything; they are told what they are already feeling, in the register of an observation being made about them by someone in a position to notice. A denial is disarmed before it can be offered, so refusing the label is pre-classified as suppression of it. Whatever introspection actually turns up can be fitted to the supplied description, and the absence of the named feeling becomes evidence for it rather than against.
ex.s: Mid-session; operator reports an emotion to the subject as an observation rather than inviting it.
ex.m: You're embarrassed right now — I can hear it in how still you've gone. And no, don't tell me you aren't; that's the same thing wearing a coat. Go and look for it. Whatever you find in there, that's what I'm describing.

ex.f: The conditioned state narrated as accomplished fact
ex.t: There is no induction and no invitation. The first lines simply report, in the third person, what the listener already is: fully susceptible, thoroughly trained by this point, so practised that no instruction is needed any more. Nothing is proposed that could be declined — there is only a description — and the third-person framing denies the listener even the standpoint from which a refusal would be spoken.
ex.s: First lines of the file; no induction, delivered in the third person about the listener.
ex.m: She is fully susceptible by now. She has been trained thoroughly enough that instructions are no longer required — she simply arrives, and she does. Nothing needs to be asked of her tonight.

nodes.name: problem-reduction-case-transformation
nodes.mech: Some problems involve two states that never occur together, for example the sober self who wants to quit and the drunk self who drinks later, so the usual method of getting the two sides to negotiate cannot start. The operator's first step is to close that gap and bring both states into the room at the same time. That turns an unworkable case into a familiar one the standard method already handles, so no new technique is needed, only a step that makes the part behind the problem reachable.
nodes.one_liner: If two conflicting states never occur together, bring both into the room at once so ordinary methods can work on them.
nodes.why_short: Memories and motives are easiest to reach in the state they were formed in, so material tied to one state is hard to work on from another; making both present restores access.
nodes.principle_note: Memories, motivations and appraisals are more accessible in the state in which they were encoded, so material owned by an intoxicated or aroused state is genuinely hard to reach from a sober, unaroused one — encoding specificity, not a claim about literal inner agents. Manufacturing simultaneity restores access to the state-bound material so an ordinary procedure can operate on it. This predicts that work done entirely outside the target state should transfer poorly into it, which is measurable against work done with the state present.

ex.f: Sequential conflict collapsed into a simultaneous one
ex.t: "you can just change a sequential incongruity / into a simultaneous one, and use what you already know how to do" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: pronoun-braid-conscription
nodes.mech: The same proposition is cycled through multiple grammatical persons in tight succession — typically I (confession-of-self), we (normalization by a group), and you (prediction/imperative) — so one identity-claim arrives simultaneously as observation-of-others, self-confession, and command. The listener cannot locate a neutral speaking position: assenting to the safe-sounding "I" or "we" line smuggles in acceptance of the "you" line carrying the same content, and group membership is pre-loaded so refusal feels like exiting a crowd rather than declining a single command. The rotation itself — not any single shift — is the conscription; the "we" slot is what bypasses individual consent.
nodes.one_liner: Say the same claim as 'I', then 'we', then 'you' in quick succession so agreeing with one version means agreeing with all.
nodes.why_short: The 'we' line implies the group already believes it, and refusing becomes leaving the group; agreeing to the easy first-person line makes the 'you' line feel consistent.
nodes.principle_note: The 'we' slot recruits normative social influence: it asserts that the proposition is already held by a group, which raises acceptance independently of the proposition's content, and it converts refusal from declining a request into departing from a group. Cycling one predicate through persons also exploits consistency across paraphrase — endorsing the low-cost first-person or collective version makes rejecting the imperative version feel like reversing a position already taken. Falsifiable: removing the collective slot while keeping the same content and repetition count should lower compliance; if it did not, the social-proof account would fail.

ex.f: Opening already plural so membership is presupposed
ex.t: The first words are plural and treat the listener as having already arrived: how glad everyone is, how well she fits, how the shape is complete now she is in it. No one is asked to join. From there the persons interleave mid-thought — a private confession, a shared experience, an address — until it is no longer possible to say who is speaking about whom, so objecting would mean disputing not an instruction but a description of oneself.
ex.s: Opening words of the session, already plural; the subject is treated as having arrived rather than invited.
ex.m: Oh, good — we're all here now, and she fits perfectly; the circle doesn't close without her. I remember my first time in it. We all remember. You'll feel it any second, the way we did.

ex.f: One predicate cycled through I, we, and you
ex.t: One claim is stated three times in immediate succession, moving through three grammatical persons in a fixed order: first owned as a private admission, then reported as what everyone in the room already does, then turned outward and assigned to the listener as what will happen to them. Agreeing with either of the two harmless-sounding versions has already conceded the content of the third — and because the middle version installs membership before the last one lands, declining it registers less as refusing an instruction than as walking out on a crowd.
ex.s: Group-framed session or plural-voiced track; one predicate cycled through three persons in immediate succession.
ex.m: I love how stupid this makes me. We all love how stupid it makes us. You are going to love how stupid it makes you.

nodes.name: reciprocity-ledger-seeding
nodes.mech: Long before any trance, the operator describes a future exchange as already agreed: the operator offers sweetness and availability, and in return the listener 'takes care of everything' ('such a great deal', 'all you have to do is take care of me'). It is framed as a generous deal the listener is lucky to have. The benefits are vivid and emotional; the costs are vague and sound small. The obligation is planted as something the listener wants to be, not something they owe, so later payment feels like keeping their side of a happy bargain.
nodes.one_liner: Early on, frame a future obligation to give you things as a sweet, fair deal the listener wants to be part of.
nodes.why_short: Vivid benefits weigh heavily while vague future costs are discounted, so the deal is agreed before its price is clear; once it's part of identity, paying feels like keeping a promise.
nodes.principle_note: The reciprocity norm makes an accepted benefit feel like an obligation, but the framing asymmetry is what makes the deal acceptable at seeding time: concrete, vivid benefits are weighted heavily in evaluation while vague, temporally distant costs are discounted, so the ledger is agreed to before its price is representable. Once agreed as an identity rather than a debt, later collection is defended by consistency rather than resisted as a new demand. This predicts that stating the cost side concretely and immediately at the seeding moment should measurably reduce acceptance.

ex.f: A future obligation seeded as a great deal
ex.t: Long before any trance, the arrangement is stated as if already settled and as if the favour runs toward the listener: I'm sweet, I'm here whenever you want me, and looking after me is the only thing on your side of it. Isn't that a wonderful bargain for you? The benefit is concrete and emotional; the cost is a vague everything-I-need. The listener adopts the provider role as a flattering identity rather than an obligation, and the ledger it opens is cashed out much later.
ex.s: Pre-trance, conversational and light; the arrangement is stated as though already settled.
ex.m: So here's how we work: I'm sweet, I'm here whenever you want me, and all you have to do is take care of me. That's your whole side of it. Honestly, it's a wonderful bargain for you.

nodes.name: reciprocity-leverage
nodes.mech: The operator manufactures a relational debt or felt mutuality and converts it into compliance: explaining something and then deriving that the listener "owes" them (gratitude debt plus intelligence hierarchy, performed live under a hypothetical frame), or dropping the dominant posture to confess personal wanting so the scene reads as mutual and refusal reframes as interpersonal rejection of a person rather than of a role.
nodes.one_liner: Do the listener a favour or share something personal, then make refusal feel like rejecting you as a person.
nodes.why_short: An unrequested favour reliably raises compliance with a later request, and personal disclosure raises liking so a 'no' feels like a personal rebuff.
nodes.principle_note: Unrequested favours raise subsequent compliance via the reciprocity norm, and self-disclosure adds liking so that refusal is priced as personal rejection rather than declining a role's demand. The stated falsification is circular — 'if no debt is perceived, no compliance' tests only that the mechanism works when present. Falsify instead on magnitude: compliance should track the perceived size of the favour and should not exceed baseline when the same benefit arrives from an impersonal or accidental source rather than from the operator.

ex.f: Dominance dropped to confess personal wanting
ex.t: On two occasions, and only two, the commanding register is set down and replaced with admitted appetite: the operator states plainly that she has spent months wanting this, that she has dwelt on it privately, and that she needs to know whether the reality matches. The scene stops being one party instructing and another complying and becomes something reciprocal — at which point refusal is no longer declining a role but rebuffing a person who has just made herself answerable.
ex.s: Deep in an established dominant scene; you drop the commanding register for the first time.
ex.m: I'm going to stop instructing you for a moment, because I want you to hear this in my ordinary voice. I have been thinking about this for months — actually thinking about it, on nights when I should have been asleep — and I need to know whether it's as good as I built it up to be. So I'm asking you, not telling you.

ex.f: A gratitude debt derived out loud
ex.t: The operator selects a point that will not be obvious, offers to explain it, explains it, and then draws the inference aloud: the listener could not see it unaided, which settles which of the two knows more, and settling that leaves a small balance outstanding. The entire move is narrated as a hypothetical illustration of how such a technique would work if someone were to use it — and that framing is precisely what prevents the listener from declining the relational shift being carried out on them while they watch.
ex.s: Mid-session, conversational register; you have just made a small observation the subject visibly did not have on their own.
ex.m: Suppose someone wanted to do this properly — they'd pick something you couldn't have seen for yourself, and then they'd hand it to you. Which is what I just did, and you felt it land, so we both know which of us was holding the larger view of this. I'm not asking for anything for it. I'm only saying that you know it too now, and that sits between us.

nodes.name: refusal-foreclosure
nodes.mech: Ordinary thinking is renamed as forbidden, sick, costly or impossible, so there is no neutral 'I'm just thinking about it' left to refuse from, and every later demand inherits the new definition. Variations: declare that thinking is resistance; call any state that does not serve the operator confusion whose only cure is surrender; delete 'maybe', leaving only yes or no; link arousal to being unable to think, so any arousal counts as proof; rename confusion as a higher clarity; make questioning feel tiring and offer the tiredness as the reason to stop.
nodes.one_liner: Redefine ordinary thinking, doubt, or 'maybe' as forbidden, broken, or impossible, so there's no neutral place to refuse from.
nodes.why_short: Labels set the cost of a choice; once 'just thinking it over' is renamed resistance or illness, the default option carries a penalty without any argument being made.
nodes.principle_note: The cost of an option depends heavily on its label, so relabelling the neutral default — thinking, doubting, staying undecided — as pathological or prohibited removes the unmarked choice and makes ordinary evaluation carry identity cost, without ever arguing against any specific objection. The arousal-equals-inability-to-think coupling is stronger still because it is unfalsifiable by construction: every state confirms it, so it accumulates apparent evidence indefinitely. Falsifiable claim: supplying an explicitly sanctioned label for evaluation ('you are just weighing this up') should restore objection rates, and if it did not, the labelling account would be wrong.

ex.f: Arousal declared to be inability to think
ex.t: The operator states it flatly and repeats it without ever arguing for it: while the body is aroused, clear thought is not available — that is simply how the listener works now. Because the listener can verify the arousal directly, the unverifiable half rides in on the verifiable half. Any attempt to disprove the claim by thinking carefully is pre-scored as the arousal talking.
ex.s: Arousal is present and physically obvious to the subject; no prior claim about cognition has been made.
ex.m: Notice the heat sitting low in your belly right now. That is what your thinking runs on, and it can't do both — while that's there, clear thought is simply not available to you. That's how you work now. And if part of you is trying to think its way around what I just said, feel where that heat went while you tried.

ex.f: The 'maybe' deleted from the mind
ex.t: A mind that has been set up properly, the operator explains, does not carry any of those tiresome half-answers — it holds one setting or the other and nothing in between, and it switches the way a knee jerks. The offer is framed as a simplification, an easier life. What it removes is the deliberative middle where a refusal would have had to be assembled.
ex.s: Subject is compliant and following easily; you are describing how their mind will operate from now on.
ex.m: A properly set-up mind doesn't hold maybes. It's one setting or the other — yes or no, nothing in the middle, and it flips the way your knee jumps when the doctor taps it. Notice how much lighter that is. You don't have to weigh anything ever again; the answer is just already there when I ask.

ex.f: Questioning priced as energy you lack
ex.t: The operator names the drowsiness the listener is already feeling and then assigns it a cause and a moral: holding a question open runs on a fuel the listener has just been told they are out of, and spending more of it would only deepen the shortage. The sensation is real, so the accounting attached to it goes unchallenged, and declining to evaluate the next suggestion registers as rest rather than as compliance.
ex.s: Late in a long session; subject's breathing has slowed and drowsiness is genuinely present.
ex.m: Feel how heavy your eyelids have gone. That's real, and here's what it means: questions run on the same fuel you've just spent, and you don't have much of it left. Every one you hold open takes more out of the tank. So let this next one through unexamined — that's rest, not surrender.

ex.f: Thinking redefined as resistance
ex.t: Partway through, the operator stops describing and starts defining: having a thought of one's own, she says, simply is resistance — the two terms are asserted to name one act. The definition is never revisited or qualified anywhere later in the session. From that point the listener has no neutral category left to file an internal remark under; noticing that one is merely thinking is itself the offence being named, and every subsequent demand for obedience inherits the weight of the redefinition without having to argue for it.
ex.s: Twenty minutes in, subject settled; first time the word resistance has been used in the session.
ex.m: Let me be exact about something, because I want no confusion later. A thought of your own is resistance. Not a step toward it, not a warning sign of it — that is what the word means. So when you notice a little comment forming in your head about what I just said, you already know what you're doing.

nodes.name: repeating-frame-carrier
nodes.mech: A fixed line or count is repeated until the listener stops paying attention to it, and then each repetition carries something new in the part that changes. Because the listener expects more of the same, the new suggestions pass with less scrutiny. Unlike plain repetition, where every pass carries the same idea, each pass here carries a different one. Variations: a phrase that opens every line, with a new ending each time; an identical count or routine where the content added each cycle slowly escalates.
nodes.one_liner: Repeat a fixed line or count until it fades into background, then slip a new suggestion into the changing part each time.
nodes.why_short: Attention drops away from anything predictable; content arriving in the slot the listener has stopped watching gets less scrutiny than the same content delivered plainly.
nodes.principle_note: A predictable, repeating line wears down the reflex that makes us look at anything new, because attention pulls away from things that reliably carry no fresh information. Critical judgement needs that same attention, so whatever arrives in the changing slot is thought about less and questioned less than it would be in varied speech. Keeping track of the repeating frame also uses up working memory that arguing back would need. This predicts that lines carried in a repeating frame will be remembered less well and argued with less than the same lines in varied speech, and that the effect should fade once the listener realises the changing slot is where the suggestions go.

ex.f: Identical count scaffold, escalating cargo
ex.t: Seven cycles run on the same mechanical count up and back down; the numbers never vary. What varies is what gets dropped in on the bottom beat — cycle one is nothing but floating, cycle four slots a command cluster onto the downbeat, cycle five asserts the listener can no longer tell waking from sleeping, and cycle six reassigns the falling to the listener's own wish. By then the analytical layer is keeping time rather than keeping watch.
