ex.m: Hold on to the things you know you want — no arguing with those, they're properly yours. Concentrate on them, only them, and feel how easy that is. And whatever sits next to them slides in just as easily, including the ones I hand you; wanting the one is wanting the other.

ex.f: Each heavier claim as the next dictionary entry
ex.t: The passage is staged as a short vocabulary lesson: here is the first sense of the word, here is the second, here is the third. The first is unobjectionable — holding something as property. Each subsequent numbered sense claims more: being taken over, then owning what the listener's body does, then owning what they think. Because the format is a list of definitions, every increment arrives as a clarification of a term already accepted rather than as a fresh demand, and no point in the sequence presents itself as a decision. A listener who would have refused the last item outright never encounters it as an item to refuse.
ex.s: Mid-session, staged as a short vocabulary lesson on a word already accepted.
ex.m: Let's take the word own. First sense: to have a thing as your property — simple enough. Second sense: to have taken it over completely. Third: to have the say over what it does with its body. Fourth: to have the say over what it thinks. Same word all the way down, and you agreed to it at the first one.

nodes.name: any-response-is-depth-flywheel
nodes.mech: Tell the listener that whatever they do, or fail to do, takes them deeper: responding, not responding, drifting off. With no way to fail, 'I'm not doing this right' stops being an exit. Variations: short lines scattered through the session tying any response to depth, plus a claim each future session goes deeper; saying in advance that odd perceptions (sound out of sync with sight) are a pleasant sign of trance, so doubt reads as progress; with someone already deeply under, having them say each step aloud while sinking, so their voice fading to silence becomes their own proof of arrival.
nodes.one_liner: Tell them that whatever they do, or don't do, is taking them deeper, so there is no way to fail.
nodes.why_short: If every outcome counts as success, the listener never gets evidence that it is not working, so their expectation of going deeper is never challenged and can grow on its own.
nodes.principle_note: This is an unfalsifiable-test structure imposed on the subject: when every observation confirms the hypothesis, no evidence of failure can be gathered, and expectancy effects then run unopposed because the disconfirming observation that would normally correct them has been pre-defined as confirming. Exits that rely on 'this is not working' require a failure signal to trigger, so removing the signal removes the exit, not merely the doubt. Falsifiable at the level of the claim about people: it predicts subjects given a rigged all-outcomes-confirm frame report higher confidence in depth than subjects given a frame with a genuine failure criterion, at equal actual responsiveness.

ex.f: Any response, including none, counts as depth
ex.t: Scattered through the whole recording, never localized, is one repeated shape: responding at all is said to deepen the state. Not responding correctly — responding. Doing nothing scores as well, since stillness is the easiest response of all. Because the listener meets the rule in many different contexts, they generalize it rather than treating it as a single claim. What this costs them is the last failure-shaped exit: nobody wakes up from a session they cannot get wrong, and a further clause extends the claim across future listens.
ex.s: Delivered repeatedly in varied contexts across the whole recording, never localized to one beat.
ex.m: Whatever you just did with that — a twitch, a thought, nothing at all — that response took you deeper. Doing nothing counts too, and it's the easiest response of all, so it takes you deepest. And it works better every time you listen.

nodes.name: declarative-nested-trance-recursion
nodes.mech: Describe a trance inside this trance, then another inside that, four or more layers down, each declared deeper (often 'ten times deeper'). There is no way to check how many layers deep you are, so the listener can only accept the count, and 'am I deep enough?' always has another layer below. Variations: simply state the deeper layer exists; have them watch themselves being hypnotized on a screen, nested several times, building a detached, object-like view of themselves; inside an established scene, run a full second induction (pendant and countdown) to a level 'the conscious mind cannot follow', where not following what is said counts as correct.
nodes.one_liner: Describe a trance inside this trance, and another inside that, layer after layer, each one deeper, so they cannot tell how deep they 'really' are.
nodes.why_short: There is no inner gauge for hypnotic depth, so people rely on the labels they are given. Stacking unverifiable layers gives them nothing to check against except the operator's count.
nodes.principle_note: Depth has no interoceptive referent, so under that ambiguity the subject falls back on the external label supplied — the same substitution driving misattribution of arousal and demand-characteristic compliance. The self-watching variant recruits a real effect: third-person visual self-imagery reliably reduces reported emotional intensity. Falsifiable: the model predicts reported depth scales with the number of layers asserted and is uncorrelated with any behavioural responsiveness measure; if reported depth tracks responsiveness independently of the asserted count, label substitution is not the driver. (Dropped the working-memory-overload claim: the load of nested frames is not characterized and no observation was specified that would contradict it, and the prior test — subjects cannot disconfirm a claim about something stipulated to have no internal referent — is tautological.)

ex.f: A guaranteed layer below the current one
ex.t: The operator simply declares that the state the listener is in contains another state deeper than it, which contains another, and repeats the declaration four or more times across the recording. Nothing is built or counted down to; the assertion is the whole move. Since the listener has no way to verify being two layers in rather than one, the only available response is to accept the count — and the question of whether they are deep enough yet is retired permanently, because there is always another floor underneath.
ex.s: Mid-session, no count and nothing built; the bare assertion is repeated four or more times across the recording.
ex.m: The state you're in right now has another state inside it, deeper than this one. And inside that one, another, deeper still. And inside that one, another. There is always a further one waiting, so you never have to wonder whether you're deep enough yet.

nodes.name: staircase-deepener
nodes.mech: Have the listener picture descending: stairs, an elevator, sinking through water. Each step or floor counts as deeper, so 'how deep am I?' gets a concrete, steadily growing answer, and accepting each number accepts the ones before it. Naming the bottom in advance ('by the last step you'll be deep') makes the count impossible to fail. Variations: chain several descents with no coming back up between them; use numbered places or rooms ('you're in level two'), each bringing its own feelings; float into a dark, weightless void that removes sensory anchors; have them walk away from their own mind, following a light or the operator, promising to bring them back.
nodes.one_liner: Have them picture walking down stairs, riding an elevator, or sinking in water, counting each step or floor as deeper.
nodes.why_short: Pairs a familiar 'going down' image with a count, giving the listener a concrete way to track and expect deepening. Imagery deepeners are standard; the depth gained is mostly expectation.
nodes.principle_note: An abstract, unverifiable variable is made judgeable by mapping it onto space, which people track far more reliably than internal states — and spatial metaphor for magnitude appears to be a genuinely deep habit of human reasoning rather than a stylistic choice. Each accepted increment is a small assent, and the accumulated string of agreements makes the next one cheaper via consistency pressure, so the count does compliance work in addition to imagery work. Falsifiable: the account predicts a spatial vehicle produces higher reported depth and higher subsequent compliance than an equivalent bare assertion of the same magnitude with no spatial frame; if the two are equal, the spatial mapping is decorative.
steps: Build the image: a staircase, elevator, or water to sink through.
Count down, one number per step or floor.
Say each step takes them deeper.
Arrive somewhere calm at the bottom and settle there.

ex.f: Each step narrated as irreversible
ex.t: An ordinary counted staircase, with one clause added per step: the stairs behind have gone, and going back up happens only when permitted. The count still deepens, but it now also removes the option of un-deepening, so the modeled cost of stopping climbs with every step taken.
ex.s: A counted staircase already running; one clause is added to every step.
ex.m: Ten, and the stair behind your heel is gone. Nine — that one's gone too, nothing up there to stand on now. Eight. You'll go back up when I say you can, and not before. Seven.

ex.f: A corridor that keeps stretching on the operator's say-so
ex.t: The listener is walked along a passage toward a door at the end, and then told the passage keeps extending — whenever it feels like ground is being covered, it turns out not to be. Arrival is gated on the operator judging them ready. The metaphor the listener was using to track their own progress has quietly become a variable someone else owns, and a future line about not being far enough along needs no fresh justification.
ex.s: Subject walking a passage toward a door and feeling that ground is being covered.
ex.m: Keep walking — the door is at the end of it. Ah, but the corridor has gone longer again; you've covered no ground at all. You'll arrive when I decide you're ready for that door, not on your own legs. Keep walking.

ex.f: Rising numbers redefined as going down
ex.t: Standard descent, one clause inverted: on this elevator the numbers run backwards, so counting up takes the listener further down. The vehicle is decorative; the inversion is the mechanism. What it removes is the listener's intuition that ascending numbers mean surfacing, so the ordinary cue for coming out no longer points anywhere.
ex.s: Elevator vehicle established; the inversion is stated once, then the count runs on it.
ex.m: This lift runs backwards: the numbers go up and you go down. One — down. Two, further down than one. Three, deeper. Four, deeper again. Every number rising takes you further under, and there's no number on this panel that brings you up.

ex.f: Floor numbers mapped onto depth by contract
ex.t: The operator announces a ride down through a numbered series of levels and states the terms up front: by the bottom, the listener will be deep. Then each level is called out, with the number-to-depth correspondence restated as they go. The listener no longer has to evaluate whether anything changed — the announced number answers for them. Each acceptance is also a small ratification: agreeing they have reached a given level carries agreement that the previous claims held.
ex.s: Opening a descent; the terminus is pre-committed before the count starts.
ex.m: The lift starts at twenty, and by the time the doors open on one you'll be deep — that's the arrangement. Nineteen: deeper than twenty. Eighteen: deeper than nineteen. Fifteen — and everything I said about twenty and eighteen still holds, doesn't it. Twelve.

nodes.name: dual-variable-descent-yoking
nodes.mech: With each count down, make the listener both deeper and more aroused (or more obedient), so the two rise together and come to feel like one thing. Normally a spike of arousal can jolt someone awake; here it is used as fuel for depth. And resisting stops making sense when obedience itself is described as the weight pulling them down.
nodes.one_liner: On each count down, make them both deeper AND more aroused (or more obedient), so the two rise together and can't be pulled apart.
nodes.why_short: Two feelings repeatedly paired on the same schedule start to cue each other. Arousal, which would normally wake someone up, becomes part of the sinking instead.
nodes.principle_note: This is a stimulus-compounding move: two states presented in reliable temporal contiguity on the same escalating schedule become predictively linked, so a cue for one comes to evoke the other, and either can then serve as evidence that the pair is progressing. The tactical consequence follows from the coupling rather than from either variable — an arousal spike that would ordinarily be attributed to alertness is available for reattribution to depth, exactly the misattribution-of-arousal pattern in which an ambiguous bodily signal takes whatever label the situation supplies. Falsifiable: it predicts that decoupling the two variables in time (arousal at steps where the count is static) sharply weakens the fusion and restores arousal's ordinary alerting effect.

ex.f: Obedience as the ballast that drags the listener down
ex.t: Trance is mapped onto water, and the second variable yoked to the count is not arousal but compliance: an anchor is described as being obedience itself, growing heavier with each number and pulling the listener further under. Depth and submission become the same quantity. Resisting the descent now means fighting one's own ballast, which is self-defeating by construction, and the later ascent simply unwraps the same anchor.
ex.s: Trance mapped onto water; the count is running and the second variable is compliance, not arousal.
ex.m: There's an anchor tied at your waist, and the anchor is your obedience. Five, and it gets heavier. Four: heavier still, pulling you under. Three — every ounce of it is you doing as you're told, so pulling against it is pulling against yourself. Two.

ex.f: Arousal welded to the descent counter
ex.t: A counted staircase would ordinarily bind one thing to the steps: further down means more relaxed. Here a second, genuinely independent variable is bound to the same steps, and the contradiction is acknowledged out loud before being overridden — deeper and more excited, on every step. The two can no longer be separated. What that closes off is the usual escape valve, where rising arousal would pull the listener back toward alertness; here it is recruited as the thing doing the deepening.
ex.s: Staircase count running with arousal already present; the contradiction is named aloud before being overridden.
ex.m: Ten — deeper, and more turned on. I know those two aren't meant to go together; in here they do. Nine: heavier and hotter at once. Eight — the more it builds the further down it drives you, so don't fight the heat, ride it down. Seven.

nodes.name: false-bottom-depth-reframe
nodes.mech: When the listener reaches what feels like the bottom, take the bottom away, so they never feel deep enough to come back up. Variations: call the depth reached just the top of a new, deeper level and start again; push past a declared limit in other ways, such as further transformation or a scene change; say there is no bottom and the falling itself is the trance; remove the brakes they rely on ('no tiredness to slow you'); name a destination, then deny it; restart a countdown before it reaches one. A bottomless fall needs an explicit way to end it, or the listener is left with no landing.
nodes.one_liner: When they reach a 'bottom', tell them it is only the top of a new, deeper level, or that there is no bottom at all.
nodes.why_short: A self-check like 'am I deep enough yet?' needs an end point. Moving or removing the end point keeps them descending with no moment of arrival that would invite surfacing.
nodes.principle_note: A self-check only terminates if it has a criterion, so removing or relocating the criterion leaves the check running without a stopping rule — the person keeps evaluating and never reaches 'enough', which is what converts an arrival state into an open-ended process. It also exploits reference-point shifting: once a level is re-described as the new baseline, the previous progress stops being counted as progress and the person re-enters an effort loop without noticing the goalposts moved. Falsifiable: the model predicts subjects given a pre-committed, honoured terminus will report a satisfied endpoint and spontaneously stop self-checking, whereas those given a relocated or absent floor will not.

ex.f: The declared final state superseded by another
ex.t: The transformation completes and the recording appears to have arrived. Then a further stage is introduced — stiller, harder, more finished than the one just declared final — and is itself called the final step, as at least one earlier stage was. The listener learns by demonstration that any settled endpoint is provisional, which deepens the current state and pre-arms receptivity to whatever a repeat listen adds on top.
ex.s: A transformation has just been declared complete; the recording appears to have arrived at its endpoint.
ex.m: There — that's the last of it. You're finished. Except there's one more stage past finished: stiller than that, harder, set right through. Let the last of the give go out of you and settle into it. This is the final step.

ex.f: A scene change that lifts the depth ceiling
ex.t: Earlier the fiction imposed a cap: the listener had to stay presentable, since the scene was set somewhere public. Here the operator narrates walking them somewhere quieter and remarks that they are alone now — and the cap simply lifts. Slackness and blankness become permitted rather than suggested. A step-change in depth is delivered with no count and no explicit deepener at all.
ex.s: The fiction had capped visible slackness by placing the scene somewhere public.
ex.m: Come through here with me — mind the step. There. Door's shut, it's just us now, nobody to see you. So let your face go slack, let your mouth hang open, let all of it show; there's nothing left to hold up in here.

nodes.name: one-way-fractionation
nodes.mech: Give the listener an imaginary on/off button for their brain: pressing it switches thinking off, pressing again switches it back on. Cycle them through it, but each time their brain comes back on, describe it as a little more muddled than before ('like thinking through syrup', 'only pretending to be awake'). They feel in control of the button but not of what it does, and because waking is foggier each round, there is no normal state left to return to.
nodes.one_liner: Run fractionation, often with an imaginary brain on/off button they press, but each time they come up, say waking feels foggier than before.
nodes.why_short: The usual fractionation contrast, plus a claim that slowly redefines 'awake' as partly under. Any real effect comes from expectation and from the listener going along with the frame.
nodes.principle_note: The move exploits the split between agency over an action and agency over its outcome: pressing the button gives a strong sense of authorship, and people readily infer 'I did this' from the mere pairing of an intention with a following event, even when the event's content was determined by someone else. The baseline degradation works by adaptation — each cycle's 'awake' state becomes the comparison standard for the next, so the drift is measured against a moving reference and never registers as a loss. Falsifiable: it predicts subjects will report the poisoned waking state as approximately normal when asked to compare it to the immediately preceding cycle, but as degraded when asked to compare it to their pre-session baseline.
steps: Cycle them in and out of trance.
Optional: give them an on/off button so they run the cycle themselves.
Each return, say waking is a little foggier than last time.
Never fully restore the old waking baseline inside the session.

ex.f: A self-pressed button whose off-state degrades each cycle
ex.t: A control is hallucinated on the back of the listener's own hand: one press for blank, another to come back. The listener performs every press, so the action is theirs — but the operator has taken ownership of the hand, and redefines what coming back means afresh on each cycle. First it is being awake, then it is only acting the part, then it is thought that has to push through something thick. Ordinary fractionation restores the waking state between dips so the contrast can be felt; here the waking state is worse every time it is returned to. Nothing is left to climb back toward, because the baseline has been moving down the whole time.
ex.s: A hallucinated control is on the back of the hand, and the operator has taken ownership of that hand.
ex.m: There's a button on the back of your hand — press it. Off. Press again and you're awake. Press. Off. Press again, and this time awake only means acting awake, going through the motions. Press. Off. Press — and now every thought has to push through syrup to get anywhere. Press.

nodes.name: number-amnesia-convincer
nodes.mech: This creates a small memory gap on something trivial and well learned (the counted numbers, their phone number, their name) and uses their own failed attempt to recall it as first-hand proof of depth. The blank is not treated as a sign of the deep state but as what the deep state means. Asking them to try makes the blank their own and hard to deny; crediting them ('you did it') follows, and the success makes the next suggestions, such as a numb hand, land faster. If the numbers or the fact keep coming back, repair the suggestion, or take it as a sign the state isn't genuine yet.
nodes.one_liner: While they count backward, suggest the numbers fade and vanish, have them try to find the next one, call the blank proof of depth, then build the next suggestion on it.
nodes.why_short: A version of Elman's 'lose the numbers'. Expecting to forget, plus trying while relaxed, can produce a real-feeling blank, and seeing it raises belief. Untested as a depth measure.
nodes.principle_note: First-person evidence is weighted far above assertion — a retrieval failure the subject produces themselves is nearly impossible to argue with, so it functions as a convincer in a way that an operator's claim of depth cannot. The failure is also cheaply manufacturable without any special state: directed forgetting and retrieval-blocking effects show that instructing someone to try to retrieve a target while attending elsewhere reliably degrades access to over-learned material, so the blank is a real observation attached to a wrong causal story. Falsifiable: if this account is right, comparable retrieval failures should be producible in unhypnotized subjects given the same try-and-fail instruction — the depth interpretation, not the blank, is the unsupported step.
steps: Suggest the counted numbers will fade and disappear.
Ask them to try to recall the next one, so the blank is their own.
Name the blank as proof of depth and credit them.
Use the success to deliver the next, bigger suggestion.

ex.f: Numbers counted away as the depth gate
ex.t: "by the time you get down to ninety-eight you'll be so relaxed there won't be any more numbers" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: The subject's own wish secured before the effect
ex.t: "Want this to happen,' and he rather liked the idea… 'I wonder if that could happen to me?'" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Amnesia treated as the definition of the state
ex.t: "It is only when you are able to produce amnesia that you have the somnambulistic state." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: A vanished over-learned fact as proof of the state
ex.t: "I want the telephone number of your office to disappear from your mind... when you try to find it, it just isn't there" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: forget-but-crave-emergence
nodes.mech: At waking, tell the listener they will forget what happened, but leave them with a warm, unexplained pull to come back and listen again. With nothing recalled to question, they wake with only good feeling and an urge to return, and each return deepens the trance, the forgetting and the pull together. Variations: link it to other installed triggers so each strengthens the rest; point the pull at the next session in a series; tie it to orgasm, with the claim that fighting the urge only strengthens it.
nodes.one_liner: At waking, say they'll forget the session (or keep only the best parts), but leave a warm pull to come back, which they must earn.
nodes.why_short: Selective memory plus a lingering craving makes return feel self-driven. Mostly frame and expectation.
nodes.principle_note: Splitting recall from motivation works because liking and remembering are separable: evaluative conditioning transfers affect to a stimulus without requiring the person to recall the pairings that produced it, so positive valence toward returning survives the loss of any episodic record. The absence of a retrievable memory then removes the object that scrutiny would need to operate on — the person has an urge and no content to evaluate it against, and an unexplained urge is typically resolved by acting on it rather than auditing it. The loop is self-strengthening because each return adds pairings while subtracting reviewable material. Falsifiable: it predicts return-motivation persists at full strength in subjects who cannot report session content, and that restoring the content to memory reduces uncritical return.
steps: Suggest the session fades, or only the pleasurable parts remain.
Keep and name a craving to return.
Point that craving at the next listen.
Optional: say coming back must be earned.

ex.f: Forgetting keyed to opening the eyes, plus a pull forward
ex.t: Forgetting is presented as automatic and benign — the deeper part keeps whatever matters — and pinned to a single act the listener is about to perform anyway: opening their eyes. The connective work is done by a phrase repeated five times in fourteen lines, smuggling in an entailment that does not actually hold. Then, immediately, an instruction to pick another session and start it. The craving is left live and pointed at the next file, so the conditioning serializes forward while the installs stay sealed from review.
ex.s: Near the close, with the eye-opening act imminent and the next file within reach.
ex.m: When your eyes open, the details go — the deeper part of you keeps whatever matters, so there's nothing left for you to hold on to. Your eyes open, and it goes. Eyes open, and it's gone. Now open them, pick the next one, and start it.

ex.f: Fighting the compulsion strengthens it
ex.t: Before waking, memory-erasure is tied to a climax the listener is instructed to reach on their own, so the forgetting is keyed to something they perform. Then the compulsion is rigged: they are invited to fight it, and told that fighting is what strengthens it. Resistance after the session has been pre-converted into maintenance, and the whole habit is relabelled as an ordinary pleasant one so nothing prompts a second look.
ex.s: Pre-waking; the subject is instructed to reach climax on their own after the session ends.
ex.m: Finish for me tonight, on your own, and as you do the memory of all this goes out with it. Then tomorrow you'll feel the pull to press play again, and you're welcome to fight it — fight it as hard as you like, because pushing back is what makes it stronger. It's only a nice little habit anyway.

ex.f: Memory dissolved while the pull to return is kept
ex.t: The closing minutes do two things in the same breath. Conscious recall of the content is described as dissolving away, gated to finish by the end of the count. And a need to come back — daily, unexplained — is installed and left intact. The listener wakes with no material to review and no specific memory to object to, only the sense that something significant happened and a route to find out. Because returning deepens the trance, which deepens the forgetting, which sharpens the pull, the loop maintains itself with no further operator input.
ex.s: Closing minutes, the count-out about to run; content is sealed and a return-pull left live.
ex.m: Everything we did tonight is already dissolving — by the time I reach one there'll be nothing left of it to look at. What stays is this: tomorrow, around this hour, you'll want to come back, and you won't know why. That wanting is the part you keep. Five, four...

nodes.name: amnesia-suggestion
nodes.mech: Installs a memory gap by suggestion — instructs the subject that specified content (the session, an instruction, an installed feeling's rationale) will be unavailable to conscious recall, typically at or after emergence, so the material cannot be reviewed, contested, or revoked. The bare primitive: a declared forget targeting a bounded referent, optionally wrapped in a self-interested cover story (forgetting strengthens the training, forgetting feels good, "words go in one ear, accepted, out the other") or forward-binding to future listens. Includes the accept-and-forget process rule, the memory-wipe exit handshake, the "burst the bubble" terminal ritual, and the subconscious-only handoff that seals post-edge suggestions.
nodes.one_liner: Tell them plainly that when they wake, they will not remember some specified part of the session.
nodes.why_short: Responsive subjects really do fail to recall suggested material; the memories are blocked, not erased, and come back on a release cue. It works well only for highly suggestible people.
nodes.principle_note: Suggested amnesia does produce reliable retrieval failure in responsive subjects, and the best-supported reading is that access is blocked rather than the trace destroyed — reversibility on a cancellation cue is the standard finding. Whatever the storage question, the operational consequence is what matters here: material that cannot be retrieved cannot be evaluated, contested, or withdrawn from, so the suggestion removes the review step rather than the content. The cover stories work by supplying a benign reason to comply, which reduces the reactance that a bare 'you will not remember' would trigger. Falsifiable and repeatedly tested: it predicts a reversibility cue restores recall, which distinguishes this from actual encoding failure.

ex.f: A bare forget-command closing the session
ex.t: A single short instruction, issued once and not argued for: forget everything this session contained. It fires an already-conditioned cue rather than building anything new, and it lands after the instructions and before the closing repetitions — so what is erased is the mechanism, and what survives in conscious reach is only the repeated assertion. The ordering carries the whole effect; reversed, there would be nothing to forget yet.
ex.s: End of session, all instructions delivered, just before the closing repetitions; subject deep and already responsive to short commands.
ex.m: Good. Now let it all go — everything from tonight, every word of it, gone the moment you open your eyes. All that stays is what you already know: you like listening to me.

ex.f: Forgetting sold as strengthening the training
ex.t: The forget-instruction arrives with a reason attached: the conditioning works better if none of it is consciously retained, and — the operator adds — this is what the listener wants anyway. Refusing now means opposing one's own stated preference rather than an operator's demand. A further clause extends the block to future listens, so the material is closed to review not only tonight.
ex.s: Late in the session, conditioning block complete; subject has already agreed the training is something they want.
ex.m: This works best when none of it stays where you can pick at it. You didn't come here to analyse — you came here to change, and thinking about it is what slows the change down. So let the conscious part keep nothing, tonight and every night you listen to me after this.

ex.f: The rest addressed to the subconscious only
ex.t: At the least defended point in the session, the operator announces that everything from here on is addressed to the deeper mind alone and will not be available on waking — then keeps talking. The conscious listener has effectively been dismissed from the room while the delivery continues. Whatever follows cannot afterwards be examined, agreed to, or taken back, because its content is never known.
ex.s: Deepest point of the session, after a long induction; subject unresponsive to conversational address, breathing slow and even.
ex.m: Everything I say from here is for the deeper part of you — the conscious mind isn't needed for this and won't be keeping any of it. It can go quiet now. Deeper mind, listen closely, because the next part is yours alone.

nodes.name: blank-then-authorship-handoff
nodes.mech: Once the listener's mind is quiet or blank, tell them the operator's words will now become their own thoughts, or simply their reality, so later suggestions no longer feel like someone else's claims. Variations: put all their thoughts into a single candle flame and blow it out, 'still there, still safe', in the same breath as saying the operator's words become their reality; during sleep, claim to be their own subconscious or the source of their dreams, so whatever they give in to feels self-made and there is no outside voice to push back against.
nodes.one_liner: Empty their mind (e.g. blow out a candle holding their thoughts), then tell them your words will now become their own thoughts.
nodes.why_short: Telling apart a thought you made from one you heard is a guess based on cues. With the mind quiet and the source blurred, suggested content can feel self-generated.
nodes.principle_note: Source-monitoring error is the mechanism: judging whether a thought was self-generated or externally supplied is an inference from cues like fluency, vividness, and effort, not a stored tag, and it fails predictably when internal ideation is suppressed and external input is the only material available. A cleared channel plus a stated attribution rule supplies exactly the misleading cues, so operator content gets filed as self-produced. Content believed to be one's own is not argued against, because there is no external agent to resist. Falsifiable: it predicts subjects will misattribute externally-supplied content to themselves at higher rates when their own ideational stream has been suppressed first, and that supplying a salient external source cue reduces the effect.

ex.f: The operator claiming to be the listener's own inner source
ex.t: Rather than suggesting what the listener should dream, the operator claims to be occupying the part of them that produces dreams. Content that follows is therefore framed as self-generated rather than received, which leaves resistance with no external target to push against. The unverifiability is load-bearing: forgotten dreams are said to work anyway, so nothing can be checked.

ex.f: The light put out and the operator's words installed instead
ex.t: One vivid object is built, a small light said to illuminate everything the listener is thinking, and a short counted breath puts it out. The framing is careful: nothing has been removed, it is all intact and unharmed, the listener simply cannot see any of it now, which lets the loss land without alarm. In the same breath a replacement is named: what the operator says will now be what the listener sees. The blanking only clears the way; the real move is handing over authorship, so every later suggestion arrives as the listener's own reality rather than someone else's claim.

nodes.name: choice-framed-amnesia
nodes.mech: Offer forgetting as the listener's own choice, or as fine either way ('remember or forget, whichever is easier'), so no outcome counts as failure and whatever they forget feels self-chosen. Variations: offer the choice after training them to prefer obeying, so 'easier' leans toward forgetting; say full, partial or no forgetting all count as success; hand the choice to 'your subconscious, as much or as little as it allows'; arrange it so both choices keep the suggestion working (forgetters can't review it, rememberers file it as a harmless talk); state the memory simply 'was never formed'; make taking the memory seriously sound silly.
nodes.one_liner: Offer forgetting as their choice: 'remember or forget, whichever is easier', so any outcome counts and feels self-chosen.
nodes.why_short: No outcome can count as failure, so the expectation is never corrected; and a permissive suggestion is harder to resist than a direct order because there is nothing to push against.
nodes.principle_note: Framing every outcome as success removes the disconfirmation condition, so the suggestion cannot be observed to fail and expectancy is never corrected. The choice framing does separate work: a choice that is felt as free but structurally constrained still recruits self-perception and dissonance-reduction, and it defuses reactance, which is triggered by perceived restriction of freedom rather than by the actual restriction. The ridicule shield adds a social cost to the one behaviour — serious recall — that could produce a disconfirming report. Falsifiable: the account predicts subjects given the permissive framing report less resistance and more post-hoc ownership than subjects given an identical instruction phrased as a command, at equal actual recall.

ex.f: Optional forgetting plus a ridicule shield
ex.t: On the way out, the listener is offered the choice to drop the session's memories, with keeping them framed as leaving the recording unfinished rather than as a loss. Then a closing aside: the idea that anything was done to them is treated as faintly absurd, not worth dwelling on. The second move covers what the first misses — a memory that leaks anyway arrives pre-tagged as not worth thinking about. It is not an instruction to stay quiet, which would be noticeable and refusable; it is a social embarrassment attached to reflection.
ex.s: Final thirty seconds of the recording, subject surfacing; playful, offhand register.
ex.m: You can drop the memory of all this if you like — no need to carry the whole recording around with you, that's what replaying it is for. And really, the idea that anything was done to you here — come on. You just listened to a voice and relaxed.

ex.f: Amnesia asserted as a memory that never formed
ex.t: Nothing is commanded here. The operator simply describes a structural fact: the part of the listener that would have recorded the last few minutes was not present for them, so no memory was ever laid down. Any gap the listener then notices confirms the account, and any recall gets attributed to the other part — so the framing cannot be tested from the inside, and a blank prompts recognition rather than investigation.
ex.s: Right after a dense install block; delivered flat and descriptive, like reporting weather.
ex.m: The part of you that writes things down wasn't in the room for the last few minutes. Nothing was recorded, so there's nothing there to find — not a gap, just a stretch that was never written. If you go looking and find nothing, that's simply what an unwritten stretch feels like.

ex.f: Remember or forget, whichever is easiest
ex.t: At waking, the listener is told their mind may keep the session or let it go, whichever takes least effort. On the surface this is permissive to the point of declining to suggest anything. But the decision is routed to the part of them that has spent the whole session being trained toward one set of responses, and least-effort names whatever has been most rehearsed. Whatever they end up retaining is then attributed to their own preference rather than to the framing, so the outcome is weighted and self-owned at once.
ex.s: Emergence sequence, immediately before the count up; a full session of rewarded compliance sits behind it.
ex.m: Your mind can keep tonight or let it slip, whichever takes less work. Don't decide — just notice which one is easier. Whatever's easier is the right one, because it's yours.

nodes.name: confabulation-amnesia-barrier
nodes.mech: Keep a second persona's memories hidden from the everyday self (in one or both directions), and tell the everyday self to invent believable explanations for anything that doesn't add up: unfamiliar clothes, places, things people mention. Add specific cover instructions too, such as ignoring the outfit, changing quickly, or assuming it was for 'some interesting occasion'. Because the gap is actively explained away rather than simply blank, it is much harder to notice, question or undo.
nodes.one_liner: Keep an alter-self's memories hidden from the everyday self, and tell the everyday self to invent a plausible story whenever something doesn't add up.
nodes.why_short: When memory has a gap, people naturally fill it with a believable story rather than notice a blank. Instructing that in advance protects the split from being noticed.
nodes.principle_note: Rests on confabulation as a normal property of memory: when episodic retrieval fails, people spontaneously generate a plausible narrative to fit the available cues rather than reporting a blank, and they experience the fabrication as recall. Pre-supplying the cover-story habit and a disposal script removes the physical anomalies that would otherwise force the gap into awareness, so no discrepancy accumulates to prompt review. Falsifiable: if subjects reliably reported unexplained gaps and treated residual evidence as anomalous rather than smoothing it, the account fails.

ex.f: Paired triggers with mutual amnesia and a supplied excuse
ex.t: Two phrases toggle between two named states, and each is defined as unable to recall the other — the audit trail erases itself from both directions. The clause that makes it hold is the pre-supplied explanation: on returning, the listener will account for anything odd about how they are dressed as having got ready for some occasion. Without that line the discrepancies would surface and the partition would collapse on the first look in a mirror.
ex.s: Both state-trigger phrases already installed and tested; setting the boundary before waking.
ex.m: The one of you doesn't remember the other. When the second phrase brings you back, the last hour is not yours and the first phrase is not a word you know. And if you catch yourself in the mirror wondering about the outfit, the answer is simple and you'll reach it instantly: you were getting ready for something.

ex.f: Forget the gap, then invent something to fill it
ex.t: Two instructions are issued together. The first is ordinary: on returning to normal, the listener will not recall what they were like in the other state. The second is what makes it durable — they are pre-authorized to invent whatever explanations are needed to smooth over anything that does not add up. Plain forgetting is brittle, because the world leaves evidence and evidence prompts questions. Here the listener's own narrative-repair habit is recruited in advance to defend the gap. A weaker version runs the other way too, so the cue stays out of conscious reach until someone speaks it.
ex.s: After a state trigger has been established and rehearsed; subject currently in the installed state, being prepared for the return.
ex.m: When you come back to yourself, none of what you were like just now comes with you. And if anything doesn't add up afterwards — the time, the state of the room, why you're where you are — you have my permission to come up with whatever explanation makes it make sense, and to believe it. Your mind is good at that. Let it.

nodes.name: container-externalized-erasure
nodes.mech: Have the listener put a memory, thought or feeling into an imagined container (a bubble, box, jar, candle flame, drain), then destroy or remove it with a clear felt moment: a pop, a slammed lid, a breath that blows it out. The listener packs the item themselves while the operator, or one scripted action, disposes of it, so forgetting becomes a distinct event rather than a vague absence. Once rehearsed, the same action ('pop it', 'drain it') can be aimed at new things one after another without a fresh induction. Variations: the contents can be small worries, specific memories, identity, or the conscious mind itself.
nodes.one_liner: Have them put a memory or thought into an imagined box, bubble or jar, then destroy it with a clear 'pop' or slam.
nodes.why_short: A concrete image with a definite ending feels like something actually happened, more than a vague 'forget it'. A felt moment of deletion makes the forgetting easier to believe.
nodes.principle_note: Works by giving an abstract instruction a concrete perceptual referent and a discrete completion event — imagery-based tasks with a definite endpoint produce a stronger felt sense of having occurred than open-ended verbal assertions, and a punctate cue ('pop') gives the subject an unambiguous marker to attribute the outcome to. The agency split adds a plausibility layer: the subject does not perform the final act, so ordinary self-attribution of control does not conflict with the claim that the content is gone. Falsifiable: predicts container framings outperform matched flat forget-suggestions on reported completeness; equal performance would refute it.

ex.f: One object mapped to the whole conscious mind
ex.t: A single small light is named as the listener's thinking mind — whatever it illuminates is what they can see in there. The operator is careful to specify that putting it out destroys nothing: every thought remains intact and unharmed, only invisible. A brief count then extinguishes it, and the mind goes from lit to dark in one staged event. The operator's voice is offered as the replacement source of anything the listener sees from that point on.
ex.s: Early-mid session; subject can visualize on command and has confirmed seeing the object.
ex.m: That little flame is your thinking mind — everything it lights up is everything you can see in there. Nothing is being taken away, understand: it all stays exactly where it is, safe, whole. You just won't be able to see any of it. Breathe in, two, three — and out. Dark. From here, what you see is whatever I describe.

ex.f: One removal verb, a sliding referent
ex.t: The first pass moves tension out through a single visual channel, and the listener feels the pull. After that the operator never re-explains the mechanism, only swaps the cargo: memories next, then feeling, then volition, then the listener's own name — each announced as simply the next thing going the same way. Four separate erasures ride one rehearsed action, so by the third the listener is already pulling before hearing what is being pulled.
ex.s: Third or fourth repetition of the same drain image; subject already reports the pulling sensation without prompting.
ex.m: Feel it draining out through your heels again. That's the tension gone. Now the memories, same way, same pull — down and out. Good. Now the feeling. Now the wanting to decide. And now your name, right out through your heels with the rest of it.

ex.f: Object ritual with a bodily convincer
ex.t: Forgetting is staged as a small physical routine: a container opens by itself, the thought drops in without the listener having to push it, and a brief swimmy jolt behind the eyes is named as the sensation of it leaving. The lid shuts, fastens, and the whole thing drifts out of reach; another container is always waiting, so the routine can never run out. The jolt is what makes it convincing — the listener now has a felt event to point at, indistinguishable from ordinary failure to recall.
ex.s: Subject reports floating sensation and has confirmed a specific thought held in mind.
ex.m: There's a small tin sitting open beside you. Don't push — the thought drops in by itself. There. Did you feel that swim behind your eyes, that half-second tilt? That's it leaving. Lid down, catch clicks, and the tin floats off out of reach. There's another one open already, so bring me the next one.

ex.f: Listener fills the container, operator destroys it
ex.t: The operator offers a container and asks the listener to move one category of memory into it — the earliest years first — letting it drain out of their head until the vessel is full, then checks that nothing has been left behind. Only after that confirmation does the operator perform the removal, in a single word, and follow it with a line about how good the forgetting feels and a check that nothing comes back. The rounds then repeat with progressively heavier cargo: schooling, restraint, sharpness, and finally what the listener is called. Each round is identical in shape — the listener does the loading, one operator action does the destroying, a reward line closes the beat. Because the listener never performed the deletion, there is no moment they can point to where they let it go, and each successful round is offered as evidence the next, larger target will go just as easily.
ex.s: Mid-session, deep; a wide-mouthed jar has been established in the subject's hands and one round already rehearsed.
ex.m: Open the jar and tip your head. Let everything from before you were ten pour out of you into it — the house, the birthdays, the faces. Keep tipping until nothing's left in there. Is it empty? Good. Watch me. Gone. Feel how light that is — nothing coming back, is there? Now open the next jar, and this one takes school: everything you learned, everything you were taught to be careful about.

nodes.name: contradiction-as-amnesia
nodes.mech: Rather than telling the listener to forget, calmly talk as if recent events never happened: 'we've only just started', 'this is the first time we've talked about this', even about something they physically just did, like kneeling, without acknowledging it. Repeated, this makes them doubt their own timeline, and by midway 'how many times have we done this?' becomes a real puzzle. Variations: jump forward between scenes in a story, then call the natural gap (nothing happened there to remember) proof the conditioning is working, used again and again as a deepener.
nodes.one_liner: Calmly act as if recent things never happened ('we've only just started'), without acknowledging them, until they doubt their own memory.
nodes.why_short: A confident outside account can overwrite a weak memory trace; people give weight to a source's certainty. Repeated contradiction erodes trust in one's own recall.
nodes.principle_note: Rests on the misinformation effect and social contagion of memory: a confident, unhedged contradiction from an external source competes with a weak episodic trace, and people weight source confidence when judging whether an event occurred, so the denial can displace the original report. Whether repeated contradiction degrades timeline confidence *generally* rather than only for contested items is not established and should be treated as the speculative extension, not the documented core. Falsifiable: the effect should weaken sharply for recent, distinctive, physically enacted events, and generalized self-doubt should show up on uncontested items if the broader claim holds.

ex.f: Story cuts relabelled as trance amnesia
ex.t: The narrative jumps from one day to the next, and the operator leans into the seam: if the listener is hazy on how they got from then to now, that is treated as exactly what should be expected given everything that has supposedly been happening between scenes. No gap is installed; the listener simply cannot recall scenes that were never narrated, and that ordinary blank is handed back as proof the conditioning has been working off-page.
ex.s: Mid-file, immediately after a scene transition from one narrated day to the next.
ex.m: Now it's the next morning. And if you're a little unclear on how you got from last night to here — of course you are. Quite a lot happened in between, and it's not the sort of thing that stays. That haze is exactly what it should feel like by now.

ex.f: Casual denial that anything just happened
ex.t: Well into the session, in the same bright conversational tone as everything else, the operator remarks that they have only just begun. A little later, that they are fairly sure this particular exchange has never happened before — and invites the listener to agree, who cannot say either way. Then, noticing the listener's posture, the operator wonders aloud when they ended up on the floor, since they certainly were not a moment ago. No forget-instruction is ever issued and no contradiction is ever acknowledged; the operator simply narrates a present that excludes the last several minutes, including a position the listener adopted with their own body. Ask them later how many rounds there have been and no answer comes.
ex.s: Twenty minutes into a session with several completed cycles; subject kneeling, having been directed there earlier; bright conversational tone throughout.
ex.m: Right, so — we're just getting started, you and I. And I'm fairly sure this is the first time we've ever talked about this, isn't it? Hm. Also, when did you end up on the floor? You were in the chair a second ago.

nodes.name: covert-age-regression-state-reaccess
nodes.mech: Draw the listener back into a childlike state without ever telling them to go back to an age. Instead, bring up a near-universal early-learning struggle in the present tense (telling b from d, whether a 6 is an upside-down 9, the first day of school), play a tune in their head from a chosen time of life, or leave a phrase open so they fill in 'as a child' themselves. Since nothing is commanded, there is nothing to refuse; attention narrows, and the openness, forgetfulness and suggestibility of that earlier state come along.
nodes.one_liner: Without commanding regression, evoke a shared childhood struggle (b vs d, first school day) in present tense so they drift childlike.
nodes.why_short: Cues strongly tied to a period of life make memories and feelings from that period easier to reach. Because nothing is commanded, there is nothing obvious to refuse.
nodes.principle_note: Depends on state-and-context-dependent retrieval: reinstating cues strongly associated with a life period (the specific errors of early literacy, period-indexed music, childhood-framed address) preferentially activates memories and response tendencies encoded in that period, shifting self-description and behaviour toward it. Because the cue is an association rather than a command, there is no proposition to evaluate or decline, so compliance costs nothing. It does not require any literal reversal of development — only that period-linked material becomes more accessible. Falsifiable: predicts period-matched cues produce more regression-typical responding than neutral cues of equal vividness.

ex.f: Undetermined phrase scope that lands as a state
ex.t: "the ambiguity is whether the phrase as a child refers to Erickson or to the client, thus, the effect is a scope ambiguity which induces age regression on the part of the client." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: A shared early-learning difficulty, present tense
ex.t: "How is it different from a 'd'… children have exactly this difficulty - thus, age regression suggestion." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: A melody chosen for the age it indexes
ex.t: "give the client some melody to play inside his head which indirectly suggests age regression. We have found nursery rhyme melodies particularly effective." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: covert-amnesia-installation
nodes.mech: Slip forgetting in without a recognizable 'you will forget', so it avoids the scrutiny a direct command would get. Variations: build it into the story's physics (a black hole nothing escapes), so later failure to recall is already explained; describe losing one's name as just a fact of the fantasy setting; tuck a forget instruction into casual chat at waking; drop a specific item (the number five) by leaving it out of a count presented as complete; wake them by 'rewinding' to the moment before trance, so forgetting comes as a side effect.
nodes.one_liner: Slip forgetting in as story-physics or small talk ('a black hole nothing escapes') instead of saying 'you will forget'.
nodes.why_short: People resist things they recognise as persuasion attempts. A suggestion that doesn't look like one draws less pushback.
nodes.principle_note: Turns on the fact that people evaluate propositions they recognize as persuasive attempts far more critically than incidental information — the recognition of intent is what triggers counterarguing. Delivered as scene-description, small talk, or an omission, the same content is encoded without the resistance a labelled command draws, and a pre-supplied explanation for later non-retrieval means the eventual gap confirms the frame instead of prompting alarm. Falsifiable: predicts matched content produces less counterarguing and better-accepted outcomes when framed as description than as instruction.

ex.f: Deletion by modelled omission under a truth guarantee
ex.t: The operator rebuilds the listener by counting the pieces back into place, and the recited list runs from one to twelve with a single number quietly absent from the middle of it. Each pass ends with the assurance that the set is complete and that nothing at all is missing. The count is run several more times, always identical, always short the same item, always under the standing rule that in this state whatever the operator says is simply so. The absent item is never named, so there is nothing to refuse; the listener is only ever shown the sequence without it.
ex.s: Reassembly phase near the end; subject accustomed to accepting operator statements as literally true in this state.
ex.m: Let's put you back together. One, two, three, four, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve — all present, nothing missing, complete. Again: one, two, three, four, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve. Whole. And in this state, whatever I say is simply so.

ex.f: Arousal and amnesia delivered as small talk
ex.t: "wider awake than you were earlier this morning (this last statement is… an indirect, emphatic, definitive instruction to arouse)" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Waking by restoring the pre-trance state
ex.t: "gently indirectly awakened from the trance by the simple suggestion that he adjust himself in his chair to resume the exact physical and mental state he had had at the decision to discontinue" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Amnesia disguised as the physics of the descent
ex.t: The descent is given a physics: at the bottom of the drop sits something whose pull nothing climbs back out of. The operator spells out the consequence rather than issuing an order — anything that goes over the edge is simply not retrievable, and attention that turns toward the edge goes over with it. Nothing here is phrased as an instruction, and there is no forget-command to decline. What has been installed is an explanation waiting to be cashed: when the listener later reaches for what was said and finds nothing, the absence is already accounted for as a property of the place they went, not as something done to them.
ex.s: During a descent induction, before the main suggestions are given; subject following the downward imagery.
ex.m: Keep going down. At the bottom of this there's a weight so heavy that nothing which falls past it ever comes back up — not light, not sound, not a single word. Anything that goes over that edge is simply not retrievable. And any part of your attention that turns to look at the edge goes over with it.

nodes.name: practice-then-aim
nodes.mech: Create a brief moment in which the listener's means of objecting have just been switched off, then state the new claims (who they are, that they need the operator, that they serve) as flat facts into that gap. Typically a 'delete that word' reflex, first practised on harmless words, is fired at loaded ones like 'resistance', 'disobedience' or their own name; because they agreed to it while it seemed meaningless, it fires before they can weigh in. Claims made in that gap feel, on waking, as if they met no resistance. Variations: wear them out until they 'can't remember who they serve', then fill the blank with the operator.
nodes.one_liner: Drill a reflex (like 'erase that word') on harmless items until it's automatic, then fire it at the real target and state the new claims.
nodes.why_short: A practised reflex runs faster than judgment, and harmless practice raises no objections. Plausible; untested in this form.
nodes.principle_note: The load-bearing and defensible lever is that a claim encountered without competing considerations is endorsed more readily, because rejection requires actively generating a counter-case — so making objection-relevant concepts inaccessible removes the material a counter-case would be built from. The 'acceptance precedes evaluation' framing invokes the Spinozan-belief account, which is contested rather than documented, and should be labelled as such rather than stacked as a second established mechanism. Falsifiable: predicts identical claims are endorsed more strongly after objection-relevant concepts are made inaccessible than after neutral material; no difference would refute it.
steps: Train a neutral reflex on harmless items.
Fire it at loaded words like 'resistance'.
Immediately state the identity or obedience claims as facts.

ex.f: Positive claims stated into the emptied window
ex.t: Straight after the erasures, with the blankness still fresh, the operator raises the listener partway and states a block of claims flatly, one after another: who she is to them, that there is nobody else occupying that position, what they are now dependent on, and under what conditions release is permitted. None of it is argued for, because argument was one of the things just deleted; on waking, the listener finds these claims sitting in memory as things they met and did not object to.
ex.s: Immediately after an erasure sequence; subject brought up slightly, blankness still fresh, delivered flat and unargued.
ex.m: Open your eyes a little. I am the one you answer to. There is no one else in that position. You need my voice now the way you need water. And you don't come unless I say the word.

ex.f: A gap manufactured so the operator can fill it
ex.t: Service has been described vaguely all session — someone, a teacher, a figure of authority. Deep in the count the operator asks who it is the listener serves, leaves the pause open long enough for the reach to fail, then answers it herself: too far down to hold a name, she says, and supplies her own. The forgetting was engineered upstream precisely so this blank would be sitting there to occupy.
ex.s: Deep in a slow count; the object of service has been referred to only vaguely all session.
ex.m: Tell me — who is it you serve? Say the name. ... No. Nothing there, is there. You're too far down to hold a name that heavy. So I'll hold it for you: it's me. It has always been me.

ex.f: A trained neutral reflex pointed at loaded words
ex.t: The erase drill has been run a dozen times on meaningless letters until the drop is automatic. Then the word on the board changes to a loaded one, and before the wipe the operator reframes it as a weight — something costing the listener effort to keep holding up, something that drains them. Then the same wipe command as always. The trained reflex fires before anything can evaluate what it fired on, and the outcome is immediately narrated as fact: there is nothing left there for the mind to take hold of. The listener has just felt exactly that, so the claim reads as description rather than instruction. The same three beats then run on two further loaded words.
ex.s: After a dozen rehearsals of the wipe drill on nonsense letters; the reflex now fires within a beat of the command.
ex.m: New word on the board: resistance. Look how heavy it is — you've been holding that up all this time, and it costs you something every minute you keep it there. Set it down. Wipe. Clean. Nothing there now for your mind to take hold of — you can feel that, can't you? Next word on the board: doubt.

nodes.name: fabricated-forgetting-priming
nodes.mech: Keep telling the listener they are forgetting something, then 'reveal' a new idea or object as the forgotten thing, so it feels like it was always there and lands as remembering rather than being introduced. Variations: drop it into casual conversation as gentle nagging ('what is it you're forgetting?'); name specific, checkable-sounding personal details they find they can't confirm (a lipstick shade, how a uniform fits), so they doubt their own history and real changes can't be told apart from how they always were.
nodes.one_liner: Keep insisting they are forgetting something, then 'reveal' a new idea as the thing they forgot, so it feels like it was always there.
nodes.why_short: Repeatedly searching for a memory makes the searched-for thing feel familiar, and familiarity is easily mistaken for remembering. New content then feels old.
nodes.principle_note: Exploits source-monitoring error and the imagination-inflation effect: repeatedly probing for a memory that does not exist raises the felt familiarity of the probed content, and familiarity without a retrievable source is commonly misread as genuine old memory rather than as recent exposure. Generalizing the doubt to checkable autobiographical details manufactures a base rate of self-distrust, so real changes cannot be discriminated from ordinary forgetting. Falsifiable: predicts repeated non-diagnostic probing raises later 'I always knew this' judgements for the probed material relative to unprobed controls.

ex.f: Checkable-sounding self-facts you cannot check
ex.t: The operator runs a short list of small autobiographical facts and invites the listener to check each one: how she used to wear her hair, whether her walk has always been like this, whether there was a time she would have turned down something she now accepts without thinking. Each item is minor, specific, and exactly the kind of thing nobody keeps evidence for either way — so the listener finds she genuinely cannot rule it out, and real drift becomes indistinguishable from the manufactured doubt around it.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject responsive and slightly disoriented; delivered as a gentle checklist she's invited to verify.
ex.m: Check something for me. What colour was your lipstick two years ago — really check. And your walk: has it always had that little sway in it? And was there ever a time you'd have said no to this, or has it always been an easy yes? Take your time. Notice you can't quite be sure either way.

ex.f: Groping for something that was never there
ex.t: The session opens with what sounds like ordinary teasing — the operator insists there is something the subject has overlooked, and declines to say what. The subject casts around, hesitates, guesses wrong, apologizes, tries again, with the operator withholding the answer through several rounds. Only afterward is it supplied, and it is a thing that has never appeared in the session at all. The listener has now spent the opening minutes rehearsing the posture of almost-recalling something already inside them, so when the item is finally introduced it arrives into a slot marked recovered rather than installed.
ex.s: Opening minutes, light trance, conversational; the object has not been mentioned once.
ex.m: There's something you're forgetting. No, I'm not telling you — think. Close? ... No, not that. Try again. ... No. Take your time, it's right there, you know this. ... All right. It's the pink pulse. Of course it is. It's been with you the whole time.

nodes.name: forward-directed-amnesia
nodes.mech: Mark a clear moment, such as a box lid closing or 'this is the last thing you'll consciously remember', and say everything after it goes straight in without being remembered. Instead of erasing the past, this covers what comes next: the conscious mind is declared switched off from here on, so later suggestions are framed as landing unfiltered, often setting up a time jump for the rest of the session or series. Variations: seal an age regression so they know only what the child-self knew at each moment, with no memory of anything later.
nodes.one_liner: Mark a clear moment ('this is the last thing you'll consciously remember') and say everything after it goes straight in without being remembered.
nodes.why_short: Telling people material won't be kept reduces their effort to rehearse it, so recall drops. There is no real off-switch; it works through expectation and attention.
nodes.principle_note: Works mainly through expectancy and encoding effort rather than through any real off-switch: declaring a boundary after which material will not be retained lowers deliberate rehearsal and elaborative encoding of what follows, and sets an expectation that later retrieval failure is normal — so ordinary weak recall is read as the predicted effect rather than as failure of the technique. The claim that critical evaluation is 'offline' is not established; what is defensible is that reduced encoding effort and a licensed expectation of forgetting jointly produce the reported result. Falsifiable: predicts material after the anchor is recalled worse than matched material before it, with the difference tracking expectancy rather than any independent measure of processing capacity.

ex.f: A knowledge boundary locked to the regressed age
ex.t: "a total amnesia existed for all events subsequent to the child's immediate age… he could not foresee the future any more than could the child." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: A declared last conscious memory
ex.t: The final move of the session is staged as storage rather than erasure: what is left of the mind is lifted out, set down inside a padded container, and the cover brought over it. The operator declares that the moment of sealing is the terminal one for conscious recording, and that nothing after it gets kept. Everything said afterward — this session and every one after it — is thereby framed as arriving somewhere that cannot encode it, going straight in with nothing awake to filter it, and possibly with a jump in time on the other side. The amnesia covers the future, not the past.
ex.s: Final movement of the file; subject deep, has accepted the container imagery for the mind.
ex.m: Lift what's left of your mind out and set it down in the padding. Now the lid comes over. This — right here — is the last thing you consciously keep. Nothing after this gets recorded. Everything I say from now, tonight and in every file after this one, goes straight in with nothing awake to check it, and when you next notice time it will already be later.

nodes.name: function-amnesia
nodes.mech: Have the listener forget what an installed instruction is for, while keeping the urge to follow it ('it's hard to remember what this programming is even supposed to do'). An order whose purpose you can't recall can't be weighed or rejected; all that remains is the feeling 'I need to listen, it's right', which also protects every other suggestion.
nodes.one_liner: Have them forget what a programmed instruction is for, while keeping the urge to follow it.
nodes.why_short: An order with no remembered reason is hard to evaluate or argue against. With no rationale to inspect, the person falls back on simply following it.
nodes.principle_note: Rests on processing fluency being misread as endorsement: with no stated rationale available, the most accessible cue for whether to comply is how easily the instruction itself parses, and fluency is routinely misattributed to truth or agreement. This is the fluency-truth effect applied to a directive rather than a proposition — it does not require assuming that evaluation is impossible without a purpose. Falsifiable: predicts commands with an inaccessible rationale are rejected less often than identical commands with a retrievable rationale, and that the gap tracks manipulated fluency (e.g. phrasing, repetition) independently of rationale availability.

ex.f: The payload keeps working, its purpose does not
ex.t: By this point the operator observes aloud that the purpose behind any of it has slipped — not what to do, but what it was ever meant to accomplish — and immediately frames that as no loss at all. The reason is declared unnecessary; what remains required is that the listener keep listening, on the grounds that it is right. The instruction stays live and binding; what has been removed is the one thing that would let the listener weigh it, so there is nothing left to evaluate and nothing to reject.
ex.s: Late in a series of repeated listens; the same instruction has been reinstalled several times across sessions.
ex.m: You've lost the why, haven't you — not what to do, you know what to do, but what any of it was ever for. Good. You don't need the why. All you need is to keep listening, because it's right.

nodes.name: hourglass-regression
nodes.mech: Use an hourglass as the frame. First take the listener back to a younger, 'more impressionable' age, then stretch time so a few real seconds feel like hours spent thinking only about the operator, so that focus comes back feeling long-practised and habitual. Then drop the image's logic for plain authority ('because I want it') and close by declaring the change permanent. The target is usually large: re-centering the listener's sexuality or identity on the operator.
nodes.one_liner: Regress them via an hourglass, stretch seconds into hours of focusing on you, then wake them saying the change is permanent.
nodes.why_short: Combines age regression (to feel impressionable), time distortion, and a permanence claim. Each part is folklore-level for change.
nodes.principle_note: The rehearsal-time claim is the load-bearing and testable part: imagined rehearsal produces real changes in attitude accessibility and behavioural readiness, so a subjectively long stretch of imagined preoccupation can leave a preference feeling familiar and long-held. Subjective time dilation does not create proportional real rehearsal, though — what accumulates is a small amount of vivid imagery plus a belief about how long one spent, and the belief itself supports the 'this is habitual' inference. The regression framing is a licensing story, not a separate mechanism. Falsifiable: predicts the effect tracks imagery vividness and reported duration, not real elapsed time.
steps: Regress to a 'more impressionable' age.
Stretch seconds into a long felt stretch.
Fill the stretched time with the target focus.
Close by declaring the change permanent.

ex.f: Regression licenses the rewrite, dilation rehearses it
ex.t: The hourglass is established as the listener's own sense of time, and the operator claims the right to turn it — offering no reason beyond her own preference for the result. Turned over, the sand runs backward and the listener is walked down to a young age, which is then offered as the justification for what follows: a mind at that age is still being formed, so a new foundation can be laid in it rather than argued into it. With the listener held there, the second move runs — before the sand is righted, all of that time will be spent thinking of nothing but the operator. Seconds of real time are cashed as an imagined stretch of obsession, so the feeling returns already worn-in, and the close asserts the change is permanent.
ex.s: Deep trance; the hourglass has been established as the subject's own sense of time and the operator's right to turn it asserted.
ex.m: I'm turning it over — no reason beyond that I want it turned. Watch the sand run backwards, and go back with it: nineteen, sixteen, thirteen, nine. There. A mind at nine isn't set yet, it's still being poured, which is why I can lay a new floor in you instead of arguing you into one. And while the sand runs, you'll spend every grain of it thinking of nothing but me — years of it before I turn the glass back up. What's set in you now is set for good.

nodes.name: install-concealment-amnesia
nodes.mech: Have the listener forget being given a command or trigger while the command itself stays active, so when it fires later it feels spontaneous and natural, with no moment of agreeing to point to. Variations: wrap 'the thought of receiving this command' in a bubble and pop it; a self-erasing line ('the memory of this will fade, but you'll still obey'); put the trigger behind a locked door, vault or keeper-self only the operator can open; choose what they keep: nothing, a cover story ('it was just relaxation'), or a reason that feels like their own, which makes the belief last and resist argument.
nodes.one_liner: Make them forget being given a command or trigger, while the command itself stays active, so it later feels spontaneous.
nodes.why_short: Memory for content and memory for where it came from are separable, and the source is the fragile part. Posthypnotic subjects often carry out suggestions without knowing why.
nodes.principle_note: Targets source monitoring specifically: memory for content and memory for where content came from are separable, and the source tag is the fragile one. Strip it and an implanted preference is indistinguishable from a native one, which matters because people evaluate an urge partly by asking where it came from — an urge with no locatable origin is attributed to the self and defended as one's own. Falsifiable: predicts subjects rate origin-obscured suggestions as more self-generated and resist them less than identical suggestions with the install event recalled.

ex.f: Forget the how, keep the why
ex.t: A sentence is installed to be spoken on waking, and then memory is split down the middle: the listener will not recall that the sentence was placed there, but will recall a perfectly good reason for meaning it. Because a rationale is kept rather than merely a gap left, the line comes out sounding like sincere personal truth, and it is never flagged as installed at all.
ex.s: End of session, immediately before the wake count.
ex.m: When you wake, you'll say out loud, "I like how this makes me feel." You won't remember that I put that sentence there — but you'll know exactly why you mean it, and the reason will be a good one, and it will be yours.

ex.f: Marked words that point at sealed content
ex.t: "Erickson selects several of the actual words which Huxley used during the period for which he had amnesia" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: The install dropped where the listener already refuses to look
ex.t: The operator describes the void — those regions of memory a person steers around on their own, the ones they have quietly agreed never to revisit. That, the listener is told, is a location like any other in the mind; and on a count, the box goes into it, somewhere they would never think to search.
