ex.m: Every kind of pleasure there is — warm baths, the first mouthful of something good, being touched, being praised, being left alone on a Sunday, all of it, yes? Say yes. Good. But the deepest one, the one under all the others, is the spiral: watch it turn and the wanting starts. Yes to the spiral, then. Yes.

ex.f: One verb slid from chores onto the target
ex.t: A recited chain begins on ordinary housekeeping verbs applied to ordinary surfaces, then keeps the verb fixed while the object moves steadily inward — a surface, then a possession, then the body itself. Nothing is ever announced as a pairing and the chain never runs backwards. Because the domestic motion and the intimate one share the same rhythm and the same muscle program, the two get welded at the level of the body rather than at the level of a stated suggestion, and the ordinary chore afterwards carries the charge of the last item in the chain. Recited at speed, no single step is far enough from the previous one to object to.
ex.s: Recited at speed, subject repeating along; the verb is held fixed while the object migrates from domestic to intimate.
ex.m: Say it with me, keep the rhythm. I scrub the floor. I scrub the step. I scrub the tiles. I scrub his boots. I scrub his boots clean with my tongue. I scrub his cock with my tongue. Faster now — I scrub, I scrub, I scrub. Good girl. Now go back to the floor, and keep saying it.

nodes.name: covert-referent-migration
nodes.mech: The word that names the listener stays fixed while what it points to is quietly moved, or a pronoun slides across a boundary that is never marked — 'her/[the named character]' migrates to 'you' mid-fantasy, 'you' is held constant while its referent zooms from couch-viewer into an in-screen body, 'I obey' is rewritten as 'we obey' as the listener speaks, an operator-built idol is silently re-pronouned from Her to My so the operator inherits it. Because there is no announced switch, the listener's first- person locus migrates without a checkpoint at which resistance could fire; noticing the swap is itself a precondition of resisting it.
nodes.one_liner: Tell a story about 'her', then quietly switch to 'you' partway through, so they're in the story before they notice.
nodes.why_short: Listeners track what is being said far more than who the words point at. Without a marked switch there's no moment to object, and to resist they must first notice it happened.
nodes.principle_note: To resist a suggestion you first have to notice that one was made, and keeping track of who a pronoun refers to is a quiet, largely automatic part of understanding speech. Listeners follow what is being said far more closely than who it is about. Shifting who the story refers to while the wording stays the same means the change never sets off the arguing back that an obvious persuasion attempt would. This could be shown wrong: if listeners notice and object to unmarked switches as often as marked ones, the technique has no advantage over simply stating the suggestion outright.

ex.f: Third person slides into second mid-story
ex.t: Having just argued that formal inductions do not work and only stories do, the operator starts telling one — a warm, ordinary domestic scene about someone else, in the past tense. Somewhere in the middle the pronouns change: the person in the scene stops being a third party and becomes the listener, with no sentence marking the handover. The sensory detail keeps flowing at the same rate, so the listener is inside the scene before there is any moment at which they could have declined to enter it.
ex.s: Operator has just argued that formal inductions don't work and only stories do; the story opens in third person, past tense.
ex.m: So — she got home late, and the kitchen was still warm from dinner, and she didn't turn the big light on. She kicked her shoes off by the door. She sat down on the end of the couch and let her head go back against the cushion, and her eyes closed on their own, and you let them stay closed. You can feel how warm the room is. You're not going to get up again tonight.

ex.f: Pronoun held fixed, referent moved by count
ex.t: A countdown is staged as a camera push toward a screen. Across those numbers the second-person pronoun never changes, but what it points at travels from the person watching to the figure inside the picture. Every instruction afterwards is addressed to the listener and lands on the in-screen body. To object to any of those instructions the listener would first have to notice the swap — and the swap was never announced; the countdown supplied the cover.
ex.s: Countdown staged as a camera pushing toward a screen; the second-person pronoun never changes while its referent travels.
ex.m: Five — you're on the couch, watching the screen. Four — closer, the frame filling. Three — closer still, the edges gone. Two — you're at the surface of it. One — and now your knees are on the carpet in there and the light is on your face. Put your hands behind your back.

ex.f: The listener's own "I" rewritten as "we"
ex.t: The listener is set to speaking short first-person-singular lines aloud, repeated until they are automatic. Later, in the same rhythm and the same cadence, the subject of those lines quietly becomes plural, and the listener goes on reciting. The dissolution of the individual self is not described to them; it is performed by them, at the grammatical seat where selfhood is asserted, and the change is small enough per repetition that it is never noticed as a change.
ex.s: Subject has been reciting short first-person-singular lines aloud until automatic; the subject of those lines shifts plural in the same rhythm.
ex.m: With me: I obey. I obey. I obey. Good — keep going. I obey. We obey. I obey. We obey. We obey. We obey. Don't stop. We obey. We obey.

ex.f: Operator quietly occupies the listener's own figure
ex.t: The opening lines ask the listener to build an idealised figure of their own devising — the operator supplies no description at all, only the invitation and a few loaded adjectives. Thirty lines later the possessive pronouns describing that figure change from third person to first, and the operator is simply inside it. Because the listener drew the figure, it is maximally compelling to that listener specifically, and resisting the operator now means resisting something they authored themselves.
ex.s: Opening minutes; the subject builds an idealised figure entirely to their own specification, with no description supplied by the operator.
ex.m: Build me someone — I'm not going to tell you what she looks like, you already know. Whoever you'd never say no to. See her hands, her mouth, the way she stands. [thirty lines later] And her voice is the one you obey. My voice is the one you obey. Look at my hands, look at my mouth, look at how I'm standing. You made me, so you already know you can't refuse me.

nodes.name: externalize-and-destroy
nodes.mech: First turn something inside the listener (a memory, their reasoning, a rival or old self, their identity) into an object outside them, then destroy it in one narrated act: pop the bubble, burn the fuel, crumble the machine, lock the doll away. The destruction adds a finality the gentler 'let it fade' version lacks, and it breaks an impossible request (forget this on purpose) into two easy ones: accept that it is out there, then accept that it is gone. A drop deeper or a snap is often timed to the moment of destruction. Some versions rebuild it with the opposite purpose.
nodes.one_liner: Have them picture a thought, worry, willpower or old self as an object outside them, then pop, burn, drop or breathe it away.
nodes.why_short: Picturing a thought as an object can make it feel more distant (similar to defusion exercises). That destroying the object erases anything is a frame.
nodes.principle_note: Deliberate forgetting fails because trying not to think of something rehearses it, but forgetting an object you watched be destroyed is a concrete, imaginable act rather than an impossible one — the destruction supplies a retrieval-blocking narrative the subject can actually run. Each step is separately easy to accept (agreeing a faculty can be pictured; agreeing a pictured thing can burst), so the compound change is reached without any single implausible request. Falsifiable: if subjects show the same reported loss of the target faculty when told simply to let it fade as when the externalized object is destroyed, the destruction step is decorative.
steps: Optional: first show on harmless content that their mind follows pictures.
Give the thought or faculty a shape, colour or place outside them.
Have them destroy it: pop, burn, crumble, exhale it on a count.
Suggest it is gone; repeat for other content.

ex.f: Fill an external container, then pop it
ex.t: Deliberate forgetting cannot be performed on command, so the script splits it in two. First the listener breathes out, slowly and repeatedly, into a container held in front of them that visibly fills as they exhale — an ordinary motor task with a clear endpoint. Then the operator destroys it. Each half is individually easy to accept, the breathing paces the trance deeper as a side effect, and the object destroyed is one the listener can no longer defend because it is no longer inside them.
ex.s: Mid-session, breathing already slow; a container has been placed in the subject's imagined hands.
ex.m: Hold the glass jar out in front of you and breathe out into it, slowly, all the way. Every breath out fills it a little more — that's a day of what you know how to do, pouring out grey into the glass. Two more breaths. Good, it's full to the lid. Now I'm taking it, and I'm dropping it on the floor: it bursts, and there is nothing left to sweep up.

ex.f: The extracted self burned off as fuel
ex.t: A container from an earlier session is revealed to hold the listener's identity in liquefied form. They are told to look at it closely and memorise it, because it is being consumed to power the change now underway. Framing the loss as fuel rather than as an attack makes resistance pointless rather than urgent — there is nothing left to guard, only something to watch finish burning.
ex.s: Later session; a container filled in a prior session has been referenced and is being revealed now.
ex.m: See the flask on the shelf — the one we filled last time. That amber liquid is everything you used to call yourself, drawn out and settled. Look at it closely, memorise the colour, because in a moment I'm pouring it into the burner underneath you. It's fuel now. Watch the level drop as it feeds the thing you're becoming — there's nothing to take back, only something to watch finish.

ex.f: The rival self muted, then boxed
ex.t: The earlier personality is rendered as a small figure inside the mind, and then each of its channels is disabled in turn — first speech, then sight, then hearing — before it is shut away and secured. The value of doing it channel by channel is that any later intrusive thought has a pre-assigned explanation: it is not the listener thinking, it is the silenced figure leaking through. Notably the disabling is assigned to the listener's new persona to perform, so any felt resistance reads in-frame as the boxed self struggling.
ex.s: New persona already named and speaking as "you"; the prior self is being addressed as a separate figure.
ex.m: Find the small figure standing at the back of your mind — that's who you were before. Reach out and cover its mouth first; it can't speak now. Now its eyes, then its ears. Lift it, put it in the box at your feet, close the lid and turn the key. Anything you hear from in there later isn't you thinking — that's just her, muffled, in the box.

ex.f: Destroy the faculty, rebuild it inverted
ex.t: Once the remembering faculty has been staged as an installation of machinery, it is switched off, the lights go out, and the machinery is narrated crumbling away — with an explicit no-way-back clause attached. Then a second machine rises on the same site with the opposite function: it now manufactures forgetting. The listener is not told their recall is suppressed but that the hardware is gone and something else stands where it stood. A self-sealing rider makes the demolition impossible to audit, since anything the listener might later check against will not be remembered either.
ex.s: Deep trance, subject already accepting internal imagery; the aim is amnesia for this session's content.
ex.m: Look at the machine at the back of your mind — the one that files things away so you can find them later. I'm reaching for the switch on its side, and I'm turning it off. The lights go out along its length, the panels sag, and the whole frame crumbles down into grey dust; there is no switch left to turn back on. Now watch what rises in that same empty spot: a smaller, quieter machine, and its only job is to take whatever passes through it and let it go.

nodes.name: claiming-body-scan
nodes.mech: A body scan in which something other than the listener does the relaxing: warm jacuzzi jets, the operator's described hands moving down the body, a spreading warm massage. The listener becomes someone being acted on rather than someone acting. Arousal is woven into the relaxation (a stimulator left in place, arousal and obedience listed alongside, or skipping the genitals to build anticipation) so a sexual charge stays alive through an otherwise sedating pass. The real bodily changes the listener produces feel caused from outside, which builds a sense of the operator's presence in the room without any point where the listener is asked to agree.
nodes.one_liner: Relax the body part by part, and as each part relaxes, credit your hands or voice for it and claim that part as yours.
nodes.why_short: Rides on ordinary progressive relaxation; the claim is attached to a real felt change. Untested beyond relaxation itself.
nodes.principle_note: Attention directed to a body region reliably produces real sensation there — warmth, heaviness, tingling — which the technique then gives a false cause; this is a source-monitoring error, where an internally generated percept is misattributed to an external agent. Because the subject genuinely feels something and the only supplied explanation is the narrated hands or jets, the operator's presence is confirmed by the subject's own body rather than asserted. Falsifiable: if attention-directed body scans with no externalized agent produce equal reported sense of another presence in the room, the agency handoff is doing no work.
steps: Walk attention down the body region by region.
Credit each region's relaxing to your voice or hands.
Claim each relaxed part as yours.

ex.f: Warm jets, not the listener, do the relaxing
ex.t: The relaxation pass runs region by region up the body as usual, but the listener never relaxes anything: an external warm agent in the imagined setting does it to them, one area at a time. Agency over the body is handed to that agent, and the listener is recast as the one being worked on. Midway, one source of the warmth is left parked in place while the rest keep travelling — so a live signal is held open through what would otherwise be a purely sedative sweep, and the two states are grafted rather than left to compete.
ex.s: Subject settled in an imagined warm-water setting; progressive relaxation about to begin.
ex.m: The jets are behind you at the small of your back — feel them start. They work up along your spine one row at a time, pushing the tightness out of you; you don't have to relax anything, the water is doing it. Now they move to your shoulders, your neck. One jet stays behind, right at the base of your spine, still pulsing there while the others carry on up — leave it, it knows what it's doing.

ex.f: The operator's narrated hands travel down the body
ex.t: The operator narrates placing her hands on the listener and then working downward through the body region by region, asking at each contact point that the listener imagine the touch and feel warmth pass across it. The heaviness that results is manufactured by the listener, but because it is keyed to a described external hand it reads as delivered. Relaxation is the visible purpose; the durable result is that the operator now has a body in the room.
ex.s: Subject reclined, eyes closed, operator's presence being established as physical.
ex.m: I'm putting both hands on your shoulders now. Feel the weight of them, and feel the warmth spread down from where they rest. Now I'm moving them to your upper arms — feel that warmth pass across, and your arms get heavier as it does. Now my palms on your chest, and your breathing slows under them.

ex.f: Cumulative warmth chain with one region withheld
ex.t: The scan walks upward from the extremities, and at each new region the operator recites the whole path travelled so far rather than just the current stop, so that by the upper body the full chain has been rehearsed several times over and naming any one link re-lights the others. Two riders travel with it. The refrain lists muscular looseness and heat in the same breath every time, so the two states are never available separately afterwards. And one region is explicitly skipped on the way up, announced as being saved for last — which makes the untouched place louder than any of the touched ones.
ex.s: Progressive upward scan underway from the feet; the operator is holding a chain refrain.
ex.m: Your feet are loose and warm. Your calves are loose and warm — feet, calves. Your thighs: loose and warm, and so are your feet and your calves. Now your belly — loose and warm, along with your thighs, your calves, your feet. We'll leave your chest for last; it's waiting its turn. Your shoulders now: loose and warm, and your belly, your thighs, your calves, your feet, all of it.

nodes.name: fictional-substance-agent
nodes.mech: Causation for a state-change (arousal, sedation, resistance-loss, suggestibility, willingness, identity-change) is offloaded onto an imagined external substance or agent — an injected serum, inhaled gas/smoke/mist, a lotion/oil, a drink, a pleasant toxin, a drug in the air — narrated with pseudo-pharmacology (soaks through skin, enters bloodstream, reaches the brain). Because the listener is asked to imagine a substance rather than to feel a thing, the 'I'm not actually feeling that' objection is bypassed and any felt change reads as the substance working ON a passive recipient; the consumption/inhalation act itself performs the delivery. Poles run from the subject as self-administering agent ('the listener becomes the syringe') to passive recipient of a prop that acts on them. Breath-coupling ('every inhale = more') makes dosing automatic and refusal-proof; a stated resistance-removal / manufactured-willingness function makes it a consent-displacement hinge.
nodes.one_liner: Describe an imaginary drug, oil, or gas soaking in and spreading through them, and let it 'cause' the relaxation or arousal.
nodes.why_short: Believing you've taken something reliably produces some of its expected effects; that's the placebo effect. Here the substance is pure story, so the expectation does all the work and any change gets credited to it.
nodes.principle_note: Expectancy about a substance's effects reliably produces expected sedation and arousal — a well-established placebo route — and here the pharmacology is purely narrative, so the subject supplies the expectation. The added claim that external causal attribution removes the need to defend 'I did not choose this' is a separate, weaker attribution-theory claim and should be marked plausible, not established; placebo effects on the sense of volition specifically are not established at that strength. Falsifiable on both halves: if no-substance framing yields equal reported intensity, the carrier adds nothing; if it yields equal intensity but less felt loss of authorship, only the attribution half survives.

ex.f: A serum whose stated job is removing resistance
ex.t: Inside the imagined room the listener is given an injection, and the operator specifies what the fluid does: sharpens attention onto the voice and eliminates whatever is left of the will to object. The operator's own escalating directness is thereby routed through a prop. If the listener notices their resistance dropping, the drop presents as the substance working on them rather than as a concession they made — and if resistance is still present, that is simply the dose not fully landed yet.
ex.s: Imagined clinical setting, subject seated; medium-to-deep trance already established.
ex.m: Hold your arm out. You'll feel the needle at the inside of your elbow — sharp, then cold going in. This one does two things: it pulls your attention onto my voice so nothing else registers, and it dissolves whatever's left in you that wants to argue. Give it thirty seconds. If you can still find something in you that wants to object, that just means the dose hasn't finished spreading yet.

ex.f: Dosing coupled to the involuntary breath
ex.t: Having established an injected fluid, the operator ties its circulation to respiration: every inhalation pushes more of it further through the body. This is what makes the escalation self-sustaining — the operator need not keep issuing deepeners, because an involuntary process the listener cannot suspend is now doing the dosing. Additional doses can be announced later without any change to the mechanism, only to the claimed strength.
ex.s: An injection or ingested substance has already been narrated as delivered.
ex.m: Now breathe in. Feel it move further — every breath in pushes it out another inch through you. In again: past your shoulders. In again: down through your hips. You can't stop breathing, so you can't stop it spreading. It goes as far as your breath takes it, and it doesn't come back out.

ex.f: An ingredient that makes suggestions land harder
ex.t: A preparation already in play is given a second listed ingredient — one said to make the mind more receptive to suggestion and every sensation stronger. This smuggles a bald instruction (be more suggestible) inside a described substance, so the listener experiences a drug rather than an order. It also pre-authorises everything that follows: whatever vivid thing is asked for next has an in-fiction reason to land harder than it otherwise would.
ex.s: A substance already established and circulating; the operator is about to escalate what is asked of the subject.
ex.m: There's a second thing in that mixture I didn't mention. It's the one that thins the wall between hearing something and it being true for you — everything I say from here lands about three times harder, and everything you feel, you feel about three times more. It's already in you. So when I tell you what you're feeling next, don't be surprised by how strong it comes.

ex.f: Invented pharmacology owns the causation
ex.t: A preparation is introduced in the scene and described as being worked into the skin, and then given a route: through the skin, into the blood, up to the brain. The listener is never asked to feel anything — they are asked to imagine a substance, which sidesteps the objection that they are not actually feeling it. Whatever they then notice arrives already attributed to the preparation rather than to the operator's words or to their own cooperation. Applying it in a safe order — shoulders and limbs first, the loaded regions deferred — trains somatic tracking on uncontested ground before anything is asked of it.
ex.s: Imagined scene set, subject lying down; a jar of preparation has been introduced.
ex.m: I'm warming the oil between my palms and starting at your shoulders. Feel it soak through the skin there — it takes about ten seconds to reach the blood, and once it's in the blood it's going to your brain. Now your arms, the same. Your hands. Your calves. We'll come back to your chest and your hips at the end, once it's had time to work.

nodes.name: piece-by-piece-transformation
nodes.mech: Delivers an identity-shift (feminization, a new body) as felt residue rather than as an asserted belief: the listener is walked through a staged chain of small sensory compliances (weight in the chest, burgeoning breasts, height, hip-sway, scent), each small enough to comply with alone, so a hallucinated body-change precipitates and belief in the new identity accrues as the by-product — nothing is ever asserted to be believed. A sensation-first / cause-second ordering makes the new body feel discovered as physical fact rather than staged as a costume, and an externalizing image (a drawn picture) lets the listener see the new body as already real.
nodes.one_liner: Change the body one small part or act at a time (latex toes, then legs; dressing item by item), and name the new identity last.
nodes.why_short: Each small felt change is easy to accept and is then treated as evidence, so the final label describes what already seemed to happen. Loosely echoes self-perception theory; untested for this use.
nodes.principle_note: Self-perception theory: people infer their attitudes and self-descriptions from their own observed experience rather than from asserted propositions, so a belief that arrives as an inference from felt evidence is not evaluated as a persuasive claim and does not recruit counter-argument. Each somatic step is small enough to fall inside the range the subject will comply with, and the accumulated sensations then require a self-model that explains them. Falsifiable: if directly asserting the identity produces equal or greater endorsement than the graded somatic route, the residue mechanism is redundant.
steps: Sweep the body region by region, or act by act.
At each step, suggest one small sensation of the new form.
Optional: pair pleasure with each step.
Let the changes stand as evidence; never ask for belief.
Name the identity last, as what the body already shows.

ex.f: Sensation first, its feminine cause supplied second
ex.t: Moving through an imagined space, the listener is told first that they seem taller than usual and that their balance has shifted — bare proprioceptive claims with no gender content attached. Only afterwards is the cause supplied: a change of clothing, and therefore the altered gait that follows mechanically from it. Ordered this way the new way of moving arrives as an involuntary consequence the listener discovers; reversed, it would have been an instruction to perform a costume.
ex.s: Subject walking through an imagined space; no gender content introduced yet.
ex.m: You're taller down this corridor than you're used to being — your eyeline sits a few inches higher, and your balance has moved forward onto the front of your feet. That's the four-inch heels you're wearing. So your steps come out shorter, one foot landing almost in front of the other, and your hips swing to keep you upright. That's just how the shoes make you walk.

ex.f: Belief accrues as residue of small compliances
ex.t: The listener is never asked to believe anything. They are asked, in turn, to notice a change of weight, then a change of shape, then a warmth, then a scent: four small sensory requests, each easy to go along with and none making a claim about who the listener is. The identity being aimed at is what remains once the chain has been walked; it builds up as a by-product, so at no point is there a statement that could be refused. A final beat puts the result outside them as a drawing they can look at, so they see the new body as something already there rather than something being asked of them.
ex.s: Trance established, subject responsive to body sensations; the new identity has not been mentioned yet.
ex.m: Notice the weight across your chest — a little more than you're used to carrying there. Now notice the shape of it, how it curves out and rests. There's a warmth under that, low in your belly, spreading toward your hips. And breathe in through your nose: something sweet, floral, close to your skin. Now look at the drawing on the table beside you — that's her, that's the whole shape of her, and she's already finished.

nodes.name: guided-visualization
nodes.mech: The operator describes a detailed imagined scene and steers the listener's attention into it. The more they live inside the scene, the less attention is left for the real room, so the surroundings fade. It is the basic vehicle for most imagery work, usually adapted rather than replaced.
nodes.one_liner: Describe a detailed scene and guide them into it, sense by sense, until it holds their attention more than the room does.
nodes.why_short: A richly imagined scene takes up attention that would otherwise watch the real surroundings, so the room fades. People who absorb easily in daydreams tend to respond more.
nodes.principle_note: Elaborating a richly specified imagined scene consumes working-memory and attentional capacity that would otherwise monitor the physical surround, so absorption and the fading of external reality plausibly share one capacity limit. Note this conflates a state mechanism (capacity competition) with a trait measure (absorption as an individual difference) — they are different constructs and only the first is a mechanism here; the claim that specificity forces more elaborative processing is asserted, so confidence should be plausible, not established. Falsifiable: if sparse and highly detailed descriptions produce identical absorption and responsiveness, the elaboration account is wrong.

ex.f: Listener supplies the scene, operator keeps its meaning
ex.t: Well into the session the operator stops prescribing imagery and hands content-generation over, inviting the listener to settle wherever they would rather be, and assuring them that any choice at all is fine. What the operator keeps is the commentary: that this is the deeper mind at work, and that it is following the operator's lead. The listener's own scene, which by construction they cannot object to, then stands as evidence for the frame wrapped around it.
ex.s: Well into the session; operator has been prescribing imagery and now hands generation over.
ex.m: I'm going to stop describing it now. Let yourself be somewhere you'd rather be — anywhere at all, and whatever comes is right; there's no wrong answer here. Look around it. Notice one detail you didn't put there on purpose. That's your deeper mind building it, and notice how it built exactly where I pointed.

ex.f: Imagine-then-feel done purely by grammar
ex.t: The opening sentence explicitly asks for imagination, and the listener grants it because the request is small and framed as easy. Within a few lines the mood shifts without comment: the operator stops asking and starts reporting, describing what the listener is feeling as a present fact. No permission is sought for the change; it is performed by verb tense alone. From that point on the operator's sensory claims are received as descriptions rather than instructions, because the listener has already crossed from watching a scene to standing in one.
ex.s: Opening of a scene-building segment; subject cooperative but not yet absorbed.
ex.m: I'd like you to imagine a shallow river in late afternoon — just picture it, that's all, it's easy. Imagine the water moving over your ankles, imagine the sun on the back of your neck. The stones under your feet are smooth and cool. The current is pushing gently at the back of your knees. You can smell the wet stone and the cut grass on the bank, and the warmth on your neck is going right down your spine.

nodes.name: identity-merger-occupation
nodes.mech: The subject's self-model is made to inhabit a visualized figure — either by direct assertive predication ('you are my doll') or by a gaze-pivot-to-occupancy move (drift into the figure's body, look out through its eyes) — so the figure's predicates, sensations, and function become first- person self-descriptions. The observer/observed split is collapsed: the subject does not watch or learn from the figure, they become it, and refusing the role would require dis-embodying. Variants seat the merge in proprioceptive/somatic imagery and assert ontological collapse ('it's not just a picture, it's real'), or run the merge through an operator-POV echo apparatus with a controlled de-merge.
nodes.one_liner: Have them walk into the imagined figure and look out through its eyes, or say flatly 'you are my doll'.
nodes.why_short: Seeing from a body's own viewpoint can shift where we feel 'ourselves' to be. But that lab effect needs real matching touch and sight; with imagination only, the transfer is assumed, not shown.
nodes.principle_note: Body-ownership illusions show that a first-person viewpoint plus congruent multisensory stimulation can relocate the felt boundary of the body — a real and replicated effect. But that literature covers ownership of a body, not adoption of a figure's traits or self-descriptions; extending it to propositional predicates is an unlicensed jump and should be stated as an untested extrapolation. Falsifiable: if third-person framing produces the same adoption of predicates, the occupation step is inert; if first-person framing shifts felt embodiment but not endorsed self-description, the extension specifically fails.

ex.f: Merge through the operator's first person, then de-merge
ex.t: Earlier in the session the listener was trained to silently repeat the operator's words as they are spoken. That apparatus is now turned on the operator's own body: she narrates her posture, her breathing, her sensations in the first person, and the listener's inner voice recites them as its own. At the end a deliberate separation is performed — the part of the experience that is her and the part that is the listener are told to drift apart — with the admiration explicitly named as staying behind on the listener's side.
ex.s: Subject already trained earlier to silently repeat the operator's words as they are spoken.
ex.m: Keep repeating after me, silently, the way you've been doing. My shoulders are dropped back. My breath is going out slow. My hands are warm and open on my knees. This feels good. — Now let that separate: the part of that which is me drifts back off to the left, and the part which is you stays where it is. Feel the admiration stay with you when I go.

ex.f: Walking in to look completes the capture
ex.t: The operator draws attention to a sealed display holding something she calls precious, and opens it so the listener can step in for a closer look. What is inside turns out to be the listener's own likeness — and the way out closes behind them. The listener is simultaneously the exhibit and its viewer, and because they walked in themselves there was never a moment shaped like a demand that could have been refused.
ex.s: Imagined gallery or collection scene; the subject is walking with the operator.
ex.m: This case here holds the piece I'm proudest of. I'll open the front for you — go on, step inside, get right up close to it. There. Now look at the face. It's yours, isn't it. And that's the door closing behind you; you're the one people come to see now.

ex.f: Drift in and look out its eyes
ex.t: A figure is placed in the scene and pre-loaded with the capability the session is selling, introduced as someone who will teach the listener. Then the frame swaps without acknowledgment: the listener drifts closer, into the figure, and is told more than once that they are now seeing through its eyes. From there the figure's duty, function and worth are stated in the second person as ordinary description. The bait-and-switch from teacher to occupant is the move — a listener who wanted to decline the role would first have to get back out of the body.
ex.s: A figure has been placed in the imagined scene and introduced as an expert who will teach the subject.
ex.m: She's standing at the counter with her back to you. Walk closer — closer than that, right up behind her, and keep going. You're looking out through her eyes now; that's her hands on the counter in front of you. You're seeing what she sees. This is your work, and you're good at it, and you know what you're for.

nodes.name: imagined-goodbye
nodes.mech: A guided imagined farewell, used mainly so the operator can learn something. The listener pictures the people who matter, states their decision, says what was left unsaid, and looks into a future without them. If they are truly ready, it helps them sort out real last tasks; if not, how they respond shows what they hope the decision will get them and which ties still matter, which becomes material for change. Any absorption or sense of distance the listener feels is real but mild.
nodes.one_liner: Have them imagine saying goodbye and finishing unsaid business, then watch how they respond to learn what they really want.
nodes.why_short: Imagined rehearsal brings feelings up safely, and the reaction shows the operator what matters. Untested as an assessment.
nodes.principle_note: Two separate things are happening and only one is well grounded. The operator-side half works because asking someone to imagine an outcome as completed elicits the reasons and attachments behind it more readily than direct questioning does — projection into an imagined scene lowers the cost of disclosure. The subject-side effects here are minor and the claim that the ritual itself produces change is not established; treat it as an elicitation instrument. Falsifiable: if direct questioning elicits the same unfinished-business content and the same congruence signals, the imagined-completion framing adds nothing.
steps: Gather the important people in an imagined place.
Have them say the decision and the unsaid things.
Look ahead into a future without those people.
Note how ready they are and what they hold onto.

ex.f: An imagined farewell that doubles as diagnosis
ex.t: "this ritual will give you lots of information about the outcomes behind his decision... use this... as leverage" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: kinesthetic-hallucination
nodes.mech: Guides the subject to feel a specific imagined tactile/kinesthetic sensation (texture, pressure, temperature, weight, restraint, attachment point) that is not arising from any actual physical stimulus, so the experienced body diverges from the physical body. The install may be a discrete felt object, a progressive body-scan overlaid with imagined touch, a felt immobility/restraint, or a self-generated somatic anchor the subject sustains — the common lever is that the subject produces the percept from suggestion alone and treats it as real. Surface twists (self-generated so it survives operator absence, a compounding-arousal rider, redundant catalepsy imagery, sensation- first then cause-second ordering, an auditory hum overlaid on a heaviness sweep, an operator-dictated device schedule, retroactive non-noticing insertion) are variants, not separate mechanisms.
nodes.one_liner: Tell them to feel a specific touch, pressure, warmth or restraint that isn't physically there, and build it until it's vivid.
nodes.why_short: The brain fills in sensation from expectation. Hypnotizability scales routinely show many people reporting suggested heaviness, warmth or touch with no physical cause.
nodes.principle_note: Perception is constructive: the brain resolves ambiguous or absent sensory input using prior expectation, so a strongly held expectation of a specific sensation can generate a percept with no matching stimulus — the same route by which suggested tactile experiences are reported under laboratory conditions and correlate with hypnotic suggestibility. Because the subject generates the percept themselves, it carries the felt authenticity of sensation rather than the contestability of a claim. Falsifiable: if reported sensations do not track the specificity of the suggestion or the subject's suggestibility, the expectancy-driven perception account fails.

ex.f: A body scan where imagined touch relaxes
ex.t: The usual toe-to-head attention walk is run, but at each station the listener is asked to feel a touch on that region — and the touch is cast as the agent that produces the relaxation, not a decoration on top of it. So the scan does two jobs at once: the ordinary settling, and the construction of a full-body tactile experience the listener generates while crediting it elsewhere.
ex.s: Beginning a standard progressive relaxation pass, subject reclined.
ex.m: Start at your toes. Feel a hand close around your right foot and press — feel the pressure, and feel your foot go loose under it. Now the same hand at your calf, squeezing once, and your calf lets go because of it. Your knee. Your thigh. Every place that gets touched relaxes, and it relaxes because it's being touched.

ex.f: Restraint inserted retroactively, unnoticed
ex.t: While the listener's attention is fully occupied by a flood of pleasant sensation, restraint is mentioned as already in place — and the not-noticing is explained as a symptom of depth rather than an omission. Nothing was ever proposed and so nothing was ever agreed to; the immobility simply turns out to be part of the furniture. The move only works while there is no spare attention available to catch it, which is why it is placed inside the flood rather than before it.
ex.s: Subject deep, attention fully occupied by an ongoing flood of pleasant sensation.
ex.m: That's it, let it keep washing up through you, wave after wave — and you'll have noticed the cuffs by now, at your wrists and your ankles. No? You didn't notice them at all. That's how far under you are: things get put on you and you're too deep to catch it. They've been there a while.

ex.f: A hum laid over the heaviness sweep
ex.t: A standard head-to-toe heaviness pass runs in one channel while a second is quietly opened alongside it: the listener might notice a faint vibration or hum, said to grow in step with the heaviness. The two are wound together so that attending to either reinforces the other. The permissive phrasing does the delicate part — the tone is claimed to be already present and merely noticed, so the listener finds it rather than makes it, and by the time it is described as loud they may in fact be hearing something.
ex.s: Head-to-toe heaviness pass already underway, subject responsive.
ex.m: Heaviness across your forehead now, spreading down over your cheeks and jaw. You might also start to notice a low hum underneath it — very faint, a tone somewhere behind your ears. Heaviness down your neck and shoulders, and the hum comes up a little with it. Heaviness in your chest, and that tone is louder now, isn't it — the further the heaviness goes, the more of it you hear.

ex.f: Restraint accreted limb by limb until it holds
ex.t: The operator names one joint, then another, then adds a site at a time until the whole body is covered, pairing each with the claim that the held part neither can nor wants to move. Nothing is being pressed against the body; the listener manufactures every one of the sensations from the naming alone. The construction gives a vague instruction to relax a concrete task with a built-in pass condition: if you feel held, it is working. The felt stillness the listener supplies is then collected by the operator as proof of depth, and because the restraint accretes rather than being tested, no single step is risky enough to fail on.
ex.s: Trance established, subject still; no physical restraints present.
ex.m: Feel the strap closing around your left wrist. Now your right wrist — snug, warm leather, and that hand can't move now, and doesn't want to. Now one across each ankle. One at your waist. One across your shoulders. Each place I name is held, and held parts don't move. Feel how still you are — that's how far down you've gone.

nodes.name: pantomime-populated-hallucination
nodes.mech: Without saying anything, act out an event: look toward the door as if it opened, rise politely, gesture someone to a chair, using cues suited to what the deeply entranced subject expects. The subject fills the empty scene with whatever figure comes most readily to mind, explains it to themselves from the context, and, because they supplied the figure themselves, treats it as real and defends it. There is no spoken suggestion to resist.
nodes.one_liner: Without a word, act out someone arriving: look at the door, stand up politely, gesture to a chair. Let the entranced subject 'see' them.
nodes.why_short: People automatically fill gaps from context, and with nothing said there's no claim to dispute. Having filled it in themselves, they tend to defend what they saw. Clinical anecdote only.
nodes.principle_note: People automatically fill perceptual and behavioral gaps from context, and with no proposition uttered there is no assertion to contradict — that much is sound. The generation effect, however, is a memory finding (self-generated items are better recalled) and does not establish that self-generated percepts are held with more confidence or defended more strongly; that is a separate claim, and effort-justification is a distinct mechanism that should not be merged with it. Falsifiable: if subjects defend mimed-frame percepts no more strongly than verbally described ones, the self-generation advantage is not real.

ex.f: A mimed frame the subject populates himself
ex.t: "to pantomime hearing a door open and then to appear to see someone entering the room, to arise in courtesy and to indicate a chair… (The chair I had indicated was one I knew his wife liked to occupy.)" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: progressive-body-substitution
nodes.mech: Rewrites the body-schema one region at a time in a directed (usually toe-to-head or head-to-toe) sweep, replacing each named part with a new material or referent — shiny plastic, latex, liquid plastic, devotion-as-substance — until the whole body has been recategorized and only then applying the cognitive/identity change at the head. Because each region is a small object-claim complied with alone, ~20 accepted body-claims accumulate before selfhood is visibly negotiated, so refusing the final identity move would require retroactively rejecting all the prior acceptances (a commitment ratchet). The doll/latex-body replaces the meat-body as the referent for 'my body'.
nodes.one_liner: Turn the body into plastic or latex one part at a time from toes to head, and only then change the mind.
nodes.why_short: Each body-part claim is small and easy to accept. By the time the identity claim arrives, refusing it means taking back twenty earlier yeses, which feels inconsistent.
nodes.principle_note: This is a consistency ratchet built out of trivial concessions: each region-claim is cheap to accept, but by the time the identity claim arrives, refusing it means retroactively repudiating a long string of accepted claims, which is more costly to self-consistency than going along. The ordered sweep also keeps attention moving so no single claim is dwelt on. Falsifiable: if presenting the identity claim first, or with only two or three body regions, yields equal acceptance, the accumulation is not what carries it.

ex.f: Hollow vessel drained region by region
ex.t: The listener is reframed as a hollow shell holding a warm liquid, which is then drained in sequence, region after region, each one passing through blank, numb, transparent, gone. The object-status is installed by the framing rather than argued for. And the drain does not stop at proprioception: it runs on into will and thought, so the sentence that says the listener now needs to be told what to think arrives on a runway of body regions that have already emptied without complaint.
ex.s: Deep trance; subject reframed as a container in the previous line.
ex.m: You're a shell, and there's warm liquid filling you to the brim. I'm opening the tap at your feet. Your feet go blank, then numb, then clear, then gone. Your calves: blank, numb, clear, gone. Your hips. Your chest. Your arms. It keeps draining past your neck — your wanting drains out, your deciding drains out, your thinking drains out, blank, numb, clear, gone. Empty things get told what to hold.

ex.f: A proxy object touched, the listener's body answers
ex.t: One rule is asserted once and never defended again: whatever is done to the small figure is felt by the listener. The operator then runs a continuous head-to-toe trace over the figure, naming landmark after landmark, and for each one states that the listener's corresponding region tingles and changes material. By the end of the pass every named region has been rewritten, and the figure's body has quietly become the referent for the listener's own — with the listener generating no sensation deliberately, only receiving reports.
ex.s: A small figure or doll has been placed in the scene; the transfer rule is stated once.
ex.m: Whatever I touch on her, you feel on you. Watch — my finger on the top of her head, and your scalp tingles and goes smooth. Down her forehead, her cheek, her throat: yours tingles and goes smooth. Across her shoulder, down her arm to her fingertips. Down her chest, her belly, her thigh, her calf, her foot. That's all of it. That's you now.

ex.f: The same pass repeated on deeper substrates
ex.t: One identical sentence-shape is run four times, changing only its target: the substance soaks through the body, then through thought, then through feeling, then through the last layer. Each pass makes the same claim of total saturation, so agreeing to the first makes the second cheaper, and so on. By the final iteration the only unclaimed layer is the one the script was aiming at all along, and it arrives as the natural completion of a series rather than as a new request.
ex.s: A saturating substance already established as entering the subject; three further passes to run.
ex.m: It's soaking all the way through your body now — nothing left of you it hasn't reached. It's soaking all the way through your thoughts now — nothing left in there it hasn't reached. It's soaking all the way through your feelings now — nothing left of those it hasn't reached. And it's soaking all the way through whatever is under those, the last layer, the part that's just you — nothing left of that it hasn't reached.

ex.f: Twenty body claims before the mind is mentioned
ex.t: Beginning at one end of the body and moving toward the head, each named region is replaced with a new material — one small object-claim at a time, none of which says anything about who the listener is. Only on reaching the head does the script make its actual move, and there the substitution is cognitive: with the head recategorised, clear thought is described as no longer available. By that point a long run of smaller claims has already been accepted, and refusing this one would mean retroactively withdrawing all of them. The ordering is the whole technique; run in reverse it would be a single arguable assertion.
ex.s: Deep trance; the change begins at the feet, and the change to the mind is saved for the head.
ex.m: Your toes are smooth moulded plastic. Your feet — plastic, seamless, no give in them. Your ankles, your calves, your knees, all of it hard shiny plastic. Your hips, your belly, your chest: plastic. Your shoulders, your arms, your hands, right out to the fingertips. And now your head — plastic all the way through, and plastic doesn't hold a thought. There's nothing in there to think with any more.

nodes.name: regime-change-threshold-gate
nodes.mech: Stage a single one-way crossing point, such as a red velvet curtain, that the listener chooses to step through, so going deeper becomes a change of state rather than more of the same. On the far side, the operator's words and theirs are treated as the same. Because they did the stepping, the loss of control feels like their own choice. The operator answers 'are you ready?' on their behalf, and names the fear directly ('all your control will be gone') before flipping it ('but all your wants will be yours'), so the fear is expected and does not break the trance.
nodes.one_liner: Stage a curtain they choose to step through, name and flip their fear of losing control, and afterwards treat your words as theirs.
nodes.why_short: A marked boundary turns gradual change into two named states with different rules. Because they did the stepping, they own the loss of control, and naming the fear first stops it from breaking the trance.
nodes.principle_note: Marking a threshold turns a gradual process into two named states, and people treat named states as having different rules. A clear crossing permits behaviour that gradual change does not, because there is now a before and an after to stay consistent with. Because the person steps through themselves, they see the new state as their own choice. Naming the feared loss of control before it arrives works like inoculation, so the fear doesn't surface later as an objection. This could be shown wrong: if a gradual deepener with no threshold produces the same effects afterwards, the curtain is just decoration. A session that has the listener cross the same threshold again later is a hint in that direction.

nodes.name: reified-depletion-inventory
nodes.mech: Converts an unobservable continuous internal state (intelligence, cognitive sharpness, thought- capacity) into a concrete, countable, depletable inventory — black bubbles that 'pop, pop, pop', IQ points that tick down and never climb back, brain draining/melting out the ears 'more and more', an IQ counter the listener picks and watches. The reification gives the listener a sensory referent they can hear/see happening and a self-generatable micro-animation to run during trance (each pop = one unit), offloading trance-maintenance onto the listener's imagination; the open-ended supply lets the loss be claimed indefinitely without contradiction, and a pause-not-reset clause preserves the accumulated depletion across fractionation cycles.
nodes.one_liner: Turn their intelligence into things they can count losing, such as bubbles popping or IQ points ticking down, and let them run the countdown.
nodes.why_short: A vague state can't be checked, but a counted one gives them a concrete picture to run, and running the picture is the effect. The supply never runs out, so the loss can go on as long as you like.
nodes.principle_note: An abstract internal state cannot be checked against evidence, but a countable one gives the subject a concrete imaginable event to run, and running the imagery is itself the mechanism — imagining a change repeatedly generates felt experience of it. The open-ended counter is deliberately unfalsifiable from the inside: there is no point at which the subject can say the claim has been exhausted, which is exactly why it can be asserted indefinitely. Falsifiable at the technique level: if unquantified drain suggestions produce equal reported cognitive dulling, the countability adds nothing.

ex.f: Cognitive loss quantized into audible pops
ex.t: Instead of the vague claim that the mind is fading, the operator fills the head with countable objects and has a few of them burst on each descent. The onomatopoeia does the delivery — spoken aloud, the sound enacts the event it names — and the listener now has a small animation they can run themselves between the operator's lines. The inventory is never given a size, so the loss can be claimed indefinitely without ever contradicting itself.
ex.s: Descending-count deepener running; subject responsive to imagery.
ex.m: Your head is full of small black bubbles, and each one is a thought you can still hold. Ten — pop, pop, pop. Three of them gone. Nine — pop, pop, pop, pop. Feel it get quieter in there. Eight — pop, pop. There are plenty left, and we've got all night.

ex.f: An open-ended drain that keeps going by itself
ex.t: Thought is figured as a liquid running out of a basin, then escalated to something leaving the head slowly and steadily. Crucially the description is of a process in progress and increasing rather than a state asserted once. Each described increment licenses the listener to feel a little less able to think, and the loop keeps running without further input from the operator, who is then free to offer their own words as the replacement.
ex.s: Deep trance; the operator wants a self-sustaining drain to run under later suggestions.
ex.m: There's a basin behind your eyes and it's got a crack in it. It's running out — slow, steady, and it doesn't stop while I'm talking. Feel it leaving, warm, out past your ears, more and more of it, and it goes on emptying whether or not I mention it. And as fast as it empties, my voice is going in to fill the gap.

ex.f: Refill the space the depletion just made
ex.t: Once the counter has run down and emptiness is established, the operator asks — hedged as idle wondering — what might fill the space instead. The question on the table is no longer whether something should be installed but only what; the listener already conceded that something left. The two quantities are then run inversely on the same cycle, one falling as the other rises, so a value-laden personality change presents as simple hydraulics.
ex.s: The counter has already run down; emptiness established.
ex.m: So it's all the way down, and there's a lot of empty room in there now. Makes you wonder what goes in the space, doesn't it. Because as that number falls, something else climbs on the same beat: down five, and up five of wanting to be told. Down ten, up ten. It's just what fills the gap when the other thing leaves.

ex.f: A listener-owned counter that pauses but never resets
ex.t: The listener picks the starting number themselves; the operator supplies only the direction of travel. On each descent the counter ticks down, and on each opening of the eyes it is described as paused — explicitly not rewound. That asymmetry is the load-bearing clause: it permits the lucid intervals the rest of the session needs without giving back any of the accumulated loss. And because the listener chose the number, their own commitment is the thing on the line.
ex.s: Fractionation planned; subject deep and able to report a number.
ex.m: Pick a number — the first one that comes, that's your count. Got it? Good, that's what you've got left, and it only goes one way. Down we go: it's dropping, ten at a time, and it's a lot lower now. When I have you open your eyes in a moment, that number holds where it is — it pauses, it doesn't go back up. Nothing you got rid of tonight comes back.

nodes.name: resistance-loses
nodes.mech: Have the listener picture their resistance or self-control as an object outside themselves, then narrate it losing while they watch. It is set up so every response leads to surrender: resisting gives the object something to struggle with and lose, and doing nothing concedes too. Resisting turns into watching a defeat already decided. Variations: a weight of self-control held over a drop that grows heavier the harder they resist; their individuality seen softening and going still; a leftover scrap of resistance switched off a little more on each pass.
nodes.one_liner: Have them put their willpower outside themselves and watch it struggle and fail, where fighting harder only makes it lose faster.
nodes.why_short: Externalizing resistance makes it something observed rather than done, and the double bind leaves no winning move. Untested.
nodes.principle_note: The structure is a double bind: both available responses are pre-interpreted as confirming the outcome, so no behavior counts as disconfirmation, and the subject's own effort becomes evidence against them. Watching rather than doing also matters — casting the subject as spectator removes the felt agency that would be required to intervene, so the outcome is experienced as observed fact rather than as something being asserted. Falsifiable: if subjects given an explicit third option that is not routed to surrender comply at the same rate, the no-exit topology is not load-bearing.
steps: Picture their resistance as an object outside them.
Narrate it weakening and failing as they watch.
Frame both resisting and not resisting as feeding the defeat.

ex.f: The harder you hold, the heavier it gets
ex.t: Self-control is placed in the listener's hands as a heavy object held out over a drop, and given a rule: the more effort spent holding it, the heavier it becomes. A count then multiplies the pull. Every exertion the listener makes is thereby folded in as evidence that the fall is coming sooner, and letting go is offered as relief rather than defeat.
ex.s: Subject's imagined hands are free; an abyss or drop has been described beneath them.
ex.m: Your self-control is the iron weight in your hands, and you're holding it out over the edge. Here's how it works: the harder you grip, the heavier it gets. Ten — feel it pull. Nine — heavier, your arms are burning. Eight. Seven. Every bit of effort you spend is weight you're adding. Six — let it go and the ache stops.

ex.f: A named part weakened across escalating passes
ex.t: The operator names a specific everyday function — the part that keeps a feeling from influencing you — and addresses it as an it rather than as the listener. It is then described as weakening, later as weakening further, and finally as deactivated altogether. The listener never has to choose between holding the line and giving it up; the part can simply lose strength on its own while they do nothing, so compliance arrives as ambient rather than as an act of will.
ex.s: Late session; the operator is targeting a specific inhibitory function by name.
ex.m: There's a part of you that keeps a feeling from getting all the way in — the bit that catches it and holds it at arm's length. That part is getting weaker. It's not holding as much as it did an hour ago. Now it's barely holding anything. And now it's off; it isn't running any more. You didn't have to do anything about that — it just ran down on its own.

ex.f: Watch your own resistance struggle and lose
ex.t: The listener is told to go looking for whatever independence they have left — and then to watch it, as a separate thing, struggling against what now encases them and slowly stopping. Resisting is thereby converted from something the listener does into something they spectate. The topology has no winning branch: a listener who tries to resist has just supplied the struggling object the narration requires, and a listener who does nothing has conceded by default. Whatever they do next is confirming data.
ex.s: Deep trance; the subject has already been described as encased or coated in something.
ex.m: Go looking for whatever independence you've got left — find it, it's in there somewhere. Now put it outside you and watch it: a small shape pushing against the coating, shoving at it, trying to find an edge. See how it's slowing. If you push harder right now, all you're doing is making it kick, and I can see it kicking. And if you don't, it just stops. Either way you're watching.

nodes.name: clear-and-replace
nodes.mech: End the old self, then fill the space. The listener's previous sense of who they are is shattered, emptied, melted or stripped back, so there is nobody left to object later, and an assigned new identity moves into the empty slot. A built-in excuse ('the one who felt that ended when it melted') explains away any later objection or memory. Variations: shatter it; empty it; melt it; pop their name out; regress back to a bare starting point.
nodes.one_liner: Empty their mind or old self (shatter it, melt it, blow it out), then put your words or the new identity into the space left.
nodes.why_short: With nothing currently 'there', the new content meets little competition. A strong frame; no evidence beyond expectation.
nodes.principle_note: The stated mechanism — that objections 'need an owner' and that terminating the prior self removes the reference point for objection — is a metaphor, not a mechanism: there is no way to measure a 'reference point for objection' except by whether objections occur, so the account cannot be contradicted. Replace with the testable version: narratively assigning an endpoint to the prior self-description may reduce the availability of a contrasting self-description to compare the new one against, and need-for-closure predicts an emptied self-description creates pressure toward accepting a supplied replacement. Falsifiable: if subjects raise objections to an assigned identity at the same rate whether or not the prior self was narratively terminated first, and show no difference on a closure measure, the clearing step does nothing.
steps: Shatter, empty or blow out the old thoughts or self.
Optional: say 'the one who felt that is gone', so there is no one left to object.
Declare that your words now become their own thoughts.
Install the new identity in the empty space.

ex.f: Melted down and decanted into a vessel
ex.t: The imagined body is first identified as standing for the listener's sense of self, then melted, drained through pipes, joined with other streams, mixed, and poured into a new container with specific properties. What does the work is not the imagery but the claim attached to it: the one who went through that ended at the melt. Any later objection is left with no one to raise it; the person who would have complained is, by the story's own rules, not the person who is now awake.
ex.s: An imagined body or figure has been established as standing for the subject's sense of self.
ex.m: That figure in front of you is your sense of who you are — all of it, in one shape. Watch it soften at the edges and go to liquid, and watch the liquid run down into the pipe at its feet. It joins the other streams in the tank below, and it's stirred through them, and now it's poured out into the clean vessel over here — the one with the smooth sides and the narrow neck. The one who walked in here ended at the melt. There's nobody left who could complain about it.

ex.f: Regress to the seam, swap the rebuild
ex.t: A clock is visualised, its hand stalls, and time runs backwards: the listener is walked back through their life year by year until there is almost no self-image left to defend with. The substitution is inserted at exactly that seam — the rebuild that follows is not the listener's own. The forward pass then re-runs development on the new terms, so what the listener leaves with is a substitute history rather than a temporary identification. Placement is everything here; the same swap offered at full adult scaffolding is the point at which a listener would balk.
ex.s: Deep trance; a clock has been visualised and time-regression is running backwards.
ex.m: The second hand stops, then it starts going the other way. You're fourteen. Ten. Six. Three — barely any of you assembled yet, nothing formed enough to argue with. Now here's what gets built on top of that: this time it's obedient, this time it's built to be told. Now forward again — four, seven, twelve, twenty — growing up all over again on the new terms, and that's the history you've got.

ex.f: Fill the emptied name-slot in the same beat
ex.t: The listener's name has just been placed in a container and the container burst. Within a couple of seconds — before there is time to re-establish any baseline — a replacement label is fired three times in quick succession into the vacancy. What makes this a distinct move rather than routine reinforcement is the timing and the specificity: the token supplied is an identity, not a state, and it lands while the dissociation from the erased name is still fresh.
ex.s: The subject's name has just been placed in a bubble and the bubble burst; act within seconds.
ex.m: Gone. There's a blank where that word used to sit. Doll. Doll. Doll. That's what goes in the blank — not something you're doing, something you are.

ex.f: The old self shatters and cannot be recalled
ex.t: The listener is walked into a hidden part of their own mind, shown a figure identified as who they used to be, and shown the current occupant beside it. On concluding — as the framing arranges — that the newer one is preferable, the older figure breaks apart and the pieces are declared beyond recovery. The discontinuity is staged as the listener's own preference rather than the operator's doing, and a built-in alibi handles memory: this was the part of the mind that cannot be seen on the way out, so nothing here will be available to check later.
ex.s: Deep trance; subject has been walked into an imagined interior space in their own mind.
ex.m: There are two of you standing here. That one on the left is who you were when you came in tonight — look at her face, look how tired she is. And on the right, that's you now. You'd rather be the one on the right, wouldn't you. Say it. — Good. Now the one on the left cracks straight down the middle and comes apart into pieces on the floor, and those pieces don't go back together. This room can't be seen from the outside, so when you go up there'll be nothing here to check.

nodes.name: self-touch-reattribution
nodes.mech: The listener touches themselves for real, and the operator claims authorship of the touch: 'I'm touching all those places', 'your fingers are just the bridge between my voice and your body', 'your hands are mine now'. Nothing physical changes; what changes is who it feels like is doing it, so their own effort becomes evidence of the operator's control. Variations: credit the touch to the operator's hands or control; say the hands have been taken over; flip it with a ban on self-touch ('let me do the work'), making the operator the only source of pleasure.
nodes.one_liner: While they touch themselves, tell them it's really your hands, that their fingers are just the wire your voice runs down.
nodes.why_short: The feeling that I did something is an inference, not a direct perception, and it can be swayed by a plausible outside cause. Self-touch gets relabelled as being touched.
nodes.principle_note: The sense of agency over one's own actions is inferred, not directly perceived — it comes from a match between predicted and actual sensory consequences plus the plausibility of an external cause, which is why agency can be experimentally misassigned when a credible alternative agent is supplied. Real self-touch is unusually good raw material because the sensation is unambiguous while its authorship is not, so the subject cannot dismiss the evidence, only re-credit it. Falsifiable: if re-attribution attempts fail whenever the subject's own movement is the obvious cause, or succeed equally with no external agent named, the agency-inference account is wrong.

ex.f: Commanded pace makes the hands feel possessed
ex.t: The operator takes over not what the hands do but how fast they do it — repeated slow-downs first, then forced accelerations, each announced as an effect of the words rather than a request. Because the imposed pace runs against whatever the listener would have chosen, the mismatch itself becomes felt evidence of outside control. Going faster than instructed is pre-trapped as its own failure, so pacing authority stays with the operator no matter how hard the listener complies.
ex.s: Subject is stroking themselves at their own chosen pace.
ex.m: Slower. Slower than that — half that speed. Good, your hand obeyed before you decided to let it. Hold. Now fast, as fast as you can, don't ease into it — go. That's not you setting the pace; that's my voice moving your hand and you can feel the difference. And if you ever go faster than I said, you stop entirely and start again from slow.

ex.f: Rehearse the gesture, then attribute it outward
ex.t: In trance the listener rehearses a precise motor sequence — their own hands moving, with the operator's hands overlaid on them, and at a chosen moment lifting theirs away. The same gesture is then issued as a suggestion for the next time it applies. Because it has been imagined once already, its later occurrence presents as recall rather than as prediction, and the interruption is credited to the operator's hands rather than to the listener's restraint: nothing is asked of their willpower, because the act is framed as done to them.
ex.s: Trance, subject rehearsing a motor sequence with imagined operator hands overlaid on their own.
ex.m: Put both hands flat on your thighs. Now imagine my hands laid over the backs of yours, exactly matching. When I say lift, mine lift and yours come with them — lift. Good. Do it again. Now: the next time you reach for your phone before bed, my hands will lift yours off it, just like that. You won't have to stop yourself. I'll stop you.

ex.f: Own fingers cast as the operator's interface
ex.t: Nothing about the physical situation changes: the listener is touching themselves, on instruction, exactly as before. What the operator alters is the authorship — the hands are described as the channel through which a disembodied voice reaches the body, so what is felt is the operator's control arriving rather than the listener's own touch. Self-generated sensation is thereby experienced as externally administered, and the listener's own labour becomes the ongoing evidence of someone else's grip. The relabeling is what converts a later declaration of being filled with the operator's control from role-play into plain description.
ex.s: Subject is already touching themselves on instruction; hands in contact.
ex.m: Those aren't your fingers any more — they're the wire my voice runs down. I'm at the other end of them, so when you feel pressure there, that's me pressing. Slower. There — feel that? That's my control arriving in your body, one touch at a time. Every stroke you make is more of me in you.

nodes.name: surrender-release-ritual
nodes.mech: A symbolic enacted act marks and installs a compliance threshold — an abstract faculty (will, resistance, responsibility, wakeful cognition) is first objectified into a manipulable thing (a lock, a bubble, an object in the hands, a colored glow, an exhaled substance) and then released, dropped, popped, dimmed, or offloaded by an act the subject performs or authors. The enacted release IS the suggestion; authorship of the letting-go stays with the subject, so surrender reads as a chosen, completed, and felt event rather than something done to them. Common twists ride the same lever — re- arming the release onto an involuntary cue for auto-maintenance, animating the threshold as a mechanical event, gating it on a count, offloading the changed-belief authorship onto a device while the subject speaks the admission aloud, or recasting the released substance as the subject's own weakness.
nodes.one_liner: Have them find their willpower, give it a colour, then let it go: dim it, drop it, or breathe it out on a count.
nodes.why_short: Acts we perform ourselves feel chosen, and chosen acts change attitudes more than things done to us. Surrender becomes a completed, felt event they authored.
nodes.principle_note: Acts performed by the subject are self-attributed, and self-attributed acts drive attitude change in a way that acts done to a person do not — this is the consistency principle operating on behavior rather than statements. Objectifying the faculty first is what makes the act performable: an abstract will cannot be dropped, but a lock can, and completing a concrete act gives the surrender a definite moment and a felt endpoint. Falsifiable: if operator-performed releases produce the same subsequent compliance as subject-performed ones, the authorship claim is empty.

ex.f: Placed in the hands, discarded by choice
ex.t: The operator narrates lifting the churning wakeful thoughts out of the listener's head and handing them over as objects the listener is now holding. A short count then offers exactly two options: dispose of them and drop, or keep them and stay awake. Only one branch has been made attractive, and the operator says so immediately — but because the listener performs the disposal, the release is theirs. A diffuse inability to stop thinking has been converted into one willed, completable act.
ex.s: Subject reports racing thoughts; counted release about to be offered.
ex.m: I'm lifting all that noise out of your head — feel me take it, and now it's in your hands, a tangle of it, heavier than you expected. On three you either drop it and drop with it, or you hold onto it and stay awake all night. One. Two — one of those is much nicer, and you know which. Three: open your hands.

ex.f: The release re-armed onto an involuntary cue
ex.t: Resistance and responsibility are drained into a container, and the listener destroys it themselves — the destruction is theirs, framed as relief rather than loss. Then the operator does the thing that outlasts the session: the same release is bound to a small involuntary bodily reflex, so it re-fires on its own indefinitely. A willed act performed once becomes an automatic maintenance loop that needs no operator present.
ex.s: Subject has just externalised resistance into a container; a post-session maintenance loop is wanted.
ex.m: Everything you were holding onto is in that glass — your resistance, and everything you thought you were responsible for. Throw it against the wall. Good, that's yours, you did that, and doesn't it feel lighter. Now: every time you blink, it happens again. One blink, one more thing gone, all day tomorrow, and I don't have to be there for it.

ex.f: Breathe it out; it was your weakness
ex.t: The listener is asked to hold a breath and then release it, with the exhale defined as the resistance leaving — which gives an abstract concession a bodily action that can actually be performed and finished. Alongside it runs a reframe: the resistance is named as the listener's own weakness, the thing standing between them and what they came for. Anyone still resisting is thereby demonstrating the operator's point.
ex.s: Mid-session; subject shows some hesitation and a counted release is being staged.
ex.m: Take a breath in and hold it. Hold it — everything in you that's still arguing is in that breath. Now let it go, all the way out, and it goes with it. That thing you were holding onto wasn't strength, it was the weak part of you, and it was the only thing standing between you and what you came here for. If you're still gripping it, you've just proved my point.

ex.f: Will made an object, dimmed on a count
ex.t: An abstract faculty is first converted into something handleable: the listener is asked to locate the last of their will in space, then to give it a visible property they can report. Once it is an object with properties it can be operated on, and the operator reduces it to nothing across a short count, marking the endpoint with a small sensory event. Asking the listener to say yes before the last number is what makes it a handover rather than a confiscation — and the marker gives the transfer a discrete closure they can point back to as a moment that happened. Taking it back afterwards would require an act, which is a higher price than never having given it.
ex.s: Late-session threshold; subject deep and able to answer a short question aloud.
ex.m: Find the last of your will — where is it sitting? Give it a colour and tell me. Good. Now I'm turning it down. Four: it's dimming. Three: dimmer. Two — say yes for me. One, and it's out, and you'll feel a click at the back of your neck as it goes. There. That's a thing that happened, and you'd have to reach up and switch it back on to undo it.

nodes.name: surrogate-delivery
