nodes.mech: Route suggestions through a stand-in the listener identifies with, so every line is grammatically about someone else and nothing is aimed straight at them. There is nothing to push back against, and they take on the effects by identifying with the stand-in. Variations: a fictional character, a dream narrator, or a captive speaking as 'I'; a stand-in who tries to resist and fails within seconds; a narrator who acts out the whole fight-then-give-in on the listener's behalf, again and again, so their own urge to resist is used up; two openly opposed voices, one protective and one coercive, both of which actually take them down.
nodes.one_liner: Give the suggestions to someone else in a story, a character or 'a client I once had', so nothing is aimed at the listener.
nodes.why_short: Pushback is triggered by a threat to your own freedom. Instructions given to someone else threaten nothing, yet the listener identifies with that person and takes them in.
nodes.principle_note: Psychological reactance is triggered by a perceived threat to one's own freedom of action; a directive grammatically aimed at a third party presents no such threat, so the defensive response that a second-person command would provoke is never elicited. Transportation into narrative and identification with a protagonist are known to reduce counterarguing, and observed behaviour by a model the audience identifies with shifts the observer's own expectancies about what is possible for them. The falsifiable claim: matched suggestion content should produce measurably less refusal and more reported effect when routed through an identified-with proxy than when addressed directly.

ex.f: A narrator who never decides anything
ex.t: The whole piece is a dream the speaker reports having had, and inside it she never once decides anything: she finds herself already moving, she takes what is offered, the current carries her and she is too tired to work against it, and each of these is noted as having felt perfectly ordinary. No instruction is issued to the listener at any point. What is being rehearsed, well before the first actual command arrives, is the grammar of doing-without-choosing.
ex.s: Opening; operator narrates a first-person dream to a listener who has not yet been addressed directly.
ex.m: So in the dream I'm already walking, I don't remember starting. Someone holds out a glass and I take it, that's just what happens. Then the water is moving and I'm going with it — I was far too tired to swim against it, and honestly it never once occurred to me to try. And none of that felt strange at all. It felt like the most ordinary evening of my life.

ex.f: The listener's avatar resists and loses in seconds
ex.t: The opening interleaves two voices: a scripted stand-in for the listener asking frightened questions, and the operator, who never answers any of them and instead overwrites each one with a flat statement of the stand-in's condition. Before long the stand-in has stopped asking and started agreeing, echoing the operator's phrasing back a beat before she says it. The listener's own impulse to insist they would have resisted has already been performed and lost on their behalf, before any induction proper begins.
ex.s: Opening lines; a scripted stand-in voice alternates with the operator, before any induction proper.
ex.m: — Wait, what are you doing? / Your eyes are getting heavy. — No, I don't want to, I can still— / Your arms are too heavy to lift. — I can still hear you, I'm not— / You're sinking. — I'm sinking. / You're not going to fight it. — I'm not going to fight it.

ex.f: Third person migrates to second under a count
ex.t: It opens as a fairy tale about someone else, told over a slow breathing count, and the listener settles in as audience. Somewhere in the middle the pronouns slide — the tale turns out to be about you, you are its subject now — and from there every action the character performs reads as an instruction. The count is doing the work: attention is split between tracking breaths and tracking who "he" is, so neither gets enough to notice the conversion.
ex.s: Opening as a story told over a slow breathing count; subject positioned as audience.
ex.m: Breathe in, two, three. Once there was a traveller who came to a low door in a wall — out, two, three — and he knelt down to see through it. In, two, three. He put his hand on the frame, and he found he was already leaning in — out, two, three — and you're leaning in now, aren't you, because it was always you at that door. In, two, three. You put your knee on the step. You go through.

ex.f: Induction commands quarantined inside a failure anecdote
ex.t: The operator offers, as an aside, an example of someone she says she could not get under — and then delivers, in full present tense, an entire induction: settle onto a steady background sound, stop tracking my voice, let it take the thinking part offline. The listener's critical attention is pointed at the wrong question the whole time — did it work on that other person? — while the commands themselves land unchallenged, because narratively they are on record as having failed. One line slips the wall, noting that the listener can probably hear something similar right now, and re-aims at the live listener for a moment before retreating back into the anecdote.
ex.s: Early session, conversational register; operator relates an anecdote about a failed subject.
ex.m: There was one I couldn't get under at all, and I gave it a real go — I told him, let the hum of the room hold your attention, stop following my voice, just let the sound do it while the part of you that thinks about things goes quiet and offline. Nothing. Not a flicker. Though I suppose you can probably hear something like that in your room right now. Anyway, he sat there wide awake the whole time.

nodes.name: surrogate-object-property-projection
nodes.mech: Describe a state as belonging to a neutral object rather than the listener: how calm a tomato plant is, how a granite statue has no will. There is nothing about their own body they can disprove, so they feel the state by identifying with the object, and claims they would reject if said directly slip through. Variations: rule out the obvious subject ('this won't be about flowers') so the listener fills themselves in; attach a cue word to the object's already pleasant imagery so it is charged for later use.
nodes.one_liner: Talk about how calm a plant feels, or how a statue has no will, and let them feel it as themselves without being told to.
nodes.why_short: Saying it about an object gives nothing to disagree with. A loose reference invites the listener to fill themselves in. Erickson case lore; no direct test.
nodes.principle_note: Describing a state in an object rather than in the listener is the technique itself, not the reason it works. The testable explanation is narrower: a statement with no stated subject invites the listener to put themselves in that place, and content people supply themselves gets less of the arguing back that a direct 'you feel...' would draw. This could be shown wrong: statements about an object should meet fewer open rejections than direct versions only among listeners who say they filled themselves in. Listeners who take the object literally should show no difference. The generation effect is about memory for things people produce themselves, not about accepting suggestions, so it does not explain this.

ex.f: The state predicated of a plant
ex.t: "so pleasing just to be able to think about a plant as if it were a man. Would such a plant have nice feelings, a sense of comfort" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Disqualify the literal referent so he supplies himself
ex.t: "the burden of constructing a meaning for this communication falling upon Joe." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Occupy a statue, inherit its refusable properties
ex.t: The operator introduces a carved stone figure as a comparison, then moves the listener inside it — imagine being held within that shape — and only afterwards begins listing what the figure is like: it does not think, it has no mind of its own, it could not move even if it wanted to. Every one of those claims would be refused if aimed straight at the listener; attached to the stone, and with the listener already inside the stone, they are simply description. A cue word for stillness is dropped into the descending count partway through, welded onto imagery that already feels physically true.
ex.s: Descending count running; a stone figure has been introduced as a comparison.
ex.m: Look at the statue in the alcove — carved granite, seated, hands on its knees. Now be inside it: your body held in that shape, stone all around you. Twelve. It doesn't think about anything. Eleven. It has no mind of its own. Ten — still, that's the word, still — nine. It couldn't move even if it wanted to. Eight.

nodes.name: transitive-charge-chaining
nodes.mech: Lead from something the listener already feels warmly about to the final image in small, easy steps, each carrying the feeling of the one before: love her voice, the shape of her lips, how they taste, a drugged lipstick. The end image lands without ever being argued for. Anything a step brings in carries its own meaning, so 'you can't resist' arrives as part of the drug imagery rather than as a claim they could refuse.
nodes.one_liner: Step from something they already like to the final image in small links (your voice, your lips, your drugged lipstick) so the feeling carries along.
nodes.why_short: Feelings attach to things paired with them. Whether that carries through several links in a row is weakly supported in the lab, so the chain may carry less than it seems.
nodes.principle_note: Evaluative conditioning is well established for a single pairing: co-occurring representations transfer affect without any argument being made. The chaining claim is not — second-order evaluative conditioning is weak and inconsistently replicated, and it is the load-bearing step here. Downgrade to plausible and test it directly: measure affect transfer at each link, and expect sharp decay past the first step rather than the assumed cumulative displacement.

ex.f: Each image inherits the last one's charge
ex.t: The chain is built one small inference at a time, each link presented as something the listener has already done rather than something being asked. Liking the voice implies having attended to the mouth that makes it; attending to the mouth implies having wondered about contact; wondering about contact arrives at a substance the operator claims to have prepared herself, described as something that does not wear off. Nobody ever argued that the listener cannot resist. The final image simply carried that idea inside its own content, with the warmth accumulated over the preceding steps still attached to it.
ex.s: Mid-session, warm rapport established; the operator is leading step by step toward one final image.
ex.m: You like my voice — you wouldn't be here otherwise. And you can't like a voice without having thought about the mouth that makes it. And you don't think about a mouth that long without wondering what it would be like against yours. So let me tell you about the lipstick I make myself. It goes on warm, and it soaks in where it touches, and it doesn't wear off.

nodes.name: vicarious-depth
nodes.mech: Have the listener imagine the operator being hypnotized over and over, by watches, spirals, several voices, inductions stacked on inductions, and urge them to try to keep track of every way it is happening. The task is impossible; losing track turns into giving up, while their mind fills with hypnosis images. Then swap who it is happening to mid-image ('the light bulb clicks on and your brain turns off'), so the listener inherits all the depth they just pictured. Because they made the imagery themselves, it is hard to push back against.
nodes.one_liner: Have them imagine you being hypnotized over and over until they lose track, then switch: suddenly it's happening to them.
nodes.why_short: Overloads tracking, then swaps the subject of the scene so they inherit the depth they were imagining. Practitioner invention; untested.
nodes.principle_note: Imagining an event increases confidence that it occurred or could occur (imagination inflation), and self-generated imagery is later hard to distinguish from externally-supplied content (source-monitoring error), so imagery the listener builds themselves is unusually resistant to dismissal. The 'try to track all the ways' instruction is a demand exceeding working-memory capacity, and the felt tracking failure supplies the experiential evidence of losing control that the swap then reassigns. Predicts the effect depends on the listener actually generating the imagery; supplying it verbatim instead should weaken the transfer.
steps: Ask them to keep track of every way you have been hypnotized.
Fill the scene with spirals, watches and voices aimed at you.
Mid-image, swap who it is happening to: now it is them.

ex.f: Imagine the operator entranced, then swap protagonists
ex.t: The listener is pressed to attempt an impossible tally: count up every separate occasion the operator has herself been put under, and every different method used, all of it stacked into an unmeasurable span. The counting fails on purpose; the listener abandons it partway with working memory now full of trance imagery they constructed themselves. Then, without a pause, the scene keeps running but the person it is happening to has been exchanged for the listener. Whatever depth they granted the imagined figure is now simply theirs, and it is hard to dispute because they drew every frame of it.
ex.s: Mid-session; subject able to hold imagery, no direct depth suggestion yet.
ex.m: Count them for me: every single time I've been put under, every separate occasion, and every different method used on me. Try — try right now, count them all up, the watches and the spirals and the voices layered over each other. Keep counting. You can't hold it all, can you. Now the light clicks off over that chair, and the person sitting in it, going all the way down under all of that, is you.

nodes.name: words-as-touch-transposition
nodes.mech: Collapses the auditory channel into the tactile so that hearing the operator's voice IS being touched — the words/voice are asserted to BE a physical sensation on the listener's body (tracing skin, caressing, vibrating between the legs, penetrating), not merely to describe or cause one. Once made, the substitution binds a somatic component to every subsequent utterance: the listener can no longer hear without feeling, the normal evaluate-speech stance is removed, and later commands ride an already-open somatic carrier. Often the felt intensity is made contingent on trance depth, turning 'go deeper' into a chaseable sensory reward.
nodes.one_liner: Tell them your voice is hands on their skin, not sound in their ears, so every word you say lands as a touch.
nodes.why_short: Told a sound is a touch, they put attention on their skin and read ordinary body sensations as the suggested touch. After that, every line carries a physical feeling.
nodes.principle_note: Suggested cross-modal experience works through expectancy: told that a sound is a touch, attention is directed to tactile channels and ambiguous somatic noise is interpreted as the suggested sensation, which then confirms the frame. This is ordinary suggestion-plus-attention, not genuine developmental synesthesia, and it should show the usual signature of expectancy effects — strong individual differences correlated with suggestibility, and reduction when the listener is told to check whether anything is actually contacting their skin. Once established, the pairing of voice with reliably-reported sensation is a conditioning arrangement that can strengthen with repetition.

ex.f: Felt intensity made contingent on depth
ex.t: Early on, each spoken word is described as drawing a line across the listener's skin, the way a fingertip would. Then the dial is named: the further down you go, the better that contact feels. "Deeper" stops being an abstract instruction and becomes a sensory purchase the listener can make.
ex.s: Voice-as-touch already established; a depth incentive is being installed.
ex.m: Every word I say draws a line across your skin, like a fingertip tracing you — feel this sentence go down your arm. And here's the part that matters: the further down you go, the better it feels. Halfway down it's pleasant. All the way down and every word I speak is exquisite. So go and get it.

ex.f: Countable proliferation plus a self-touch ban
ex.t: Once each word is established as a hand moving down the body, the operator starts counting them up: one hand becomes several, several become too many to place, mouths are added, and eventually the number is simply asserted to be beyond counting — escalation costs nothing, because there is always one more to add and no new image is required. Mid-stack, the listener's own hands are taken off the board, with the prohibition delivered in the same indulgent register as the rest, so nothing accumulating has anywhere to go except where the operator later sends it.
ex.s: Voice-as-touch established; escalation and a self-touch ban to install.
ex.m: One hand moving down you. Now two, one on each side. Now six of them, and you can't say where they all are. Add mouths — three, four, at your throat and your hip. Now it's more than you can count, everywhere at once, and there's always another one. And your own hands stay exactly where they are, sweetheart — flat, still, nothing for them to do. Let it build. It's not going anywhere I don't send it.

ex.f: The voice asked to be touch
ex.t: There is no relaxation, no count, no eye fixation — the first line of the recording asks the listener to hear the voice as a pair of hands, and to feel it arriving on the skin rather than in the ears. Nothing is described as causing a sensation; the sound is asserted to be the sensation. From that point on every sentence spoken is a physical event rather than a statement, which quietly removes the ordinary option of listening to something and deciding what you think of it.
ex.s: First line of the session; no induction preamble at all.
ex.m: Don't listen to me — feel me. My voice is a pair of hands, and it's arriving on your skin, not in your ears. Right now it's at the back of your neck. This isn't a description of a sensation. This sound is the touch.

nodes.name: autonomic-act-rekeying
nodes.mech: The operator stops calling breathing 'inhale' and 'exhale' and gives it new, loaded names that carry extra meaning: 'expire' as a small surrender or little death, 'inspire' as the operator's breath entering the listener. A small agreeing beat seals it ('isn't that beautiful?'). From then on, every ordinary breath can be referred back to that meaning, so something the listener does constantly and automatically becomes a quiet, ongoing reminder of the operator's framing, with no further effort needed.
nodes.one_liner: Rename breathing with loaded words (expire = a little death, inspire = me entering you) so every breath carries that meaning.
nodes.why_short: Words drag their associations into how an experience is felt. Breathing never stops, so the renamed act is a constant, free reminder of the operator's framing.
nodes.principle_note: Semantic priming and label effects are correctly invoked: the term used for an experience carries its associative network into how that experience is appraised. But mere exposure is an affect effect (repetition breeds liking) and does not explain accessibility — the right mechanism for a continuous act like breathing is cue frequency maintaining construct activation. Falsifiable: the effect should track how often the listener actually notices their breath, and should fade if the original label is deliberately reinstated.

ex.f: Renaming breath so every exhale carries a death
ex.t: The operator sets aside the ordinary words for breathing in and out and installs a pair of loftier ones, then points out — mildly, almost as trivia — that one of them is also the word used when something dies, and that the other means to fill with breath, which is what she is doing to the listener from across the room. She then invites the listener to find that lovely, and the silent agreement is the whole ratification. No pacing is done and no breath is ever counted. From here the listener's metabolism runs on its own as before, except that every cycle of it is now something she named and can tag whenever she likes.
ex.s: Early-to-mid session, no breath pacing being used; conversational register.
ex.m: Let's not say breathe out. Let's say expire — because that's the word we use when something dies, isn't it, and that's what you're doing with each one, a small death, over and over. And the other one is inspire: to be filled with breath. That's me, from over here, putting breath into you through the air. Isn't that beautiful?

nodes.name: counterfeit-cue-forgery
nodes.mech: Many automatic reactions fire on one simple cue rather than on checking what is really there: laughter means it's funny, a full tip jar means people tip, a queue means it's good. The operator fakes that cue (canned laughter, coins salted into the jar, a staged line, an 'unrehearsed' testimonial) so the person's habitual response runs as if the real thing were present. Nothing new is taught; a trusted shortcut is counterfeited and the person skips checking. Once the fake is spotted, it stops working at once.
nodes.one_liner: Fake a cue people normally trust (canned laughter, a salted tip jar, a staged line) so their automatic response fires on nothing.
nodes.why_short: Snap judgments check one telltale feature, not the whole situation. A forged feature runs the routine without the real thing being there.
nodes.principle_note: Recognition routines are economical: they key on one or a few diagnostic features rather than verifying the whole referent, which is efficient when features and referents correlate in the natural environment. Forgery decouples that correlation, and because the shortcut runs before deliberate checking, the response is emitted toward an absent referent — the same structure as supernormal stimuli in ethology and social-proof heuristics in humans. Directly falsifiable: make the forgery detectable, or give the target time and motivation to verify, and compliance should collapse.

ex.f: Faking a normally reliable social cue
ex.t: "a compliance practitioner tr[ies] to stimulate a shortcut response by giving us a fraudulent signal for it" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

ex.f: Counterfeit trigger features run the program to completion
ex.t: "Responding mechanically to the beetles' trick trigger features, the ants treat the beetles as though they were fellow ants… yet they are never harmed" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

nodes.name: enacted-embodied-proof
nodes.mech: Have the listener perform an action so their body produces the felt evidence for an abstract claim or rule; the metaphor becomes something they have just done. A suction image is backed by 'suck your cheeks in right now'; a 'plus two, minus one' rule is locked in by self-stroking paced to the breath; a guided self-touch tour runs alongside induction language so arousal and deepening can't be separated and the touching itself shows compliance. Once the body has done it, 'your mind works the same way' rests on enacted proof rather than argument, and the attention the action takes is itself a sign of going along.
nodes.one_liner: Have the listener physically do something (suck in cheeks, stroke on the inhale) that acts out the rule you are about to claim.
nodes.why_short: People infer what is true about themselves from what they just did. A performed action feels like evidence, not argument.
nodes.principle_note: Self-perception theory: people infer their attitudes and states from observing their own behaviour, especially when internal cues are ambiguous, so an action just performed becomes evidence for the claim it was framed to illustrate. Compliance with a small physical request also engages consistency pressure, making the following larger claim cheaper to accept than to contest. Falsifiable: the claim should be accepted more when the listener actually performs the action than when they merely imagine it or are told others do it.

ex.f: Suck your cheeks in, then hear the claim
ex.t: Mind-emptying gets explained as a pressure difference — the fuller side flows toward the emptier side. When the listener is described as not following, the register drops and the explanation is reissued as an instruction to draw the cheeks inward against the mouth, immediately, without waiting. Once the mouth has actually done it, the follow-up claim that thinking behaves identically no longer has to be argued for; it is riding on something the listener just felt happen in their own face.
ex.s: An emptying-as-pressure-difference explanation has just been given and the subject is not tracking it.
ex.m: You're not following. Suck your cheeks in. Right now — don't wait, pull them in against your teeth and hold it. Feel that? Feel it pulling inward because there's less in there than out here. Good, let go. Your mind does exactly that, and you just felt it happen in your own face.

ex.f: A directed self-touch tour carrying induction copy
ex.t: The listener is routed through a geometric tour of their own body — shoulders, chest, ribs, down to a named boundary and no further — with the operator keeping routing authority while handing over the actual contact. Laid over the same lines, without a break or a change of tone, is standard deepening copy: this is becoming automatic, those hands of yours are beginning to feel like they belong to somebody else. There is no discrete induction event to point at, and by the end the listener cannot cleanly separate being aroused from being under.
ex.s: Subject aroused and under; operator directs contact while continuing deepening copy on the same line.
ex.m: Both hands on your shoulders — slide them down over your chest, and this is getting automatic now, isn't it. Out along your ribs, down to your hips and stop there, nowhere lower, and your hands are starting to feel like they belong to somebody else. Back up the same way. Down again, slower, and further down feels further under.

ex.f: Paced stroking binds a rule to proprioception
ex.t: The rule — two steps up on the way down, one step back on the way up — has been stated abstractly for several minutes. Now the listener is told to run it with their own hand against their own breathing, moving downward on the inhale and back up on the exhale. The pairing is deliberately the reverse of the usual rise-on-inhale template, which makes it slightly awkward, which means the listener has to attend closely to get it right — and that careful attention is itself compliance. When the pacing stops, the rule is no longer a claim to be evaluated; it is a shape the listener's body has just spent a sustained stretch tracing, and future arousal will feel like it.
ex.s: A two-forward-one-back arousal rule has been stated abstractly for several minutes; subject's hand is free.
ex.m: Now do it with your hand. Two strokes down as you breathe in — down on the in-breath, yes, opposite to what you'd expect, so pay attention. One stroke up as you breathe out. Again: down, down on the breath in. Up on the breath out. Keep it exactly on the breath. Two forward, one back, and that's the shape everything in you moves in from now on.

nodes.name: induction-less-work-as-onramp
nodes.mech: The session has no separate induction: no relaxation, counting, or body scan. It opens already inside the scene and lets the content do the induction's job, a sustained image, arousal, or conversation, carried by rhythm and repetition. This usually assumes a listener who already drops on a learned cue. Because there is no clear moment of 'going under', there is also no clear moment to decline. Variations: work as the on-ramp, where arousal or one image carries the listener in; ambient role-occupation, a conversational piece that never marks an entry point and is about 'putting on' a role rather than going under, sometimes still ending with a wake-up count.
nodes.one_liner: Skip the formal induction entirely; open already inside the scene and let the content itself (arousal, an image, conversation) carry the listener in.
nodes.why_short: For a practised listener, the familiar voice and material are themselves cues for trance, so a separate warm-up adds little.

ex.f: Opens inside the frame and never ramps
ex.t: There is no relaxation pass, no breathing pass, no eye fixation, no body scan. Line one is already inside the state, and the next two hundred lines restate and thicken that state at constant pressure with no rest beats and no signposts announcing a change of section. A listener cannot orient by phase because there are no phases; the absence of structure is the structure. It only works on someone who already drops on a learned cue — this is a top-up, not a first session.
ex.s: Line one of the file, with no relaxation, breath-count, fixation or body-scan anywhere in the recording; listener already drops on a learned cue.
ex.m: There you are — already down, already soft, exactly where you land every time you hear me. Nothing to do first, nothing to count, no getting there; you're there. Stay open and let me keep saying it, because I'm going to say it for the next twenty minutes without stopping.

ex.f: One image does induction, work and emergence
ex.t: A single image is introduced almost immediately and never left: something of the listener's is placed inside a device that works on it by a single repeated motion. The induction consists of nothing except that device's one action, said over and over on the beat; the main suggestions ride the very same picture, which is never swapped out or added to; and the wake-up, at the end, is done by running the image's one action backwards and handing the thing back. There is no way to cut this recording into induction, deepener, suggestions and wake, because one image is doing all four jobs at once.
ex.s: Opening minute; the one image the file will ever use is introduced immediately and never swapped, and it will carry the induction, the main suggestions and the wake-up.
ex.m: Your thoughts are folded up and fed between two rollers, and my hand is on the crank. Turn — and they press thinner. Turn — thinner, turn — thinner still, nothing left between the rollers but a bright flat film that says yes, and at the very end I'll crank it backwards, once for each thought, and hand them back.

ex.f: First descent cue fused straight onto the payload
ex.t: The entire preamble is a single line naming what the session will consist of. The first cue to go down arrives within the opening handful of lines, and the main suggestion is attached to it in the very next line; there is no ramp between them. Deepening after that comes from rising repetition rather than new content, until the closing stretch is little more than one word repeated on the beat. A first-time listener gets nothing from that closing stretch; a listener already conditioned to the cue is long since down.
ex.s: The first four lines of the file, before anything else; listener already conditioned to the drop-cue used here.
ex.m: This is twenty minutes of dropping and obeying. Nothing else in it. Sleep now — and going down is obeying, obeying, obeying, obeying.

ex.f: Arousal as induction, climax as depth-peak
ex.t: No count down, no relaxation, no fixation — the listener is put to work almost immediately, and the narrowing of attention is produced by the pleasure itself rather than by any induction move. The operator names the substitution out loud partway through. Because there is no before-and-after threshold, there is no moment at which the listener could have said no to going under; the state has been sliding since the first few minutes. The arc is inverted too: climax is the deepest point rather than the exit, and the wake-count at the end is brief and decorative because the refractory state does the coming-up on its own.
ex.s: About a minute in, with no induction of any kind offered; listener already stroking on instruction and about to have the substitution named aloud.
ex.m: Keep that slow steady stroke going, because that is your induction tonight — you don't get another one. Every pass of your hand does the work a counted number would have done, so the closer you get, the further under you go. And when you finish, that is the deepest point of this file, not the way out of it.

nodes.name: measurement-confound-mitigation
nodes.mech: A rule for whoever is observing someone's behavior, not something done to them. A single observation misleads in two ways: a behavior may simply not show up that day or in that setting, and people act differently when they know they are watched. So the observer spreads observations across different times, places, and people, keeps the watching as unobtrusive as possible, and repeats it over several days until the person gets used to it and their behavior settles back to normal.
nodes.one_liner: When observing someone's behavior, watch across many times and settings, and keep watching until they stop reacting to being watched.
nodes.why_short: One sample can miss behavior that only shows in some contexts, and people act differently when newly observed; repeated, spread-out observation fixes both.
nodes.principle_note: Behaviour varies across settings and observers, so a single sample is an unreliable estimate of a rate; aggregating across occasions reduces sampling error and raises the reliability of the estimate — basic measurement theory, not a claim about the subject. Reactivity is a well-documented artifact in which being observed changes the observed behaviour, and it typically attenuates with repeated exposure as the observer's presence loses novelty. Falsifiable and routinely tested: reactivity predicts a systematic difference between early and later observation sessions that should shrink over days.

ex.f: Vary time, setting and person to defeat masking
ex.t: "if data are collected only during morning sessions, at home, or with a specific caretaker, the 'target' behavior may be masked in the afternoon, at school, or with different caretakers" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Repeat observations until reactivity decays
ex.t: "behavior analysts mitigate reactivity when they make observations as unobtrusive as possible, repeat observations until apparent reactive effects subside" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: no-exit-reachability-closure
nodes.mech: The whole session is designed so every way the listener might leave (doubting, waking, distraction, seeking relief) has already been turned into a way deeper in. It is a property of the whole arc, not of one line. Variations: fuse opposites so relief feeds the state (relaxing makes you more aroused); build a sense, remove it, fill the gap with the voice; pre-label doubt, startle, or fighting sleep as deepeners; seal each exit so fighting one feeds the next; run one unbroken ramp with no pause; assign every action a meaning in advance (stroking is good, stopping is good, holding back is failing) so nothing counts as resisting.
nodes.one_liner: Design the whole session so every possible way out (doubt, waking, distraction, relief) is pre-labelled as a way deeper in.
nodes.why_short: People reassert judgment when they hit a break or contrast. If every candidate exit is already reframed, no such occasion arrives.
nodes.principle_note: The lever is the removal of decision points. Reasserting judgment requires an occasion — a break, a contrast, or a state in which criticality is available — and pre-loading every candidate exit with a reframe means each attempted counter-move produces an outcome consistent with the frame, so the listener accumulates only confirming evidence. This is closer to a designed contingency space than to any single cognitive effect, and the claim that closure per se does the work is not separately established. Falsifiable: insert a genuine unframed pause or contrast and refusal rates should rise even with all other content held constant.

ex.f: Opposed states fused so relief feeds the system
ex.t: Relaxing further is arousal. Choosing freely is the compulsion working correctly. Coming out of trance leaves the arousal running. Getting frustrated is itself a deepener. No single one of these pairings is unusual; what makes the file closed is that the same stance is applied at every level, from the one-word cue to the shape of the week, so there is no state left that offers a way out.
ex.s: Late-file consolidation, after relaxation and arousal have each been built separately and can now be welded together.
ex.m: The more relaxed you get, the more turned on you get — same slider, one handle, and I'm the one on it. Choosing this and having to do this are the same thing now; when it feels like your own free choice, that's the conditioning running correctly. And when you come up, the ache stays running, so getting frustrated with it just walks you straight back down here.

ex.f: Build a referent, destroy it, refill it
ex.t: A vivid physical setting is built early and given real sensory weight, then taken apart piece by piece, and the space it leaves is refilled with the operator's own repeated words. By the late mantra stretch there is no environment, no story and no actively maintained sense of the body — only the voice, which is now the last remaining thing to orient by.
ex.s: Two-thirds in; the listener has spent ten minutes inside a fully-built sensory location, which is now dismantled piece by piece.
ex.m: The lamps go out one at a time, and the walls go with them. Now the floor, now the sound of the water, now the weight of the chair under your legs — and now the legs. There's nothing left to look at and nothing left to stand on, only my voice saying empty, empty, empty, and it's the only thing in here that still has edges.

ex.f: Every possible action pre-assigned a valence
ex.t: Doing it is obedience. Stopping when told is obedience. Finding the instruction faintly ridiculous is named in advance as part of the service. Holding back at the edge is pre-labelled as thinking too much, which is the one failure the file recognises. Nothing in the listener's repertoire has been left unclaimed, and none of it was achieved by issuing more commands — only by naming the likely deviations before the listener could reach for them as resistance.
ex.s: Immediately before the hands-on stretch, pre-assigning a valence to every move the listener could make.
ex.m: Touching yourself when I say is obedience, and taking your hand away the second I say stop is exactly the same obedience, worth exactly the same. If any of this strikes you as a bit ridiculous, that feeling is part of what you're handing me — the embarrassment is the gift. The only way to get tonight wrong is to hold back at the edge, because holding back is thinking, and thinking is the one thing I'm not asking you for.

ex.f: Every escape route sealed by a different mechanism
ex.t: Fight it and you are told the fighting is what breaks you. Tune out and you are told the words go in whether you attend or not. Decide the whole thing is nonsense and the doubt has already been named as the cue. Try to stop the recording and you are told the decision is no longer being made at the level that could stop it. No single one of these seals the file — each on its own leaves a door — but arranged together they cover the whole option space, and every counter-move a listener has is also the entrance to the next seal.
ex.s: Mid-file, delivered as one calm block the moment the listener first pushes back; each sentence closes a different exit.
ex.m: Fight it and the fighting tires out the part that was doing the fighting, which is the fastest way down there is. Stop paying attention and the words go in anyway — attention was never the requirement. Decide the whole thing is nonsense, and that little flicker of doubt is the cue I trained you on four minutes ago; and if you reach for the stop button, notice that the reaching is being done by the part of you that already said yes.

nodes.name: perpetual-obligation-ledger
nodes.mech: Using the urge to return favors, repay a debt plus a small, clearly labelled extra ('These five are yours... these are mine'), so every settlement creates a fresh debt and the balance never reaches zero. The exchange keeps itself going, turning a one-off favor into a standing tie you can lean on later: the obligation stays permanently open across repeated occasions.
nodes.one_liner: When you repay a favor, add a small labelled extra ('these are mine'), so they always owe you a little back.
nodes.why_short: Unrepaid favors feel uncomfortable and push people to reciprocate. A deliberate surplus restarts that pressure at every settlement.
nodes.principle_note: The reciprocity norm is established: an unrepaid favour is aversive and creates pressure to settle. But 'the ledger never closes so the pressure never discharges' cannot be contradicted — a continued tie confirms it and an ended tie is attributed to settlement. State it as a measurable dose claim instead: felt obligation and compliance should scale with the size of the unrepaid surplus, and should drop when the recipient is given a concrete means of repaying in full.

ex.f: Over-repay so the ledger never zeroes
ex.t: "the system painstakingly prevents the total elimination of outstanding obligations… 'These five are yours,'… she adds an extra measure, saying, 'These are mine.' On the next occasion, she will receive these back along with an additional measure" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

nodes.name: preparatory-target-definition
nodes.mech: Before watching anyone, the observer talks with the people involved and joins in their conversation to agree on exactly what behavior counts and which situations and reactions around it to look for. A vague complaint ('he's difficult') becomes a clear, agreed definition and a short list of things to record. This cuts down on guesswork during observation and keeps different observers recording the same thing.
nodes.one_liner: Before observing, talk with the people involved to agree on exactly what behavior counts and what to watch for around it.
nodes.why_short: Vague definitions force on-the-spot judgment, which is the main source of observers disagreeing. A pre-agreed definition reduces drift.
nodes.principle_note: Observer agreement is a measurement property, not a personal skill: vague target definitions require on-the-spot judgment, and judgment latitude is the main source of inter-observer disagreement and drift. Fixing an operational definition and a short watch-list in advance removes that latitude and demonstrably raises inter-observer reliability, which is why it is standard practice in behavioural assessment. Falsifiable and routinely measured: two observers using a pre-agreed operational definition should show higher agreement scores than the same observers working from a vague complaint.

ex.f: Interview to operationalize before observing
ex.t: "began by interviewing her teaching assistants and by participating in the conversation with them to define the target behavior and to determine what antecedents and consequences she would watch for" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: somatic-mirroring
nodes.mech: The operator picks up a sensation the listener genuinely has, such as heaviness, warmth, numbness, drifting, arousal, or a twitch, often one just confirmed, and explains it as proof that trance or the intended change is happening. Nothing new is conjured; a real feeling gets a new meaning, so the claim is much harder to dismiss than a bare assertion. Variations: credit a change the operator caused to the listener's own body; use a known perceptual effect so the body supplies the evidence; loop it so each relabelled feeling makes the next stronger; ask leading questions that assume the feeling; rename one confirmed feeling as a growing need.
nodes.one_liner: Notice a feeling the listener really has (heaviness, warmth, a twitch) and tell them it proves the trance or change is happening.
nodes.why_short: Body sensations are ambiguous, and the label given shapes how they are felt. Because the sensation is real, the claim built on it is hard to dismiss.
nodes.principle_note: Bodily sensation is ambiguous, and the label attached to an ambiguous state determines how it is experienced — the misattribution-of-arousal finding in its general form. Because the sensation is genuinely present, the listener's own interoception confirms the percept while only the interpretation is supplied, so there is no false claim to catch. Falsifiable: offer a competing plausible explanation for the same sensation (room temperature, posture, fatigue) and the suggested meaning should lose ground, which does not happen if the reframe merely rides on general compliance.

ex.f: Leading questions manufacture the reported state
ex.t: Under cover of an invitation to simply notice how you're feeling, the operator runs through a list of questions: how does the skin feel now, are the legs tired or fine, is the neck starting to droop, are you a little worked up or a lot. Each one directs attention somewhere, and attention amplifies whatever it lands on, so the listener produces the evidence and then reads it as caused by the voice. The forced choice at the end gives it away: the smaller option is offered, but 'not at all' is not.
ex.s: First two minutes, framed as an ordinary check-in; listener able to answer aloud or nod, and every question presupposes some amount of the state.
ex.m: Just notice how you're doing for a second. How's the skin on your forearms right now — heavier, or more like warm? Are your legs tired or fine, is the neck starting to droop a little, and are you a bit worked up, or a lot?

ex.f: Pre-attributing the change to the listener's own body
ex.t: Each change is credited to the listener's physiology before it is asked for: the breathing begins to slow around now, and there is nothing unusual about that; when someone is well under, the body tends to shift a little to find a better position. Anyone lying still will do both of those things anyway. So the ordinary drift of a resting body arrives already labelled as evidence of trance, and the listener experiences relaxing on their own rather than being relaxed by someone.
ex.s: Three or four minutes in, listener lying still, with no relaxation instruction yet given and none about to be given.
ex.m: Your breathing is slowing down around about now, all on its own — perfectly ordinary, nobody has to do that for you. And in a minute your body will shift a little to find a better position; that's just what a body does once someone is properly under. None of that is my doing.

ex.f: One confirmed referent renamed into a need-state
ex.t: First a neutral, entirely expected trance sensation is seeded — a warm settling somewhere around the stomach — and the listener is given time to find it and agree that it is there. Then, over a few lines, the same unchanged sensation is renamed: it's almost like being hungry, and then very hungry, and then hard to think about anything else. Nothing in the body was altered; only the label moved, which is exactly why the resulting craving feels like it came from inside.
ex.s: Mid-trance, after a neutral warm settling has been seeded and the listener has confirmed finding it; nothing in the body changes from here, only the label.
ex.m: That warm settled weight just under your ribs — you found it, it's yours, it's been there a couple of minutes. It's almost like being hungry, isn't it. And now it's very hungry, and now it's the kind of hungry that makes it hard to hold on to anything else you were thinking about.

ex.f: A sensation you confirmed, re-narrated as the theme
ex.t: Warmth belongs to the surroundings at first — the room, what the listener is wrapped in, what they are holding. Then it is offered as a shared observation rather than an instruction: are you getting that as well, the warm patch low in the torso, the one that gets stronger the longer you look at it. The listener checks, and finds something, because attention on a body part reliably produces something. Once the warmth is theirs and self-verified, it is tied to a second thing — warm places always make me drowsy — and the sensation they confirmed for themselves is now the evidence that they are going under. Refusing requires denying a feeling they have already half-reported.
ex.s: Early, listener settled and quiet, with something genuinely warm present — a blanket, a mug, a heated room — and able to nod or answer.
ex.m: It's warm in here tonight, isn't it — the blanket, the tea. I'm getting it too, that warm patch low in the belly that gets a little stronger the longer you keep your attention on it; have you found it yet? Warm places always make me drowsy — and there it is doing exactly that to you, and you found it yourself, I didn't put it there.

nodes.name: song-architecture-delivery-vehicle
nodes.mech: Build the whole recording as a song rather than as a lead-in, trance and wake-up. It works in layers, each at a different depth: short repeating mantra hooks, a rhyming sung chorus, and a spoken, drifting narrative. It is designed to be replayed, with no wake-up or return. A familiar pop sample lowers the listener's guard by presenting the content as entertainment they take in passively. What does the work is the form itself: music first, cyclical, played on repeat.
nodes.one_liner: Build the file as a song: short repeated mantra hooks, a rhymed chorus, a spoken verse, made to be replayed with no wake-up.
nodes.why_short: Repetition makes material feel familiar and easy to process, and easy-to-process statements feel truer. A song format invites replay without the listener deciding to re-listen.
nodes.principle_note: Repetition drives both mere-exposure liking and fluency: repeatedly heard material is processed more easily, and processing fluency is misread as familiarity, agreement, or truth (the illusory-truth effect), which rhyme and metre further amplify. Music-as-entertainment also invites a consumption stance rather than a scrutiny stance, and material processed without evaluative intent is less likely to be counterargued. Falsifiable: the effect should scale with number of replays and should shrink if listeners are instructed to evaluate the lyrics as claims.

ex.f: Song form as the conditioning substrate
ex.t: The piece works in three layers at once: a few short mantra hooks light enough to run in the background all day, a rhyming sung chorus carrying the main message, and spoken, drifting passages that tell the fuller story during the most relaxed stretches. There is no induction, no wake and no arc; it is cyclical, and the lyrics themselves say to replay it daily. A recognisable pop sample sits in the middle, so the content arrives as the kind of entertainment the listener already takes in without judging it. What does the conditioning is accumulated exposure, not how deep any one listen goes.
ex.s: Writing the track itself: three tiers over one loop, no induction, no wake, and the replay instruction stated inside the lyric.
ex.m: Hook, four times over the loop, light enough to hum at work: "empty head, easy yes." Chorus, on the sampled melody everybody already knows: "play me in the morning, play me every day / thinking's getting quieter and I like it that way." Then the spoken verse, half-time over the same bars, unhurried: "you don't have to follow this one, you only have to leave it running…"

nodes.name: staged-negotiation-favor-theater
nodes.mech: The operator, already knowing the outcome, stages a visible costly struggle with an off-stage authority (a 'battle' with the sales manager that never actually happens) and returns bearing fatigue signals — disheveled, weary, loosened tie, elapsed time — presenting the predetermined deal as a hard-won concession. The manufactured effort makes the target revalue an unchanged offer as a costly favor, manufacturing felt indebtedness and aligning the target emotionally with the operator ('he's on my side') against the fabricated adversary, which suppresses resistance.
nodes.one_liner: Pretend to fight hard on their behalf with an unseen boss, return looking worn out, and present the same deal as a hard-won favor.
nodes.why_short: People weigh a favor by how much it seemed to cost the giver, and can only judge that cost from visible cues like effort and fatigue.
nodes.principle_note: Reciprocity is triggered by perceived cost to the giver, not by actual cost, and humans have no direct access to the giver's ledger — so visible effort cues (fatigue, elapsed time, disarray) are used as a proxy for value received. The staged adversary also recruits in-group alignment: framing a third party as the obstacle converts the operator from counterpart to ally, and people concede more to allies than to opponents. Falsifiable: if targets who witness the effort theater do not concede more than matched targets given the identical offer without it, the account fails.

ex.f: A staged battle with an off-stage authority
ex.t: "the salesman would loosen his tie and return to his customers, looking weary but carrying the deal he had just 'hammered out' for them—the same deal he had in mind before entering the boss's office." — Cialdini (1984), Influence

nodes.name: switching-state-machine-topology
nodes.mech: A whole-script install shape that builds a two-state machine (e.g. normal / bimbo) with explicit gated transitions and an accumulation rule biasing drift toward the target state over repeated cycles — rather than pushing toward a single permanent end-state. It requires the listener to spend most time in the vanilla state and enter the target state only on cue; a protective amnesia rule shields the vanilla state from contamination so the script is re-runnable rather than one-shot. The on-trigger is the ongoing operational interface; the script itself is a one-time installer for repeated cross-session use. The lever is the state-space topology (switching with a drift bias), not a directional intensity push.
nodes.one_liner: Install two states (normal and, say, bimbo), one cue to switch in and one to switch back, with each visit making the next easier.
nodes.why_short: Things learned in one state are more easily recalled in that state, so a clear cue-gated boundary keeps the two modes separate and re-usable.
nodes.principle_note: Two-state designs work because state-dependent retrieval makes cues learned in one state more available in that state, so a gated entry cue plus a context boundary keeps the two repertoires from blurring; repeated cue-state pairings then strengthen the association each cycle, which is what the drift bias is made of. Keeping the listener mostly in baseline preserves the contrast that makes the cue discriminable — a cue that predicts nothing distinctive extinguishes. Falsifiable: if repeated cycles produced no faster or deeper entry over sessions, or if removing the baseline period left entry unimpaired, the topology claim would be wrong.

ex.f: Two gated states with a drift bias
ex.t: The file does not aim at a destination. It builds two states with a named cue for entering the second and a named cue for returning to the first, plus a rule that each visit makes the next one easier — a drift bias rather than a one-way push. It assumes the listener spends most of their life in the ordinary state, and an amnesia rule keeps the second state's content from bleeding back, which is what makes the thing re-runnable. The recording is a one-time installer; the cue is the interface that gets used from then on.
ex.s: Install section of a one-time file, after both states have been demonstrated once each; the recording will not be replayed, the cues will be used from now on.
ex.m: When you hear me say pink light, you become her — playful, easy, empty; when you hear clear, you're yourself again and back to your afternoon. Every time you cross over, the crossing gets quicker and the state gets a little wider, so next time takes less of the cue than this time did. And what she does stays with her: you come back knowing you were away and not much more, and that is what makes this safe to run again next week.

nodes.name: valued-channel-induction
nodes.mech: The operator listens to how the person talks ('I see what you mean', 'that sounds right', 'it feels off') to guess which sense they lean on, then opens the induction with a task in that sense, for example a vivid picture for someone who talks visually. Because the task feels easy and natural to them, doing it becomes the way into trance. If the induction fails, the operator blames picking the wrong sense rather than the person resisting. Note that the idea of a fixed preferred sense has not held up well in research.
nodes.one_liner: Pick the sense the person seems to favor (visual, auditory, feeling) from their word choice, and start the induction in that sense.
nodes.why_short: The claim that people have a stable preferred sense readable from their verbs has largely failed testing. Any benefit likely comes from just choosing an easy, engaging task.
nodes.principle_note: The claim that people have a stable dominant representational system readable from verb choice is the classic NLP prediction, and it has largely failed replication — predicate matching does not reliably improve outcomes. What plausibly survives is weaker and different: an opening task the subject can execute fluently succeeds more often than one they must struggle with, and early success raises expectancy, which is one of the better-supported predictors of hypnotic responding. Falsifiable and largely falsified in its strong form: matched-predicate inductions have not outperformed mismatched ones in controlled tests.

ex.f: Match the induction to the subject's valued channel
ex.t: "By bringing the client to a task which presupposes a visualization capacity, the hypnotist facilitates the transfer of control..." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: crisis-induction-live-readout
nodes.mech: Used in group or family work. The operator deliberately brings up the group's most taboo subject, sometimes even insulting a member, to set off the group's usual pattern of reactions. Then the operator stops engaging with the content and simply watches, re-raising the topic whenever things calm down. The unguarded exchange shows who sets off whom, something a polite session would hide. Tiredness and lowered resistance afterwards are side effects, not the goal.
nodes.one_liner: In a group, deliberately raise the most taboo topic, then stay silent and watch who sets off whom.
nodes.why_short: Provocation raises arousal and narrows attention onto the exchange, so people stop managing appearances and their habitual patterns show.
nodes.principle_note: Emotional arousal narrows attention onto the immediate exchange (Easterbrook), which reduces the self-monitoring that normally supports impression management, so responding under provocation is less edited than responding under ordinary conditions. Note that the stronger claim — that unedited responding reveals the 'real' influence hierarchy — is not testable as stated: it requires an independent measure of who controls whom, and without one, any observed sequence can be read as confirming it. Falsifiable in the weak form only: coded self-presentational behaviors (hedging, self-correction, deference markers) should decrease under provocation relative to matched ordinary sessions.

ex.f: Detonate the group, then read it
ex.t: "I sit back and observe… If it starts to slow down, then I step in and kick it to get it going again." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: target-selection
nodes.mech: Before doing anything, decide which concrete behaviors to train. Ways to choose: pick behaviors that unlock others; keep only targets the person's everyday surroundings will go on rewarding, avoiding ones unusual for their age or community; reward the behaviors that produce an outcome, not the outcome itself (that tends to fail); turn a vague goal into one measurable aspect (how often, how long, how fast, how much) moved in a set direction (calories, not bites); answer every trait label ('lazy', 'fearful') with 'what does the person actually do?'; and list a set number of strengths before the same number of problems, so you build, not only suppress.
nodes.one_liner: Before training anything, choose targets that unlock other skills, that the real world will keep rewarding, and that are concrete, countable behaviors.
nodes.why_short: Behavior is kept up by its consequences. A vague trait or an outcome cannot be rewarded directly, so you must aim at the specific behaviors that produce it.
nodes.principle_note: Behavior is maintained by its consequences, so an intervention aimed at an outcome or a trait label — neither of which the environment can reinforce — has nothing to act on; specifying a countable, environment-contactable response gives the contingency a surface. Targeting cusps works because responses that open access to new contingencies recruit further learning the operator never programmed, and choosing targets the natural setting already reinforces is what keeps them after the operator leaves. Falsifiable: contingencies placed on products rather than producing behaviors should show weaker and less durable change than matched behavior-level targets.

ex.f: Privilege the cusp that unlocks new contingencies
ex.t: "sets the occasion to access reinforcers that otherwise would not have been available" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Rank the eligible pool by leverage questions
ex.t: "Which behavior should be changed first?… modification is likely to provide access to more normalized settings… Will this new behavior produce reinforcement for significant others?" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: functional-analysis-methodology
nodes.mech: Turn a hunch into demonstrated cause by switching one suspected factor on and off while holding everything else steady, and seeing whether the behavior appears and stops with it. Compare against a calm control condition expected to produce the least of the behavior (usually play: favourite things freely available, no demands, constant attention), and test only the causes you suspect. Differences from that baseline show cause; the trade-off is that causes you didn't test can't be ruled out. You need control over what happens before and after the behavior, and a way to bring the behavior on.
nodes.one_liner: To learn what keeps a behavior going, switch each suspected cause on and off while holding everything else steady, and compare to a calm baseline.
nodes.why_short: Correlation cannot show which of several co-occurring factors is responsible; only manipulating one at a time and watching the behavior follow it shows cause.
nodes.principle_note: Correlation cannot distinguish which of several co-occurring variables maintains a behavior; only manipulating a candidate while holding others constant licenses a causal claim, and demonstrating control over both occurrence and nonoccurrence rules out chance covariation. The control condition matters because a rate is only interpretable against a baseline generated under the same measurement conditions. Falsifiable by construction — a hypothesized function that fails to produce differential responding is disconfirmed, and the method explicitly cannot rule out functions it never tested.

ex.f: Isolate one variable to upgrade correlation to control
ex.t: "specific manipulations of one event (the independent variable) produce a reliable change in another event... unlikely the result of extraneous factors (confounding variables)—a finding known as a functional relation" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Turn the maintaining event on and off
ex.t: "Functional analysis involves systematically manipulating environmental events thought to maintain problem behavior within an experimental design" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: design-time-reconnaissance
nodes.mech: Before designing anything, map everything the plan must survive, so gaps show up on paper, not in real life. One form: list every setting where the behavior should and should not happen, with alternative responses planned for the wrong moments; list every form the response should take and decide which to train directly; and survey the cues and rewards already present in those settings. The other: have the person write out every part of them that objects and why, checking every sense rather than stopping at the first few, warning that many usually object. Either way, a missed setting or objection can't resurface after commitment.
nodes.one_liner: Before designing, list every setting where the behavior should and should not happen, and every objection a part of the person might raise.
nodes.why_short: Learning does not automatically carry over to situations never trained, so unlisted settings and objections are where plans fail.
nodes.principle_note: Learned responses are under stimulus control, so what is trained in one set of conditions does not automatically transfer to conditions never enumerated — generalization is the exception and must be planned for, which is why an explicit inventory of settings and non-settings outperforms assumption. The objector census leans on a weaker claim: externalizing and writing down items reduces reliance on recall, and free recall reliably under-samples a set relative to prompted or exhaustive enumeration, so first-responders crowd out the rest. Falsifiable: if plans built with exhaustive enumeration showed no fewer post-commitment failures than plans built from unaided recall, the value claim is wrong.

ex.f: Survey the contingencies already running in the setting
ex.t: "What discriminative stimuli usually set the occasion…What schedules of reinforcement…are typical…What kinds of reinforcers are likely to be contingent" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Enumerate where it should and should not occur
ex.t: "situations that may appear to be appropriate opportunities…but are not…for which an alternative response is needed" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Enumerate response forms, then triage teaching
ex.t: "Only by having a complete list of all the desired forms of the behavior can the practitioner make meaningful decisions about which behaviors to teach directly and which to leave to generalization" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: generative-cusp-installation
nodes.mech: Teach a small, reusable pattern that keeps paying off: a fill-in sentence frame ('I want __') plus the habit of asking 'what's that?'. New words drop into the frame without separate teaching, and each question brings in new material on its own. A few small skills learned early lead to open-ended, self-driven learning instead of item-by-item gains.
nodes.one_liner: Teach a fill-in frame ('I want __') and a habit of asking 'what's that?', so the person keeps learning new items on their own.
nodes.why_short: A frame with an open slot is learned as a pattern, so new items slot in without separate teaching, and each question gathers new material.
nodes.principle_note: A frame with an open slot is a learned response class rather than a single response, so new items entering the slot are emitted without separate training — this is generalization across a class, and it is why returns can outrun instruction. The question-asking repertoire compounds it because each question produces information that functions as reinforcement, making the asking self-sustaining. Falsifiable: if subjects taught the frame showed no untrained fills, or if question-asking did not increase after information delivery, the compounding claim fails.

ex.f: Install one frame, get compounding returns
ex.t: "A child's ability to ask questions plays a major role in vocabulary growth by gen­erating new tacts, echoics, mands, intraverbals" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: influence-topology-node-selection
nodes.mech: First map who responds to whom in a group. Then aim the change at the one person whose shift will spread to everyone, usually the most stubborn member that others take their cue from, not the obvious 'problem' person, who is easy to change but gets pulled back by the group. The group then does most of the work, and the change lasts.
nodes.one_liner: Map who responds to whom in a group, then push change through the stubborn person others follow, not the obvious 'problem' member.
nodes.why_short: In a connected system, change at a central node spreads; change at a peripheral node gets pulled back by everyone else.
nodes.principle_note: In interacting systems, a change at a node with many inbound dependencies propagates further than an equal change at a peripheral node, and changes at peripheral nodes get reversed by the unchanged surrounding contingencies — the presenting member is peripheral in exactly this sense. Targeting the member others actually respond to means the surrounding people's behavior does the maintenance the operator would otherwise have to supply. Falsifiable: if change routed through high-influence nodes did not persist longer than matched change routed through the symptomatic member, the routing claim is wrong.

ex.f: Route change through the tenacious node
ex.t: "The person who has the symptoms will be the last one that you want to work with… the one who is really tenacious." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: natural-contingency-handoff
nodes.mech: Get a trained behavior to the point where ordinary life keeps rewarding it, then step back. Variations: prompt the behavior in the real setting just often enough for it to meet the rewards already there, then withdraw help; or keep practicing past mere correctness until it is fast and smooth enough for real-world demands, since a correct but slow response never gets rewarded and fades.
nodes.one_liner: Practice a trained behavior until it is fast and fluent enough that everyday life rewards it, then step away and let life maintain it.
nodes.why_short: Behaviors fade when reinforcement stops. One that reliably earns a natural reward in daily life keeps being reinforced without the trainer.
nodes.principle_note: Responses persist only while something reinforces them, so operator-supplied reinforcement guarantees extinction on withdrawal unless the response has contacted a reinforcer that is already present in the setting. Fluency matters because natural contingencies impose timing and quality thresholds — a correct-but-slow response fails to produce the reinforcer and therefore extinguishes exactly like an incorrect one. Falsifiable: withdrawing support before the response has contacted natural reinforcement, or before it meets the setting's rate criterion, should produce reliable decay relative to matched cases where contact and fluency were achieved.

ex.f: Train to fluency or it extinguishes
ex.t: "Behavior changes that seem to need generalization may only need better teaching. Try making the students fluent" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Bridge to first contact, then fade
ex.t: "consists of getting the learner to emit the behavior in the generalization setting just often enough to contact the contingency." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: social-reinforcement-recruitment
nodes.mech: Make the people around the subject the source of reward. Ask capable people already present to watch for and reward any reasonable effort, so gains last after the trainer leaves. If records show caregivers or staff rewarding the wrong thing (say, the end of an escalating outburst instead of polite requests), reverse it: answer the polite requests, stop rewarding the outburst, and build up tolerance for waiting. You can also choose a target because it changes how important people treat the subject, or teach the subject to check their own work and then ask an authority for praise. Pace those requests so they stay welcome.
nodes.one_liner: Get the people around the subject to notice and reward the wanted behavior (or stop rewarding the unwanted one).
nodes.why_short: Attention and approval from people who matter are strong rewards, and those people stay present after the trainer leaves.
nodes.principle_note: Attention and approval from significant others function as powerful social reinforcers, and unlike an operator they remain in the setting, so recruiting them shifts maintenance onto a source that persists. Reversing a caregiver's contingency works because whichever behavior in an escalation chain reliably produces the payoff is the one that gets strengthened — reinforcing the wrong endpoint teaches escalation directly. The dosing layer reflects that reinforcer delivery is itself behavior under its own contingencies: a recruiter who overdraws makes attending aversive and the agent stops delivering. Falsifiable: if recruited third-party reinforcement produced no better post-operator maintenance than operator-delivered reinforcement, the account fails.

ex.f: Waking the dormant reinforcing community
ex.t: "The contingency is there, but dormant. One solution… is to inform key people in the generalization setting of the value and importance of their attention… and ask them to help." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Proxy target chosen for its third-party payoff
ex.t: "not because of their direct benefit…but because of an important indirect benefit" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: compounding-dependency-loop
nodes.mech: A suggestion about the suggestions: claim that each listen permanently raises an everyday state (such as baseline arousal) instead of resetting afterward, and that the only relief is more of the same hypnosis, so the cure feeds the problem. Re-listening feels worthwhile because each session supposedly 'does more', any increase they feel is already explained as the suggestion working, and the only way out is tied to the escalation, closing a loop: more listening raises the baseline, which drives more listening.
nodes.one_liner: Claim each listen permanently raises their everyday arousal, and that only more listening relieves it.
nodes.why_short: Telling someone a change will grow makes them notice and credit any change. Making the session the only relief turns that into a reason to come back.
nodes.principle_note: Two well-supported effects interlock here. Response expectancy: pre-announcing that each session raises the baseline makes any felt change confirm the suggestion, and the pre-explanation blocks the alternative attribution that would disconfirm it. And negative reinforcement: if the installed state is aversive and the only announced relief is another session, escaping the state reinforces listening, which is the loop. Whether repeated listening genuinely raises a waking baseline is unestablished; what is established is that the arrangement makes listening self-reinforcing regardless. Falsifiable: if listeners given the escalation meta-suggestion showed no higher re-listening rate than matched listeners given the same content without it, the account fails.

ex.f: The cure that feeds the condition
ex.t: Near the close, the operator states as a rule that the effect does not reset between sessions: each replay leaves the listener's everyday, waking desire running a little hotter than before. Earlier in the same recording, the only sanctioned relief for that desire was returning to this voice. The two clauses interlock — the ache the file installs is discharged by playing the file, and playing the file raises the ache — so every relief is also a dose, and any increase the listener notices is pre-labelled as proof the suggestion is taking hold.
ex.s: Final ninety seconds, after the earlier stretch established that this voice is the only sanctioned relief for the want being installed.
ex.m: This does not reset when the file ends. Every time you play it, your ordinary daytime wanting runs a little hotter than it did before — and you already know the only thing that takes the edge off it is coming back here to me. So when you notice you need this more this week than you did last week, that isn't a problem; that's the suggestion working exactly the way it was built to.

nodes.name: object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition
nodes.mech: Declare an object the cause of the listener's state, not a reminder: a garment, an imagined device, or an everyday detail like a color. The uniform makes the blankness 'expand to fill' it or drains thought where it touches skin; an imagined collar 'radiates every word' and amplifies suggestions, so rising obedience feels like the equipment working; a color becomes where thoughts drain ('thoughts stream out into red'), so seeing it later replays the emptying. Responsibility moves onto the object ('the collar is doing it'), refusing means fighting an object, and the object becomes a portable on/off switch. Used afterward as a cue, it replays what happened in session.
nodes.one_liner: Declare that an object (uniform, collar, a color) is what causes their blankness or obedience, so wearing or seeing it 'does it to them'.
nodes.why_short: Blaming an object for your behavior lowers personal responsibility, and an object paired with a state becomes a reliable cue for it.
nodes.principle_note: Repeated pairing of a neutral object with a suggested state makes the object a retrieval cue that evokes the state — evaluative and classical conditioning, and the reason a post-session encounter reproduces the effect rather than merely reminding. The causal-agent framing adds an attribution move: locating the source of behavior outside the self reduces the perceived need to defend one's own agency, so resistance has no self-relevant target. The 'any compliance proves the object works' reading is itself unfalsifiable and is not part of the mechanism claim — it is a feature of how the frame is defended, not evidence for it. Falsifiable: object-cued state change should not occur in listeners never given the pairing, and compliance should drop measurably when the object is absent.

ex.f: Uniform as sealed precondition for the state
ex.t: The outfit is never described — no colour, no cut, nothing the listener could picture. It is simply named again and again as the thing that permits the state: sealed into it, she is allowed to be awake or asleep and nothing else.
ex.s: Any point once the outfit is on; the outfit is never described — no colour, no cut — only named as the thing that permits the state.
