nodes.why_short: Declaring importance or scarcity raises attention and perceived value before anything can be judged; scarcity effects are documented in persuasion research.

ex.f: importance asserted before any content exists
ex.t: Now now it's very, very, very important that you'll listen to me, my voice, my words, everything I'm about to tell you because what I'm about to say is so very, very important.

nodes.name: trojan-goal-contract
nodes.mech: The operator hands the listener an explicit goal or task — resist, don't touch yourself, use your mind to hold your arms down, "this is your last chance. Try to wake yourself up from hypnosis now" — that is privately the operator's win condition: the script is rigged so that earnest pursuit of the goal produces the loss ("how many times can you listen to this before you give in"). The listener's pride and stubbornness are the hook, and their effort is inversely yoked to the outcome: the task fatigues the very faculty performing it ("it's tiring, isn't it? To fight against your own body"), and "the more you struggle against my power, the more deeply you submit." Exhaustion is pre-explained so that giving up reads as relief rather than defeat, and both routes converge — compliance deepens directly while struggle converts into evidence of capture, consuming the resistance reservoir. The bind is entered by adopting the stated contract: a listener who shrugs off the challenge and does not care about winning it is not bound, which the material states outright.
nodes.one_liner: Dare them to resist or wake themselves up, but set it up so the effort tires them and every struggle is said to deepen surrender.
nodes.why_short: Pride makes them try; sustained effort fatigues, and pre-labeling fatigue as surrender turns their own tiredness into evidence they're giving in.

ex.f: stated challenge whose pursuit is the losing condition
ex.t: oh try to resist that's my challenge to you just listen to my words and don't touch yourself

nodes.name: choice-affordance-removal
nodes.mech: Choicelessness is staged as a property of the imagined environment rather than commanded: the elevator has "no buttons in here for you to push. You have no choices to make," or the held middle state is framed as aversive dissonance ("a place you'd rather not be") with "down" pre-loaded as the only named relief. Agency-suspension is experienced as ambient fact — the scene is a vector field with one attractor — so obedience or descent becomes the only remaining gravity and no obedience demand ever has to be issued at the moment of capture. Alternative exits are either absent from the scene's construction or named only as theoretical preference, never offered as structural relief from the middle. The staging can escalate to full dissolution of the scaffolding itself — "everything solid falls out from under you" — leaving the listener held aloft by nothing but "your desire to heed my call," pure dependence presented as the scene's physics.
nodes.one_liner: Build the imagined scene with only one way out (an elevator with no buttons, a middle state that feels bad with 'down' as the only relief).
nodes.why_short: When the imagined setting offers no alternatives, there's nothing to decide, and going down feels like a fact of the scene rather than an order.

ex.f: choicelessness built into the imagined environment
ex.t: There are no buttons in here for you to push. You have no choices to make. Only by your obedience. Will you get where you're going.

nodes.name: contradiction-identity-trap
nodes.mech: Make contradictory claims about who the listener is and leave them unresolved: you are a man, you are not a man, you are only a sissy. Trying to sort it out is uncomfortable, and the one claim that keeps getting repeated is offered as the only place to land. It works on a listener who follows closely and tries to make sense of it; noticing the contradiction is the trap. Variations: redefining the way out as the way in ('taking responsibility means giving it up'); adding the opposite line beside an earlier one without taking it back, after first saying both can be true.
nodes.one_liner: State contradictory identity claims and leave them unresolved (you are a man, you're not a man, you're a sissy) so every way of resolving it lands on the target.
nodes.why_short: Unresolved contradiction is uncomfortable; offering one repeated statement as the only resolution may make it the one that sticks. Untested.

ex.f: identity defined so both horns of the contradiction land on the target label
ex.t: a man forced to wear woman's clothing. A Man forced to dress like a woman, even though he is still a man. But that's not what you are. You are a sissy and that is all that you are

nodes.name: unsatisfiable-exit-gate
nodes.mech: The listener is told they may wake, but only once they have accepted, obeyed and forgotten everything. The catch is the forgetting: you cannot check that you have forgotten something without remembering it, so the condition can never be confirmed from the inside. Trying to check only keeps them under longer, and the wake decision is handed to a 'subconscious' they cannot watch. Because it is worded as a permission ('you will only be able to wake once…') rather than a ban, the lock is easy to miss.
nodes.one_liner: Tell them they can only wake once they're sure they've accepted, obeyed and forgotten everything — a condition they can't check.
nodes.why_short: You can't confirm you've forgotten something without remembering it, so the condition can never be confirmed. Trying to check just keeps them under longer. Phrasing it as a permission hides that it is actually a lock.

ex.f: wake permission gated on a forgetting the listener cannot audit
ex.t: You will only be able to wake once you are completely convinced that you have accepted, obeyed and forgotten all of your conditioning absolutely fully and completely.

nodes.name: desire-priced-in-depth
nodes.mech: A craving the listener already brings to the session — live arousal, hunger for fetish contact, appetite for a coveted title — is not satisfied directly; instead its route to satisfaction is redefined as the operator's goal-state, so that wanting the reward IS the descent engine. "Step one" toward the desired thing is a deepening instruction ("Well, step one, / sleep even deeper"), or access is explicitly priced in units of trance depth and enslavement (touching heels but not feet, direct contact only earned by going deeper), or a craved label like "good slave" is named, made desirable, and deferred behind unspecified performance. The price then ratchets or the gate recedes — heels, then bare feet, then contact; the title granted and revoked to keep the striving loop open — so satisfaction is always one surrender further down. This converts pre-existing motivation into deepening fuel rather than a competing distraction, and it runs without any discharge or release event ever being required: the mechanism operates even when nothing is released, because the coupling is between wanting and depth, not between compliance and payoff.
nodes.one_liner: When they already want something (contact, a title, release), make going deeper the only path to it — then keep moving the goalpost.
nodes.why_short: Their existing want does the motivating work, and depth becomes the price of getting it. Each partial reward keeps them chasing. This is the Premack principle in spirit: a wanted activity pays for a less-wanted one.

ex.f: fetish access explicitly priced in trance depth and enslavement
ex.t: the only way you can ever touch my feet, is by going deeper, by becoming even more enslaved

nodes.name: manufactured-deficit-compliance-relief
nodes.mech: A standing aversive drive-state — accumulating craving-tension, withdrawal distress, hunger, cold — is manufactured by the suggestion itself, misattributed to abstinence or to the world, and given exactly one permitted exit: the target behavior or the operator. The distress is scripted to escalate while unrelieved ("this tension can build and build getting stronger and stronger"), the solution space is narrowed until only one relief exists ("the only thing that can satisfy it is your cum"; warmth defined as the operator), and the causal attribution is inverted so resisting reads as the cause of the suffering rather than the suggestion that installed it. Compliance thereby shifts from rewarded to negatively reinforced — escape from a distress the script created — which is stickier than reward and runs outside the session on its own schedule with no operator input. The behavior-analytic grounding is the establishing operation: onset of an aversive state increases the effectiveness of its own reduction as a reinforcer and evokes whatever behavior has historically ended it, and the operator manufactures compliance by creating a discomfort whose relief the operator controls.
nodes.one_liner: Suggest a craving that builds and builds, say only one act (or you) can relieve it, and blame the ache on resisting.
nodes.why_short: Relief from discomfort is a strong reinforcer, so the permitted act gets rewarded each time. Blaming resistance makes holding out feel like the cause of the pain, so they stop resisting.

nodes.name: engineered-aversive-relief-binding
nodes.mech: The operator deliberately creates a passing discomfort (a threat in the story, eye strain from keeping the eyes open, pain given then explained medically) and ends it at a chosen moment with their own cue: 'relax' ending a tension they created, the first eye-close arriving on a count, pain turned into a rush of pleasure credited to the operator. Because relief comes through the cue, the good feeling attaches to the operator. Each step is genuinely felt, so it is hard to block without denying one's own experience. Repeated cycles let the cue alone bring the drop. With pain, it runs through gratitude: pleasure brings thanks, and thanks brings obedience.
nodes.one_liner: Deliberately build discomfort (eye strain, worry, tension), then end it exactly on your cue word, count or touch.
nodes.why_short: Relief that ends discomfort is rewarding, and whatever reliably comes with the relief picks up that good feeling. The cue becomes associated with letting go.

ex.f: engineered eye-strain cycle named as relief-conditioning
ex.t: selective reward for obedience with an association of pleasure in the short relief

nodes.name: concurrent-pleasure-reattribution
nodes.mech: A sensation or act already underway — masturbation arousal, the click that navigates the session, minutes of relaxation instructions already being followed — is re-credited to obedience or to the operator's voice: "that rush you feel... comes with following my commands," "Clicking is intense sexual pleasure," "how good it feels to follow My compelling commands." Because the substrate is real and simultaneous, the causal claim feels empirically confirmed from inside the listener's own body; correlation is laundered into causation, and physical sensation becomes evidence of good submission. The move creates nothing and is explicitly parasitic — the sources' required conditions state the listener must actually be touching or clicking, since "the labelling has nothing to land on otherwise." In the mildest form no concrete act even exists yet: the listener is invited to locate an ambiguous pleasant sensation and read it as "the rush of obeying," pre-rewarding a response class before any command is issued. Once installed, the link can be leveraged or severed at will — "when you leave subspace, you do not touch anymore. Or you stop feeling so good" — making the pleasure conditional property of the frame rather than of the body that produced it.
nodes.one_liner: Point at something they're already feeling (arousal, relaxation) and tell them that feeling comes from obeying you.
nodes.why_short: People often misjudge where a feeling comes from and accept a plausible label. Because the feeling is real and happening now, the claim feels confirmed by their own body.

ex.f: live masturbation pleasure re-credited to obeying
ex.t: deep down you know the pleasure is obedience and obedience is pleasure that's right you feel it you feel the pleasure of obeying me you feel it as you touch yourself at my command

nodes.name: obedience-pleasure-state-equation
nodes.mech: Instead of pairing obedience with some reward, the operator simply states, over and over, that obedience is pleasure: 'obedience is happiness, obedience is joy, and you love to obey.' It is said as a fact about the listener, usually once they are deep enough not to question it. The feeling is then expected to arrive whenever they obey, and refusing costs them both the pleasure and their sense of who they are. Variations: a sliding scale ('the more I speak, the better it feels'); resisting described in advance as feeling horrible; tying obedience to identity ('good girls obey'); forgetting why it feels good while keeping the feeling.
nodes.one_liner: Repeat flat statements that obedience simply is pleasure, as a fact about them, over and over.
nodes.why_short: Statements heard many times start to feel true, especially when the listener is relaxed and not questioning. The claim is never tested, just repeated.

ex.f: the equation stated as bare axiom at depth
ex.t: obedience is happiness obedience is joy obedience is pleasure and you love to obey

nodes.name: cognitive-loss-pleasure-relabel
nodes.mech: Every cognitive loss suggested (forgetting, emptiness, missing thoughts, fears, will, memories) is paired in the same breath with reward language: 'Forgetting feels wonderful', 'Feeling so empty. Feels wonderful', or a repeated run of 'the pleasure that comes from having no...' across several faculties. Dense repetition while the listener feels good makes the pairing stick until it holds on its own. Its job is protective rather than motivating: noticing something is missing would normally cause alarm and break the trance, and this turns that alarm into pleasure, closing off the most common way people come out on their own. It works underneath the main forgetting or emptying suggestions so they can run without interruption, rather than doing anything by itself. The repeated rhythm also deepens.
nodes.one_liner: Every time you suggest forgetting or emptiness, say in the same breath how good it feels.
nodes.why_short: Noticing a missing thought would normally startle someone out of trance. Pairing each loss with pleasure words makes the gap feel pleasant rather than alarming, so they don't pull out.

ex.f: anaphoric pleasure-tagging of each removed faculty
ex.t: the pleasure that comes from having no thoughts, the pleasure that comes from having no fears, the pleasure that comes from having no will, the pleasure that comes from having no reservations, the pleasure that comes from having no memories

nodes.name: conditional-discrimination-contextual-gating
nodes.mech: A context cue is trained to decide which response another cue gets. The same word or signal earns one reaction in one setting and a different reaction in another, and only the context tells the subject which is wanted. To make the context actually matter, the items and their positions are shuffled between trials while the context signal stays the same, so the subject cannot get it right by habit or by the item alone. What gets learned is a rule ('pick the one that matches', 'in this room, X means Y') rather than a fixed answer, and it can be switched just by changing the context.
nodes.one_liner: Train a context cue that decides which response a trigger gets: same word, different reaction depending on the setting.
nodes.why_short: Lab animals and people reliably learn 'if this context, then this answer' rules, so one cue can mean different things depending on what else is present.

ex.f: conditional cue reassigns which stimulus is discriminative
ex.t: The color of the child's shirt is the conditional stimulus that makes the same-colored circle the discriminative stimulus.

nodes.name: convergent-multiple-control
nodes.mech: Two cues that already work on their own are combined so that together they pull out one specific response neither would produce alone. Nothing new is trained: both cues must already work independently, and the combination simply makes the target more specific. Variations: a spoken question that selects among answers an ambiguous prompt could draw ('What shape?' versus 'What colour?' of the same card); extra related talk that lifts a weak cue or half-forgotten memory over the threshold; holding a word in mind and repeating it until a matching word appears, which produces a 'that's it' recognition.
nodes.one_liner: Stack two cues that each point toward the same response so together they pull out a reaction neither gets alone.
nodes.why_short: Most behavior is influenced by several cues at once; adding a second matching cue makes a weak or ambiguous prompt strong enough to work.

ex.f: stacked cue funnels one of several latent answers
ex.t: Saying 'rectangle' is multiply controlled by the actual (nonverbal) shape of the paper and by the (verbal) spoken word 'shape.'

nodes.name: omission-reinforcement-dro
nodes.mech: The subject is rewarded when a set stretch of time passes without the unwanted behaviour. They are paid for not doing it. Because the reward lands at the end of the window, anything else they did in that window gets rewarded too, so the rule is usually 'no target behaviour and nothing else unwanted.' Variations: the whole window must be clean; only the moment the window ends is checked (cheap, good for keeping gains); windows of random length so they cannot time the behaviour to safe moments; windows measured by distance travelled instead of time.
nodes.one_liner: Reward them when a set stretch of time passes without the unwanted behavior happening.
nodes.why_short: Rewarding a stretch without the behavior makes not doing it the thing that gets reinforced. Unpredictable check times stop them from timing slips to safe moments.

ex.f: leak-guard: pay only when the whole undesirable set is absent
ex.t: contingent on the absence of the problem behavior and the absence of any other significant inappropriate behaviors.

nodes.name: differential-reinforcement-low-rate
nodes.mech: License the behavior in moderation: reinforcement is delivered for the behavior's occurrence, but only when the count stays at or under a predetermined criterion — full-session (at most N per session), per-interval (exceeding the criterion cancels the opportunity and starts a new interval), or spaced-responding on inter-response times. The behavior is throttled to a tolerable band, never banned, which suits acts that are desirable in small doses (asking for help, hand-raising). The ceiling can be reified as a tangible depleting resource: a card with one box per allowed response initialed as each is spent, or a pack of coupons whose unspent remainder converts to bonus tokens with real purchasing power — and the payout is deliberately capped (one point no matter how many boxes remain) so the subject uses the allowance rather than maximizing abstention. Variants are chosen by feedback immediacy: spaced-responding gives the most accurate feedback because every response that violates the inter-response-time criterion instantly withholds reinforcement and resets the interval, a per-response consequence that lets the subject self-monitor and hold the rate down.
nodes.one_liner: Allow a behavior only up to a fixed number of times, and reward staying under the limit — e.g. a card of permitted requests.
nodes.why_short: Rewarding a low rate rather than zero keeps an acceptable behavior alive while cutting how often it happens. A visible allowance makes the limit concrete.

ex.f: ration with a visible meter, spending the quota stays legitimate
ex.t: No additional points were awarded if more than one box was left empty, because we wanted the children to use the opportunities.

nodes.name: replace-the-payoff
nodes.mech: Work out exactly what an unwanted behaviour gets the person (attention, escape, a treat), stop it getting that, and give the same payoff for a different behaviour you prefer, such as handing over a 'break' card instead of throwing a tantrum. The want is kept and redirected, not starved. Variations: choose a replacement that physically cannot be done at the same time as the old behaviour; avoid 'punishments' that actually deliver the payoff, such as time-out for someone trying to escape, or a telling-off for someone seeking attention.
nodes.one_liner: Find what an unwanted behaviour gets them, stop it working, and give that same reward for a behaviour you prefer.
nodes.why_short: Function-based treatment with a replacement behaviour is well supported in applied behaviour analysis.
steps: Find exactly what payoff the unwanted behaviour earns.
Stop the old behaviour from earning it.
Give the same payoff for a replacement behaviour.

ex.f: functionally-equivalent replacement channel for the same reinforcer
ex.t: The operator identifies the reinforcer maintaining the problem behavior (via functional assessment), then teaches an adaptive communicative response (sign, vocalization, device, card) that produces that *same* reinforcer.

nodes.name: graded-concurrent-choice-architecture
nodes.mech: Every option stays simultaneously live — including the problem behavior — and the operator instead rigs the relative terms of the concurrent contingencies so response allocation drifts on its own. The alternative is made to pay richer, faster, and more reliably ('maximizing the difference between rates of reinforcement obtained by the two response classes'), or engineered to cost less response effort than the target, or laid out as a signaled graded menu: completing the task earns a long high-quality break with preferred toys, appropriately asking earns a short low-quality break, and eloping still 'works' but yields a minimal degraded outcome — ten seconds, no toys, neutral blocking — each option tagged by color. Nothing is prohibited or withheld; the matching law does the suppression, since the subject allocates responding in proportion to obtained reinforcement and experiences only that the good option works better. This is the design of choice precisely when the maintaining reinforcer cannot be safely withheld, so unsafe extinction is avoided while demand requirements for the best-paying option are ramped up over time.
nodes.one_liner: Leave every option open but make the preferred one pay better, faster or easier than the others.
nodes.why_short: People and animals split their effort across options in proportion to how well each pays, so tilting the payoffs shifts behavior without any ban.

ex.f: concurrent-schedule payoff tilting with all options left live
ex.t: the client allocates more responding to the alternative behavior and less responding to the problem behavior, as described by the matching law

nodes.name: chain-interruption-evocation
nodes.mech: Let the subject start a routine they can do and want to finish, then block one step partway through: the scissors are missing, the jacket zip won't go. Being stuck just short of the payoff makes the missing piece suddenly valuable. The block is lifted only when they produce the new behaviour being taught, usually asking for it, so the new behaviour rides on the momentum of the routine. To confirm it is the wanting doing the work, some runs supply the missing item in advance and the request disappears. The interruption needs to be mildly frustrating: too little gives no motivation, too much becomes real distress.
nodes.one_liner: Let them start a routine they want to finish, block one step midway, and release it only when they do or ask for the new thing.
nodes.why_short: Being stopped short of a goal makes the missing piece suddenly wanted, so the new response gets learned on that borrowed motivation without any extra reward.

ex.f: interrupted link established as a reinforcer, release gated on the new response
ex.t: By interrupting the chains at the point at which these additional objects (or actions) are needed, practitioners can momentarily establish them as reinforcers and contrive opportunities to teach a wider variety of mands

nodes.name: conditioned-motivation-by-pairing
nodes.mech: A neutral cue is presented again and again while the subject genuinely wants something, for example hunger, arousal or tiredness. Over time the cue picks up the wanting itself, so later it brings back the desire and the urge to act on it even when the original need is absent, the way seeing a restaurant after a meal can still make you want to order. Variations: the aversive version, where an instruction that has repeatedly come before hard tasks becomes something the subject wants to escape, so hearing it triggers avoidance.
nodes.one_liner: Present a neutral cue repeatedly while they genuinely want something; later the cue alone brings the wanting back.
nodes.why_short: Cues present during real craving become able to trigger craving themselves, which is well documented in addiction and appetite research.

nodes.name: function-based-extinction
nodes.mech: Identify the maintaining reinforcer via functional assessment, then arrange that the behavior no longer produces it, so the response rate declines toward its pre-reinforcement baseline. The functional read replaces the lay move of just ignoring it — the payoff may not be attention at all, and mis-targeted ignoring is the named anti-pattern. The withholding must cover every maintaining source at once, since withholding one source of reinforcement while another stays live may have minimal or no effect. Realization then follows the identified channel: for escape-maintained behavior, block the exit so the behavior cannot purchase escape — physically guiding the subject through the demand or re-presenting refused food until the aversive situation no longer terminates contingent on the response; for attention- or conflict-maintained behavior, deny the payoff by flat restatement of the contingency and disengagement, including reading resistance talk as escape behavior whose complaints are ignored while reinforcement is delivered contingent only on actual task performance. The lever throughout is removal of the maintaining contingency, not delivery of any aversive event.
nodes.one_liner: Work out what a behavior gets them, then make sure it never gets that again.
nodes.why_short: Behavior that stops paying off fades. Guessing the payoff wrong, such as ignoring when the real payoff is escape, does nothing, so the diagnosis matters.

ex.f: escape payoff cut after functional identification
ex.t: Flo's tantrums can be placed on extinction by ensuring that the reinforcer (e.g., avoidance of the activities ...) no longer follows problem behavior (tantrums).

nodes.name: sensory-extinction
nodes.mech: For behavior maintained by its own sensory product there is no delivered reinforcer to withhold — instead the operator physically alters the environment or body so the self-produced sensation no longer occurs: goggles over eye-poking, mittens over hair-twirling, lima beans fouling the taste of vomit, disconnecting the switch, carpeting the spinning surface. The behavior still emits but stops producing its payoff — the response-consequence contingency is broken at the sensory channel, and the behavior decays toward its pre-reinforcement rate. This is explicitly distinct from response blocking: the subject remains free to perform the act; it simply yields no sensation. It requires that the maintaining reinforcer be automatic and sensory rather than socially mediated, and that the specific channel be physically maskable while still permitting the response. Because the apparatus is intrusive, it is not simply left on: the glove is gradually cut away so the masking fades out rather than being removed all at once.
nodes.one_liner: When a habit is done for its own feel, change the body or setting so doing it no longer produces that sensation.
nodes.why_short: Self-soothing habits are kept alive by the sensation they make; remove the sensation and the habit fades even though it's still allowed.

ex.f: behavior left free while its sensory payoff is masked
ex.t: the persons can emit the problem behavior, but that behavior will not produce reinforcement

nodes.name: extinction-procedure-fidelity
nodes.mech: The conduct doctrine that lets a withholding program survive its own side effects. Anticipate the predictable cascade — extinction burst, response variation, increased magnitude, spontaneous recovery, resurgence, emotional and aggressive outbursts — and hold the contingency steady through it, because relenting mid-burst reinforces a now-intensified response and it is critical that extinction-produced aggression not produce reinforcement, or a worse behavior is trained to do the old job. When full withholding is unbearable for the operator, titrate tolerance stepwise: baseline the comfortable ignoring duration, then wait an additional five minutes every two days until the target is reached. Re-apply after any relapse rather than treating it as failure — decreases become increasingly rapid with each successive application, and the effect is additive when the subject can discriminate the onset of extinction; where tolerable, contrive extra evoking situations so trials accumulate faster. Maintenance then splits by intrusiveness: leave the extinction procedure in effect permanently, or fade an intrusive apparatus in small increments; and guard adjacent schedules by withholding any free, noncontingent delivery for roughly ten seconds past a just-emitted problem behavior so the reinforcer never lands on it.
nodes.one_liner: When you stop rewarding a behavior, expect a flare-up first, and hold steady through it.
nodes.why_short: Behaviors that stop paying off briefly get louder before fading. Giving in during the flare-up rewards the louder version and makes things worse.

ex.f: hold the line through the burst
ex.t: Applied behavior analysts need to anticipate extinction bursts and be prepared to consistently withhold the reinforcing consequence.

nodes.name: chain-link-severing
nodes.mech: Many habits are chains of steps, each step leading to the next and the whole thing paid for by the final payoff. Take that payoff away and the earlier steps weaken too, so the chain falls apart from the end backwards. Variations: withhold the final payoff; give the payoff freely beforehand so it is no longer wanted; cut a single link by rewarding a later step every time it happens, inside or outside the chain, so the earlier step stops leading anywhere and fades while the later step stays intact.
nodes.one_liner: To end a multi-step habit, remove the final payoff, or satisfy it beforehand, and the earlier steps fall away too.
nodes.why_short: In a chain, each step is kept going by leading to the next and finally to the reward. Remove the end reward and the steps before it lose their pull.

ex.f: backward propagation of terminal-link extinction
ex.t: Because each chain link's stimulus is both conditioned reinforcer for the prior response and SD for the next, removing the terminal payoff strips the upstream stimuli of their reinforcing function, so earlier responses decline too.

nodes.name: self-administered-contingency
nodes.mech: The contingency-administrator role is relocated into the subject: the subject emits a separate controlling response that manipulates a variable of the behavior to be changed, so one of the person's own behaviors alters the probability of another. The warrant is coverage — the self is the one change agent guaranteed present in every setting and at every time, including private events no external agent can reach, so installing the person as their own prompter, monitor, and reinforcer extends the contingency where no one else can follow. Partial handovers give the subject selected roles: self-selected performance criteria and rewards, which can outperform agent-set standards but carry a documented drift toward too-lenient criteria, and self-scoring against an answer key with self-delivered reward or error correction so responses no longer wait on a busy external agent. The full form is the self-contract, which collapses all four roles — task selection, reward selection, self-monitoring of completion, and self-delivery of the reward — into one person. Across every realization the integrity of the arrangement rests on unenforced honest self-delivery: reinforcement depends on the subject withholding the reward until the criterion is genuinely met.
nodes.one_liner: Have them run the rules on themselves: set their own targets, track themselves and reward or deny themselves.
nodes.why_short: They are the only person present in every setting, so self-run rules reach places an outside trainer can't. Self-management programs work, though people tend to go easy on themselves.

ex.f: two-response split: subject as own contingency administrator
ex.t: One response, the controlling response, affects variables in such a way as to change the probability of the other, the controlled response.

nodes.name: self-monitoring-reactivity
nodes.mech: The act of observing and recording one's own behavior is itself the intervention: recording begins the moment the target is defined, before any other tactic, and the desired improvement may be achieved by self-monitoring alone — no programmed consequence is added; the measurement is the lever. It works by forcing an immediate, salient event onto a response otherwise governed only by remote outcomes: eating normally produces only delayed bodily consequences, but tallying and charting each instance triggers an immediate observable mark the person cannot make without confronting the behavior at the moment it occurs. Temporal contiguity is load-bearing — the recording must be contemporaneous with the target behavior, and a deferred end-of-day reconstruction loses the effect. The same logging simultaneously yields baseline data exposing antecedent-behavior-consequence patterns, and the documented range runs from increasing on-task behavior to decreasing smoking, stereotypy, and tics.
nodes.one_liner: Have them log every instance of a behavior the moment it happens — no reward or penalty needed.
nodes.why_short: Recording forces them to notice each instance as it happens, and that awareness alone usually shifts the behavior. Logging works best done on the spot.

ex.f: measurement alone as the intervention
ex.t: the desired improvement in behavior may be achieved by self-monitoring alone.

nodes.name: baseline-keyed-criterion-calibration
nodes.mech: When setting a target for a behaviour the subject already does, base the first goal on their own measured average so the first round can be won: for example, a gap between occurrences equal to or a little shorter than their usual gap, or an allowed count at or slightly below their normal rate. Then tighten the target in small steps, only after they have succeeded. If they fail, go back to the last level that worked and move forward more slowly. Reward low rates, not perfection, so one slip does not end the game. Variations: a rolling target that only rewards responses better than most of their recent ones.
nodes.one_liner: Set the first target from their own measured average so they can win it, then tighten gradually.
nodes.why_short: Early success keeps them in the game; a bar set too high means no reward and they quit. Moving the bar with their actual progress is how shaping succeeds.

ex.f: baseline-derived opening criterion
ex.t: use the mean number of responses emitted during baseline sessions, or slightly lower than that average, as the initial full-session DRL criterion.

nodes.name: borrowed-precedent-legitimacy
nodes.mech: The operator elicits or narrates a real autobiographical experience in which the target state already occurred with full social sanction — remembered surgical anesthesia — and frames the present suggestion as a re-activation of that known pattern rather than a novelty. Belief becomes cheap because the precedent is verified memory: the placebo is billed as 'a capsule which follows the exact nerve pattern of the previous anesthesia' so the subject will be 'anesthetized in every area where you were anesthetized before,' and the remembered IV drip already proved that surrender to a substance and to strangers was normal, sanctioned, and even pleasant ('it felt right at the time. This feels so similar to that'). The precondition is that the subject has, or can vividly claim, the prior experience — the operator elicits it first ('Have you ever been anesthetized before?'). The move can carry a covert verification gate before anything irreversible is staked on it: a graded pain test (towel clips in tender areas) so the operator proceeds only on confirmed analgesia ('If he had felt it, I wouldn't have gone ahead with the surgery').
nodes.one_liner: Have them recall a real time the state already happened (like surgical anesthesia) and frame now as a repeat of it.
nodes.why_short: Remembered experience makes the outcome feel possible and expected, and expectation shapes hypnotic and placebo responses.

ex.f: remembered surgical anesthesia lends its legitimacy to a fictional 'medicine'
ex.t: It took hold so fast as I babbled nonsense about being so easy to hypnotize... telling these total strangers all my secrets so readily, but it felt right at the time. This feels so similar to that

nodes.name: credibility-by-adjacency
nodes.mech: Place the suggestion you most care about among induction and maintenance suggestions that the person can already see working. Those working suggestions lend it an air of significance and effectiveness, so it seems as likely to work as they are and is more readily accepted. Repeat this placement until you are confident the person has taken the suggestion on board. It only works if the surrounding suggestions are visibly taking effect in this session: the credibility is built live, not borrowed from anywhere else.
nodes.one_liner: Slip the important suggestion in among suggestions that are already visibly working.
nodes.why_short: Having just experienced several suggestions work, they expect the next one to work too and are less likely to question it.

ex.f: payload seeded among already-working induction suggestions
ex.t: an aura of significance and effectiveness deriving from the already effective induction and maintenance suggestions

nodes.name: voice-as-physics-vehicle
nodes.mech: The operator's own voice is reified as a physical force or transfer substance: an 'invisible frequency manipulating your brain' whose stereo waves collide between the ears, a wave that breaks over the mind and 'surges over you and submerges you beneath the power of my will,' a medium whose qualities — gentleness, sensuality, femininity — pass into the listener by exposure, 'reflecting itself into your helpless hypnotized mind.' Because sound literally is waves and vibration, the frame is non-falsifiable, and resistance becomes a category error — the signals travel 'through your nervous system that you cannot control, that you cannot anticipate, that you cannot fight.' Compliance is thereby reframed as passive tuning rather than active choice: the change arrives from outside through the audio channel, the listener is merely the receiving surface, and any spontaneous physiology (goosebumps, trembling) is pre-attributed to the frequency as evidence the mechanism works.
nodes.one_liner: Describe your voice as a physical wave or frequency that flows into their brain and nervous system.
nodes.why_short: Sound really is vibration, so the image feels hard to argue with, and casting compliance as something physically received makes resisting it feel pointless.

ex.f: voice as literal frequency whose signals cannot be fought
ex.t: This invisible frequency manipulating your brain... It sends signals through your nervous system that you cannot control, that you cannot anticipate, that you cannot fight.

nodes.name: faculty-reified-as-depletable-substance
nodes.mech: An internal faculty — conscious control, resistance, the mind itself — is asserted, never hypothesized and with no simile, to be a finite physical substance subject to mechanics: a fluid draining out through openings at the feet, hands, and neck, or sand falling through an hourglass bound to a countdown. The grammar makes the depletion inevitable ('because if there's an opening, it just has to start draining'), so letting go is demoted from a volitional act that could fail to passive observation of physics already underway — the listener's only role is to notice. Continued resistance is framed so that exercising it spends the very quantity needed to keep resisting: a listener fighting the countdown still 'spends' sand. The reification itself removes volition — no external agent performs the change — and it often carries an operator-held reversibility gate that latches the emptied state ('There's no way to return your mind. / Until I flip the hourglass back upright.').
nodes.one_liner: Describe their control or resistance as a liquid draining or sand running out — fighting it uses up what's left.
nodes.why_short: Letting go becomes watching something happen rather than choosing it, so there's nothing to fail at. The 'resistance runs out' idea echoes ego depletion, which has largely failed to replicate.

ex.f: conscious control as fluid that must drain through body openings
ex.t: because if there's an opening, it just has to start draining

nodes.name: response-space-preclaiming-foreclosure
nodes.mech: The operator lists in advance every way the listener might push back, such as fighting, tuning out, doubting, stopping or holding back, and gives each one a meaning that feeds the target state: resisting breaks you, doubt becomes the trigger, stray thoughts become things to drift past. Since every reaction has already been claimed, nothing is left that counts as resistance. Opposite states get fused the same way: relaxation with arousal, choosing with compulsion, frustration with sinking, so every outlet feeds what it would normally relieve. Variations: lock one layer before opening the next, body first, then craving for depth, then arousal, then identity.
nodes.one_liner: Name in advance every way they might resist, doubt or drift, and tell them each one takes them deeper.
nodes.why_short: If every reaction has already been labelled as part of the process, they have no response left that feels like real resistance.

ex.f: sealed option-space as funnel topology
ex.t: The result is a topology with many entrances and no exit — a funnel where every wall is also a one-way door.

nodes.name: seamless-arc-checkpoint-denial
nodes.mech: The whole file is written as one unbroken rise, with no separate induction, no clear deepener sections, no dips and no wake-up. Each line carries on the rhythm or wording of the one before, and depth and arousal climb together. With no lull anywhere, the listener never gets a natural moment to surface and think, and leaving means breaking off mid-flow. A continuous physical activity can keep time underneath, so stopping also means breaking their own body's rhythm. If a break comes at all, it comes only after the take-home suggestion is in, and the ending keeps the charge rather than releasing it.
nodes.one_liner: Write the whole file as one continuous rising ramp with no breaks, deepener sections or wake-up.
nodes.why_short: Without pauses or section breaks there is no natural moment to step back and judge what is happening, so attention keeps riding the ramp.

ex.f: seamless ramp denies the judgment checkpoint
ex.t: Because there is no valley anywhere, the listener has no rest point at which to reassert judgment — the unbroken ramp is itself a control structure (no seam to resist at).

nodes.name: boundary-non-return-loop-design
nodes.mech: The file deliberately has no real exit. Either there is no wake-up at all and the last line matches the first, so the end flows straight back into the start, or the 'wake-up' keeps them in role ('wake slowly, my slave, life has just begun') with no count-up and no undoing of what was built. Lines like 'you'll keep coming back' come true by simply replaying it, and stopping takes an active choice while letting it loop takes none. Variations: across a series, each part relies on what earlier parts installed and leaves the listener ready for the next.
nodes.one_liner: End the file without a real wake-up — loop the last line to the first, or 'wake' them still in role.
nodes.why_short: With no clear ending the role never gets switched off, and each replay makes 'you keep coming back' literally true, which reads as confirmation.

ex.f: replay bootstraps the artifact's own confirming history
ex.t: "You come back again and again" becomes true on the second listen by mechanical fact. The script bootstraps its own history with each loop, so the equation chain (M3) and the retroactive history (M5) gain weight purely through replay, without any new content.

nodes.name: build-and-dismantle-scene
nodes.mech: A vivid sensory referent is deliberately furnished and given real experiential weight, then destroyed, and the resulting referent-void is filled with the operator's own repeated tokens. Immersion here is technical rather than stylistic: the goal is to remove every reference frame except the operator's voice, executed as a stepwise removal of competing referents. By the late mantra section the listener has no environment, no narrative, and no body schema being actively maintained — only the voice. Closure is achieved by attentional monopoly: once every competing frame has been deleted, nothing remains for attention to hold onto outside the operator's stream.
nodes.one_liner: Build a rich imagined scene, take it apart piece by piece until nothing is left, then fill the emptiness with your voice or credit.
nodes.why_short: The relaxed state from the scene remains when the scene is gone, so it can be relabelled as yours. Plausible, untested.
steps: Build a vivid sensory scene and let them settle in.
Take the scene apart piece by piece until nothing is left.
Rename the leftover relaxed state as your doing.
Fill the emptiness with your voice repeating a short phrase.

ex.f: stepwise deletion of competing reference frames
ex.t: Immersion here is technical: the goal is to remove every reference frame except the operator's voice. M2 (bath) provides a sensory referent, M3 destroys it, M4 fills the resulting referent-void with operator tokens.

nodes.name: evidence-apparatus-credibility
nodes.mech: The text sets the reader's trust level through its visible evidentiary and authority apparatus, before and independently of any single claim's merits. Dense per-claim citation converts persuasion claims from author's opinion into documented empirical finding, with the reader treating citation density as a proxy for truth. The notes work directly on the reading skeptic: replication is foregrounded ("done twice, with the same results"), and the accumulation of independently-cited instances functions as the argument itself — the weight of many converging sources standing in for demonstration. Dissent is staged and then settled in-house: an internal critique (Furman & Lepper) is surfaced and answered in-text, modeling a mature, self-correcting scholarly community that metabolizes objections rather than suppressing them. New principles borrow doctrinal grandeur by being routed through already-accepted ones — operant selection yoked to Darwinian natural selection and elevated as "the bedrock on which other behavioral principles rest" — so acceptance is engineered by association and authority before any specific claim is defended.
nodes.one_liner: In a persuasive book, pile up citations, replications and named experts so the reader trusts it before weighing claims.
nodes.why_short: Readers use citations and authority as a shortcut for truth instead of checking each claim themselves.

ex.f: citation density read as truth-proxy
ex.t: the reader treats citation density as a proxy for truth.

nodes.name: case-then-formalize
nodes.mech: A vivid concrete case is presented first and the formal apparatus is fitted onto it afterward, so the model reads as discovered in the phenomenon rather than imposed on it. A verbatim transcript alternates with formalizing commentary that retro-fits vocabulary onto moves performed without it — a famously articulate subject "spontaneously arrives at a technique which we have formalized," making the model look like natural law — while ordinary-case replication (the Mary Lou insertion) converts "Erickson did this with a genius" into "you can do this with a 45-year-old in a training group," carrying the generalization claim. The case narrative and the meta-model commentary are arranged so each licenses the other: the vivid phenomena supply the reader's belief that something real is happening, the apparatus then claims to explain it, and once the frame is accepted for the easy case, harder cases inherit credibility by analogy. The same ordering runs in textbook form: the chapter leads with a concrete, emotionally legible payoff, and only after the reader is impressed does the text name the properties — so every abstraction has already been cashed out in a concrete win before it is asked to be believed.
nodes.one_liner: In teaching, show a vivid real case first and only then name the technique, so the model looks discovered.
nodes.why_short: A concrete story is memorable and convincing, and labels applied afterwards borrow its credibility, as if the theory were simply describing what happened.

ex.f: demo-first ordering that licenses the apparatus
ex.t: so the model appears *discovered in* the master's behavior, not imposed.

nodes.name: unifying-frame-overlay
nodes.mech: One big idea is laid over many separate, individually real examples, and the sheer number of examples makes the idea feel proven, even though each example would stand fine without it. The pattern is: state the claim, say 'many other patterns support this,' then run through the cases. Once the reader adopts the lens, they start seeing everything through it. Variations: 'everything is an anchor,' collapsing many different things into one idea; a running scorecard that trains the reader to judge every method the author's way; claiming the same toolkit explains learning at every age.
nodes.one_liner: Lay one big idea over many unrelated real examples so the sheer number of examples makes the idea seem proven.
nodes.why_short: The examples are true by themselves, and the reader credits the idea with their weight even though the idea isn't needed to explain any one of them.

ex.f: one primitive absorbing all phenomena
ex.t: A whole-chapter rhetorical strategy that builds acceptance of every individual move by first making "everything is an anchor" feel self-evident.

nodes.name: participation-drill-pedagogy
nodes.mech: The reader or student is made to produce answers and be corrected against a fixed key, so vocabulary and screening rules install through rehearsal rather than through evaluation of the claims. One form is Socratic build-out: the author poses a step, lets participants give a plausible-but-wrong answer, then exposes why it fails — reinforced by live inductions on resisting students, so the audience watches the move land on someone who didn't intend to be a subject. Extended into a drill, roughly ten near-identical public failure-correction cycles hold difficulty constant while content varies wildly, so the discrimination generalizes across contexts — and by the third or fourth correction the reader predicts the rejection before it lands, which is the actual installation of the skill. In textbook form the same shift runs through recognition-grid multiple-choice items with section back-pointers, re-presenting every key term as a fact-to-be-matched rather than a claim-to-be-evaluated, and through novel-vignette items that test whether stimulus control of the reader's own verbal behavior has transferred beyond the taught examples. Across all of it the right answer is fixed and locatable, moving the reader's relationship to the material from evaluation to retrieval.
nodes.one_liner: Make the learner guess, correct them against a fixed answer, and repeat many times with varied examples.
nodes.why_short: Being made to answer and get corrected cements material better than reading, and the repetition trains the vocabulary rather than questioning it.

ex.f: serial public failure-correction drill
ex.t: You may not learn to build parts, but you're going to learn what a function is by the time you leave here!

nodes.name: front-matter-reader-positioning
nodes.mech: Before any content is argued, the opening/front matter positions the reader as already inside the method's success, working on the reader's state rather than on evidence. One route names the reader's desire as already-felt: a first-person testimonial frames understanding-how-people-work as "my biggest reinforcer" and closes with the rhetorical question "How could you resist that?", so the reader's assumed enthusiasm becomes the platform on which the dry material is then laid and skeptical reading is pre-empted by consensus framing. The other route presupposes competence: the text legitimizes itself by embedding the method in a prestige lineage (Watzlawick/MRI, Haley, Minuchin, Satir) so it arrives pre-validated, and presupposes the reader already knows the basic six-step model, converting "you should learn this" into "you already have the basics, here is the advanced layer." Combined with a hit-and-miss-art-to-systematic-interventions promise, the front matter manufactures both credibility and a forward-leaning yes-disposition before a single technique or definition appears.
nodes.one_liner: Open a book by assuming the reader is already keen or capable, via testimonial or famous lineage, before arguing anything.
nodes.why_short: Readers tend to live up to a flattering assumption and stop reading as skeptics. Social proof and prestige names lower critical reading.

ex.f: competence presupposed before any technique is taught
ex.t: pre-positions the reader as already-competent-but-incomplete

nodes.name: intervention-fit-doctrine (prefer shed-to-existing)
nodes.mech: Advice for practitioners: a technique only takes when it fits the person. Four checks. A new way of seeing things must be at least as believable to them as their current one. Any change must keep whatever protection the old behaviour gave ('never strip a protection without replacing it'). Order matters: get their willingness first and change things after, not the other way round. Trust their tone and body over a verbal yes, and watch for a delayed flip back as the sign something was forced. When something fails, treat it as information and change the approach.
nodes.one_liner: A technique only works if it fits the person's own view, leaves their protections in place, and comes in the right order.
nodes.why_short: Suggestions that clash with someone's experience or take away something they rely on get rejected. Checking fit and order keeps them cooperative.

ex.f: ordering as the operative fit variable
ex.t: Going after their willingness to communicate before I went after restructuring the communication was a very important syntactic choice. Doing it in the other order would have set up conflict.

nodes.name: arousal-cognition-shutdown-law
nodes.mech: Present a rule linking arousal and thinking as something already true, not as a suggestion: tell them to remember that this is just the way things are for them now, and that they are already wired this way. One form is a fixed budget of attention: you can pay attention with your mind or with your body, not both, so any rise in arousal means the mind must switch off, and whichever way the listener moves seems to confirm the rule. Another is a flat claim, repeated close together, that being aroused means being unable to think. The rule swallows its own counterexamples: testing it means thinking while aroused, which it says will fail, so even a struggle to think clearly becomes proof. Once accepted, arousal itself brings back the can't-think feeling without the operator present.
nodes.one_liner: State as a fixed fact that the more aroused they get, the harder thinking becomes.
nodes.why_short: Strong arousal does narrow attention and judgment somewhat, so the claim has a true core. Framed as an existing fact rather than a suggestion, the evidence of their own arousal seems to prove it.

ex.f: self-sealing clause: trying to think confirms the law
ex.t: Whenever you're feeling aroused, the more you try to think clearly, the harder thinking will become.

nodes.name: self-sealing-feedback-loop
nodes.mech: The operator asserts a closed causal ring between the subject's own states — depth and trust, depth and pleasure, obedience and pleasure, arousal and obedience and trance chained with reordered terms — so each term is offered as proof of the others and the ring has no entry or exit point. At least one variable is genuinely present (arousal, mild relaxation, the fact of listening), and whatever the subject actually feels is recruited as evidence the other terms are rising too; disconfirmation is impossible because questioning one clause requires rejecting every other clause simultaneously, and there is no "because" that bottoms out. The ring extends to wanting itself, looped onto being-told-to-want ("you always do what I tell you because you want to because I told you to want to"), erasing the distinction between desire and instruction so every escalation arrives pre-licensed. In the self-recited variant the subject speaks both halves of the loop about themselves in first person ("Slavery makes my cunt wet. My wet cunt makes me a slave"), closing the trap in their own voice; in the enacted variant, parsing the described cycle is itself running it ("the more you listen, the more confused you become, the more confused you become, the more you listen"). Naming the loop openly does not break it — it adds authority, and once accepted the engine runs self-driven, making continued operator speech optional.
nodes.one_liner: Say two of their states feed each other: the deeper you go, the more you trust; the more you trust, the deeper you go.
nodes.why_short: Anything they actually feel counts as evidence the loop is running, and a circular claim has no single point to disprove.

ex.f: operator names the closed ring openly and it works anyway
ex.t: The deeper you go, the more you trust me. And the more you trust me, the deeper you go. A wonderfully simple feedback loop

nodes.name: pseudo-syllogistic-necessity
nodes.mech: A directive is delivered in the surface grammar of valid inference so the listener experiences the conclusion as reasoned-to rather than imposed. The operator builds sentences of the form "X cause Y" where X is ongoing, verifiable behavior and Y the desired response — "Sitting all the way down in that chair will make you go into a deep trance" — even though there is "not, in fact, [a] necessary connection"; because the listener habitually models life in single-cause terms, resisting Y would mean denying X, so the response leaves the domain of choice. The same move runs as chained pseudo-syllogism, where "logically," "therefore," and "clearly" do the heavy lifting over invalid steps (thinking about being hypnotized gets you "at least twice as hot, and therefore twice as deeply"); as face-valid-but-empty bridging that licenses a refused behavior ("There's no actual logic to that statement, but it sounds meaningful, and will get your client to do it"); and as a physical-constraint metaphor mapped onto the will ("The train can only go in one direction... you can only go in one direction too"), so not-following feels like trying to derail a train. The terminal form forecloses deliberation entirely: obedience is "the only rational choice" and simultaneously "beyond the rational," covering analytic and intuitive resistance in one stroke. Either the listener accepts the chain and self-confirms the conclusion, or gets bogged down evaluating the surface logic — both branches advance the response.
nodes.one_liner: Phrase a command as a conclusion: 'sitting down in that chair will make you go deep', 'and therefore…'.
nodes.why_short: A 'because' or 'therefore' makes a request feel justified even when the reason is empty, so the response feels like it follows naturally rather than being ordered.
nodes.finding_name: Placebic information (Langer, Blank & Chanowitz 1978 'copy machine' study)

ex.f: Connectives ("logically... therefore... clearly") asserting an entailment that does no work
ex.t: thinking about being hypnotized, / thinking about being hypnotized, not hypnotized, logically, get you at least twice as hot, / and therefore twice as deeply, and transforming, clearly, you can feel that.

nodes.name: reality-claim-exit-closure
nodes.mech: Close off the 'it's only imagination' escape by insisting, with things they can actually feel or see, that it is real. One way is to disown a feeling that is genuinely there: the special feeling about you 'was there the whole time' and only surfaced once old thoughts fell away, so it feels self-discovered and there seems no other explanation for it. Another is to say imagined images become real through hypnosis, so real trance sensations count as proof the imagery works; each confirmation strengthens the next, and later suggestions are harder to dismiss as just a story. A third doses obvious impossibilities, such as boxes that hold ever bigger boxes, until the person stops checking them, which prepares them to accept bigger impossibilities later. All forms need an immersive experience already producing real feeling; otherwise there is nothing to point to.
nodes.one_liner: Head off 'it was only imagination' by insisting what they feel is real and was there all along.
nodes.why_short: If the experience is framed as discovered rather than suggested, they're less likely to dismiss it afterwards as just a trick or a fantasy.

nodes.name: function-first-targeting
nodes.mech: Before trying to change a behavior, ask what it does for the person rather than what it looks like. Saying "fire" while reading aloud and shouting "Fire!" at smoke look alike but are different behaviors with different payoffs. So first find out what the act reliably gets the person, or lets them escape, and aim the change there, so the method has a reason to work instead of being a guess at the symptom. Variations: measure each part of a skill and work on the weakest; spot a familiar pattern, such as "the harder you try, the worse it gets", and use the approach known to fit it.
nodes.one_liner: Before changing a behavior, find out what it gets the person or lets them escape, and aim there instead of at what it looks like.
nodes.why_short: The same visible act can be kept going by different payoffs. Fixing the wrong payoff leaves the real one in place, so the behavior comes back. Knowing the payoff tells you which change will actually bite.

ex.f: Identical surface acts sorted into different behaviors by controlling variable
ex.t: two responses of the same topography can be completely different behaviors depending on the controlling variables

nodes.name: attribution-hygiene-audit
nodes.mech: Before trusting a result, check whether something other than the subject could have produced it. Ask whose behavior actually changed: the subject's, the observer's (scoring drifts over time), or your own, through some unplanned change. Check whether the task can be passed without the skill it tests, for example from a picture or layout clue. Ask informants for plain facts, not guesses about feelings. Nothing is done to the subject; a result that fails is discarded or the test redesigned. Variations: test how well two observers agree; look for giveaway cues in the materials; word questions to get facts, not interpretations.
nodes.one_liner: Before believing a result, check whether you, an observer, or a hidden cue in the task produced it instead of the subject.
nodes.why_short: People unknowingly drift in how they score, and subjects pick up irrelevant cues (like Clever Hans reading his trainer). Checking the measuring setup rules out fake successes before you build on them.

ex.f: Accuracy exposed as an artifact of an irrelevant correlated cue
ex.t: Faulty stimulus control occurs when a behavior comes under the restricted control of an irrelevant antecedent stimulus

nodes.name: covert-leakage-read
nodes.mech: The operator tracks the subject's covert state by reading involuntary physiological leakage the subject does not know they emit, delivering no stimulus and asking nothing. One branch infers which inner experience is being generated: increased swallowing during a taste hallucination, nostril flaring during smell, breathing-rate and head-movement changes during hallucinated music — the subject 'betrays' the experience without awareness, since the cues are involuntary rather than performed. The other branch calibrates trance depth from a fixed list of involuntary signs — body warmth, eyelid flutter, increased lacrimation, reddening of the whites of the eyes, eyeballs rolling up — signs described as subtle and minute, which the subject neither controls nor performs. In both branches, verification shifts from subject self-report (unreliable, suggestible, compliance-theater-prone) to a private operator channel, so subsequent moves are timed to actual state rather than performed compliance. Because nothing is asked, the read runs continuously without lightening the trance — asking lightens it — requiring only a trained eye and a visible subject.
nodes.one_liner: Silently watch involuntary body signs - swallowing, eyelid flutter, breathing, watery eyes - to judge depth or what the subject is imagining.
nodes.why_short: Imagining tastes or relaxing deeply does change some autonomic and motor signals the subject is not controlling. Watching them gives feedback without interrupting. Specific sign-to-depth mappings are practitioner lore, not validated.

ex.f: Involuntary smell-hallucination leakage read without a probe
ex.t: betrayed this by the flaring of his nostrils

nodes.name: instrumented-covert-probe
nodes.mech: When a decision hinges on something the subject can't or won't report, stage an ordinary-looking event that is really a test, and read the reaction. Never tell them what you checked. Variations: word a suggestibility test in one sense (seeing, hearing, feeling) to learn which sense reaches them before choosing an induction; make a deliberately wrong guess so they correct you with specifics; fire decoy cues beside the real trigger, since only the real one should work; quote the trigger casually, or block one sense, and see if it still fires; check whether trance learning is recalled outside trance; recreate the original problem and watch for the old reaction.
nodes.one_liner: Set up a small disguised test - a wrong guess, a fake trigger, a decoy noise - and watch the reaction to learn something the subject can't tell you.
nodes.why_short: Behavior under a test is more reliable than self-report or the operator's hunch. A wrong guess provokes a correction that is more specific than a vague complaint; foils show whether a cue is really specific.

ex.f: Suggestibility test repurposed as a covert channel probe
ex.t: by shifting the predicates used to visual predicates and observing how well the client responds, the hypnotist can make a valid choice as to which kind of accessing... he will use.

nodes.name: antecedent-manipulation (retained core: cue/materials editing)
nodes.mech: The operator edits the occasion for a behavior of known function rather than touching the behavior or its consequences. One form swaps out the initiating discriminative stimulus entirely: where an ashtray next to a favorite chair evokes the smoking chain, replacing it with a TV remote, newspaper, or book both removes the evoking occasion and captures a competing, desirable chain under the same setting; likewise a waterless antibacterial gel substituted for running water removes the cue for compulsive rinsing. The other form removes the materials the response physically requires, during a low-urge window — discarding the cigarettes, clearing all cookies and chips from house, car, and office while not craving them — so the response is harder or impossible to emit at the moment of urge. Both are the discriminative-stimulus branch of the general antecedent rule that altering antecedents can change or eliminate either the motivating operation or the discriminative stimuli that trigger problem behavior. No consequence is ever applied and the subject is never confronted; the behavior becomes less probable because its occasion simply stops arising.
nodes.one_liner: Change the setting that kicks off a habit - swap the ashtray for a book, remove the snacks - instead of fighting the habit itself.
nodes.why_short: Habits are started by cues in the environment. Remove or replace the cue, or the materials the habit needs, and the habit has nothing to start it, so willpower in the moment isn't needed.

ex.f: Cue swap that both removes the occasion and captures a competing chain
ex.t: replacing the ash tray with a TV remote, a newspaper, or a book may occasion one or more desirable sequences of responses

nodes.name: mechanical-response-preclusion
nodes.mech: The behavior is stopped by making its motor topography physically unavailable, blind to function. Personal restraint has caregivers physically securing and holding body parts so that problem behavior cannot occur, applied pre-emptively — explicitly not to be confused with response blocking, which entails stopping a problem behavior that has been initiated. Protective equipment (oven mitts, splints, helmets) dampens or blocks the topography whether worn noncontingently throughout a session or placed on the subject only after an episode; in the mitt study both timings cut hand-mouthing sharply, which itself argues that prevention rather than punishment carries the effect. The subject can also emit the barrier themselves — sitting on hands, wrapping arms in clothing — a self-restraint posture that precludes the self-injurious behavior, is encouraged and seldom blocked by caregivers, and may be maintained by the same reinforcer as the behavior it prevents while interfering with adaptive skills. Rate drops to near-zero for exactly the duration of the barrier because the motor act is precluded; the maintaining contingency and the evoking environment are untouched, so the behavior returns when the barrier lifts.
nodes.one_liner: Physically make the act impossible - hold the limb, put on mitts or a splint - so it simply can't happen right now.
nodes.why_short: If the body can't perform the movement, it doesn't occur. Nothing is learned, though: the reason for the behavior is untouched, so it returns when the barrier comes off.

ex.f: Antecedent restraint, distinguished from blocking an initiated response
ex.t: Restraint involves physically limiting, prohibiting, or securing an individual in such a manner that the target behavior cannot occur.

nodes.name: aversive-procedure-administration-envelope
nodes.mech: Four rules keep any punishment working and limited. Keep it short: 2 to 5 minutes, never more than 15, because longer periods let the person find rewards inside it and get used to it. Apply it every time; if you cannot be consistent, use another technique, since occasional use leaves the person unsure what is acceptable. End it only after a set stretch free of the unwanted behaviour, so release never rewards that behaviour (one comparison found this added nothing over a fixed length, so the benefit is uncertain). From the start, plan to phase it out, switching to rewarding alternative behaviours once the unwanted one drops.
nodes.one_liner: If you use a punishment, keep it short, apply it every time, end it only after calm, and plan to phase it out.
nodes.why_short: Long punishments let the person find other rewards inside them and get used to them; patchy use teaches confusion; ending it during bad behavior rewards that behavior. These are standard rules from time-out research.

ex.f: duration ceiling: keep the aversive interval too short to acquire its own reinforcers
ex.t: Time-out periods should be as brief as possible while maintaining effectiveness... periods exceeding 15 minutes are not effective.

nodes.name: impoverished-context-permission
nodes.mech: The behavior is suppressed by permitting it — but only in one restricted, inconvenient, reward-stripped setting: a face-rubbing bathroom, a smoking chair turned away from TV and conversation, a sulking stool placed in the garage. Confining the behavior to that deliberately impoverished setting strips it of the incidental co-reinforcers (TV, company, comfort) that rode along with it and raises the response cost of emitting it, so rate falls without any prohibition or contingent consequence. In the smoking case, baseline 30 per day fell to 12, then 5, then quit as the chair was made progressively less accessible. The lever is antecedent stimulus control, and it is counterintuitive on purpose: permission-in-an-impoverished-context is what removes the smuggled reinforcers. It requires that the person reliably defer the behavior to the designated setting and keep that setting emptied of competing reinforcers.
nodes.one_liner: Allow the habit, but only in one dull, inconvenient spot - the smoking chair facing the wall - and let the rate drop on its own.
nodes.why_short: Much of a habit's pull comes from the comforts that ride along with it (TV, company). Confining it to a bare, awkward place strips those extras and adds effort, so it happens less without any ban.
nodes.finding_name: Stimulus control / stimulus narrowing (single-case smoking reports)

ex.f: permission confined to a deliberately impoverished setting
ex.t:
she would smoke only in a prescribed place, and she would
eliminate from that place the potentially reinforcing effects of other
activities

nodes.name: reward-taper
nodes.mech: When a behavior is held up by an artificial support, such as tokens, frequent free rewards, or a drug dose, remove that support gradually while something else takes over. First build the replacement: pair praise with every reward from the start, so praise becomes rewarding by itself. Once the behavior is stable, cut the support in small steps, stepping back up if the behavior slips. The support ends; the behavior continues on praise or expectation. Variations: ask for more work per reward; shorten the hours the reward system runs; raise the price of the best rewards; with a drug dose, suggest the effect continues as each cut is made.
nodes.one_liner: Pair your praise with every reward early on, then cut the rewards back in small steps so the praise keeps the behaviour going.
nodes.why_short: Thinning reinforcement while keeping a conditioned reinforcer is standard practice; intermittent reward also resists extinction.
steps: Pair praise with every reward from the start.
Once steady, withdraw the rewards in small steps until praise alone carries it; back off if it slips.

ex.f: day-one pairing that makes the artificial reinforcer removable
ex.t: the descriptive verbal praise that is delivered simultaneously with the token acquire the reinforcing capability of the token. From the beginning, a systematic aim of the token economy should be to withdraw the program.

nodes.name: matrix-recombinative-training
nodes.mech: Lay out the parts you want to combine as a grid, such as actions (wiggle, point) against body parts (fingers, toes), and teach only some of the combinations. Each part must already work alone. The learner then starts doing the untaught combinations, like "point toes", without being taught each one. Variation: teach several phrases built on the same frame ("the boy's hat", "the boy's shoe") so that the frame itself becomes reusable, and any new word dropped into the gap is understood.
nodes.one_liner: Teach some combinations of words or actions from a grid (wiggle fingers, point toes) and the untaught combinations start working on their own.
nodes.why_short: Once the parts are learned and a few combinations are practiced, people recombine parts into new pairs without being taught each one. This is well documented in language training for children.

ex.f: crossed matrix whose untaught cells emerge by recombination
ex.t: The operator teaches a subset of element combinations arranged in a matrix (e.g. wiggle×fingers) and relies on the crossed structure so untaught cells (wiggle toes, point finger) emerge from recombining already-known parts into a novel compound SD.

nodes.name: generative-substrate-training
nodes.mech: Instead of teaching every final performance one at a time, practise the basic building-block skills until they are quick and automatic. Once all the needed pieces are in place, complex performances that were never taught or rewarded start showing up as the pieces combine. You pay once for the foundation instead of paying for each target. Two conditions matter: every piece has to be present, because a partial set gives little, and the pieces must be fast, not merely correct. Variations: build basic listening and naming skills so new words get picked up without direct teaching; drill simple skills to speed until harder ones emerge.
nodes.one_liner: Drill the basic building-block skills until they are fast and automatic, then let complex performances appear without teaching them directly.
nodes.why_short: Fluent component skills combine more readily into new composites than skills that are merely accurate. Some precision-teaching research supports this, though the evidence is thinner than for matrix training.

ex.f: component repertoires installed, novel outputs emerge free
ex.t: once a child can emit echoic, tact, listener, and self-listener behaviors, new mands and tacts can be acquired incidentally with no formal training or reinforcement history

nodes.name: bidirectional-naming-transfer
nodes.mech: Teach a word in one direction only, for example "touch the cat" (understanding), and the other direction, saying "cat" when shown one, appears without being taught. Learning "A goes with B" can likewise produce "B goes with A". This only works once the learner already has the general skill of linking hearing a word to saying it; without that, nothing carries over. Variations: mix both directions in one session on the same object, so understanding and naming support each other; have the learner repeat the pair aloud as one phrase, which puts the reverse order in their own mouth.
nodes.one_liner: Teach a word in one direction (pick out the cat when told) and the other direction (saying 'cat' when shown) appears without training.
nodes.why_short: Once a learner has joined listening and speaking for words, learning one side of a word links to the other. Without that general skill, it doesn't transfer, which is why interleaving both directions helps.

ex.f: self-echoic chant bridges the untrained reverse direction
ex.t: AB training on a unidirectional intraverbal relation automatically produces a reverse BA intraverbal relation

nodes.name: class-wide-function-transfer
nodes.mech: Attach a feeling or reaction to one member of a group, and the whole group takes it on, including members the person has never met.
